items.sum: Report of the club's first track meeting at Tooting Common on 15 April, senior and junior matches against Victoria Park Harriers (both lost), with club handicap results.
items.s: First Track Meeting Report of the club's first track meeting at Tooting Common on 15 April, senior and junior matches against Victoria Park Harriers (both lost), with club handicap results. Our first Club track meeting at Tooting Common was held on April 15th and we had senior and junior matches versus Victoria Park Harriers. The weather was not too good and just after the start of the meeting we had a hailstorm but managed to carry on and get the meeting completed, for which we thank all those officials who braved the elements on our behalf. In the senior sprint events we were poorly represented and the visitors had a dual winner in R. D. Fergusson, who has on occasions run for the A.A.A. We won the 880 yards when Ches Walker beat L. N. Lait, with Archie Bedford in third place, but the visitors had first two in the 440 with Jim Beaumont gaining a point for us. In the 1 mile, Derrick Burfitt and Jack Brown strode round in the lead and never looked like being troubled and they ran in together. We scored major points in three of the five field events with our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, winning both the Shot and Discus, and young A. J. Sinton won the High Jump. When we totalled up the points we found that V.P.H. had scored 47 to our 43 and we congratulate them on their win. In the Junior match Jimmy Rae was second in the 100 yards, while Dave Marshall occupied the same position in the 220 yards. Alan Picton won the 440 yards, and this seems to be his best distance, but our team lost the 4 x 110 yards relay. We lost points on the two junior field events and the final score was: V.P.H. 31 points, Belgrave 17 pts. It is yet early in the season to attempt to judge our prospects for the season, but it still seems as if the lack of first-class sprinters will be our biggest headache. items.sum: Report and results of the club 20 miles walking championship on 22 April, won by Bert Clayton, with ten men inside 3 hours 15 minutes.
items.s: Club 20 Miles Walking Championship—April 22nd Report and results of the club 20 miles walking championship on 22 April, won by Bert Clayton, with ten men inside 3 hours 15 minutes. A really good field of 24 walkers faced the starter. Right from the outset, Bert Clayton forged to the front and at 1 mile had a clear lead of 100 yards from the rest of the field, which came along in two batches, the first consisting of probables and possibles, and the second batch of hopefuls and, we hope, future probables and possibles. Bert Clayton continued to walk in grand style and at 8 miles was leading by the same 100 yards from Charlie Churcher and Pat Sapcote, with Bob McMullen, walking his first 20, some 40 yards further back, followed by Messrs. Wright, Bidgood, Bentley and Oliver. It is interesting to note that Jack Rutland, who finished 4th, was at this stage 12th. At 11 miles, Clayton had increased his lead to 400 yards from Charlie, and McMullen and Pat Sapcote had dropped to 4th, with Wright and Bidgood making up ground. Oliver was now 8th and Rutland 9th, Bob Readman, seemingly taking it easy, 10th, and Tony Bellchamber, also walking his first 20 very strongly, 11th. Further back, Harry Shields, another “ first timer,” was pegging away. At 16 miles Bert Clayton appeared to be falling back slightly, or was it Jack Bidgood coming up? For at this stage, Bert was leading by about 300 yards, with Charlie 3rd, about 100 yards further back, with Mac in close attendance and Pat Sapcote coming up strongly. Jack Rutland was now 7th. At 17 miles Bert had come into his former strong style again and at this stage there was no doubt who would be the winner. His lead was now 600 yards and he was walking splendidly. Jack Bidgood looked good for a second and there were signs of a real fight for third place between Mac, Pat Sapcote and Jack Rutland. Charlie was tiring and retired. Further back, George Oliver, Tony Bellchamber and George Bentley were still walking strongly, especially Tony, who was walking like an old hand. Over the last two miles Mac tired badly and dropped right out of the picture, but we compliment him on putting up such a grand show for the greater part of his first 20. The result gave us great hopes for the coming National 20 and a headache for the Selection Committee as we had no less than ten men inside 3 hours 15 minutes over this strenuous course. items.sum: Report of the Redhill Road Relay on 29 April, won by Belgrave "A" with Archie Bedford setting a new course record on the first stage.
items.s: Redhill Road Relay Report of the Redhill Road Relay on 29 April, won by Belgrave "A" with Archie Bedford setting a new course record on the first stage. Held on April 29th over a 6 x 2½ miles course in aid of the National Playing Fields Association by the local Redhill and Reigate A.C. There was an entry of 13 teams and although we were without Len Herbert, Jack Brown and Bill Lucas, the latter being down with a touch of 'flu, we nevertheless managed to score a good win. Archie Bedford ran first for us and he set up a new course record with a time of 13 mins. 24 secs., beating the well-known P. J. Pirie of S.L.H. by one second for this. On his leg he actually led the S.L.H. runner by about 200 yards and this lead was never lost, and Jack Bragginton on the second stage increased our advantage to 52 secs. Len Bishop went next and Bowering of S.L.H. gained 26 secs. on Len but we were still leading and Stan Davies on the next leg gained a little to make the margin in our favour 42 secs. Len Adams further increased our lead and with one stage to go we were 64 secs. to the good. Ches Walker was our last runner and although Peter Pirie gained 20 secs. on him, he was never in any danger of being caught, and finished a comfortable winner. We also had a “ B ” team competing and Eric and Alan Bishop both ran well, as did A. W. Saville, while a newcomer to our teams in R. F. Bolam, did a faster time than Stan Davies. e: Six Miles in the Hour Invitation Walk
items.s: Six Miles in the Hour — Invitation Walk Report of the six-miles-in-the-hour invitation walk at Wimbledon on 29 April, following January's Talent Spotting Walk, with Belgrave members filling the first four places. So successful was the Talent Spotting Walk we organised on January 21st, when 57 competitors succeeded in beating the hour over five miles, that a good entry was ensured for the event which followed it as a natural sequence, i.e., an invitation to walk six miles over the same course in the hour. At Wimbledon on April 29th thirty-two competitors attempted this more difficult task and of the twenty-six who finished, no fewer than twenty-one succeeded. The weather was less favourable this time, but despite that and the extra distance, many of the contestants showed that they had gained considerably both in speed and stamina during the three intervening months. This was particularly noticeable in the following six instances:— Four of the above, Rolfe, Glover, Jones and Hall, are members of the Club and their vast improvement, coupled with the fact that Belgraves filled the first four places, speaks exceedingly well of the Club coaching, The race for first place was close indeed, with three men in the lead together for about 4¾ miles. Then Rolfe cut out the pace and eventually won by about 70 yards with the third man 50 yards further back. Quite the tit-bit of the race was the tussle between C. Young, Essex Beagles, and R. Linstead of Belgrave, who finished together in 13th and 14th positions. These boys are both 15½ years of age. Young, the shorter, has been taking part in walking races for some time past and has a most pleasing style. It was Linstead's first effort, but he is a good deal taller and, having been out with the junior runners, was accordingly quite fit. Barely a yard separated them from beginning to end of the six miles stretch although each was eager to leave the other behind. Considering their ages, the time they achieved, viz., 56 mins. 46 secs. was truly remarkable. Throughout the race the style of the competitors was very good for an event such as this and there were no disqualifications. items.sum: Report of the second annual "Brockman" Trophy inter-club meeting at Tooting Track on 6 May, where Belgrave placed 4th of eight clubs with Derrick Burfitt winning the 1 mile.
items.s: “Brockman” Trophy Match Report of the second annual "Brockman" Trophy inter-club meeting at Tooting Track on 6 May, where Belgrave placed 4th of eight clubs with Derrick Burfitt winning the 1 mile. The second annual meeting for the “ Brockman ” Trophy was held at Tooting Track on May 6th, and eight clubs had been invited to compete. With points scoring 6 for first place down to 1 for sixth position in each event it is obvious that you have to do well in all the events to stand any chance of winning the trophy. In the circumstances, and seeing it is yet early in the season, I think we did quite well in being placed 4th of the competing clubs. The 100 yards saw us with two competitors in the final, which was quite a good start, and Gordon Lowers finished third with R. D. Holtum sixth, and the latter is a useful addition to our sprinting ranks. In the 880 yards both Alan Bishop and Archie Bedford failed to qualify for the final of this event The 220 yards saw Alan Sexton qualifying for the final, but he was obviously short of training and did not push it unduly when finishing in fifth place. We scored our only win of the meeting in the 1 Mile with Derrick Burfitt beating Morley of Southgate in quite good time, and as the latter had beaten Derrick the previous Wednesday when running for the A.A.A. against London University, this win gave our runner the chance to turn the tables on his opponent. In the 440 yards both Cope and McKenzie failed to make an appearance and it is a pity that when chaps are sent a card that they do not reply if they cannot turn out. We had Alan Bishop and T. Underwood running for us but they failed to qualify for the final, and we could certainly do with another George Dunckley. The 3 miles was another event which found us short of runners, a sad state of affairs for a club which prides itself on our distance strength, but Bill Lucas, although still suffering from the after-effects of a touch of 'flu, ran quite well to finish in sixth place and so score a point for us. In the field events we fared rather better than usual, and in both the Long Jump and the Hop, Step and Jump we took third and fourth places, through P. Lowe and J. Mendes. A. Bergvalds, our Latvian member, scored points for us in the Weight Put and Discus Throw, but we missed the help of Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw. The meeting, although rather long drawn out, was carried through on time and provided the spectators with some good performances; two meeting records were equalled and five were broken, including the 3 miles, which V. Lillikas, the A.A.A. 6 miles champion, won in the fast time of 14 mins. 38.5 secs. Final placings of clubs resulted as under:— 1, Herne Hill H., 106; 2, Poly. items.s: “Gordon Stewart” Trophy Match Report of the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy four-club match at Drayton Green Track on 13 May, retained by Walton A.C. with Belgrave second on 28 points. Held at Drayton Green Track on May 13th, this meeting took the form of a four-sided match between the local club, Ealing Harriers, Walton A.C., Maidenhead A.C. and ourselves. In the 100 yards heats both our runners qualified for the final and in this “ Ginger ” Holtum was unlucky to be adjudged the loser in a “ blanket ” finish. George Lowers was close up in 3rd place but as Walton had the winner and the 4th man they scored 6 points to our 5 for this event. The 880 yards saw Archie Bedford and Jim Kennedy running for us but up against a strong Walton trio, which included Willie Nankeville, the A.A.A. mile champion, we had to be content with 4th place through Bedford, whereas Walton scored a “ maximum ” of 8 points for this race. In the 1 mile it was our turn to score a “ maximum ” and we actually had the first three men home, with Jack Brown leading Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker in the good time of 4 min. 31.4 secs. We only had one runner, R. A. Bartlett, qualify for the 220 final, and he eventually finished 4th, with Walton and Ealing sharing the other points. The 2 miles team race saw Bill Lucas lead the field home in 9 mins. 57 secs., and with good support from Reg Bolam (4th) and Steve Charlton (6th) we won the team race from Walton A.C. Thus with one event to be decided we were still two points behind and as in the Medley Relay, Willie Nankeville was running the 880 stage for Walton, our chances of regaining the trophy seemed slight. Such proved to be the case, as Nankeville gave his team about 25 yards lead from Walker and Underwood running the quarter with Holtum and Bartlett doing the 220's, found themselves unable to reduce the gap and so Walton retained the trophy which they won last year, with a total of 33 pts., with ourselves scoring 28, Ealing Harriers 13 and Maidenhead 3. items.sum: Report of the junior match held with the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy contest at Drayton Green Track on 13 May, ending with Ealing Harriers and Belgrave level on 20 points.
items.s: Junior Match at Ealing Report of the junior match held with the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy contest at Drayton Green Track on 13 May, ending with Ealing Harriers and Belgrave level on 20 points. Held in conjunction with the “ Gordon Stewart ” Trophy contest, on May 13th, at Drayton Green Track, this match found the junior sides of the four trophy clubs in opposition. D. Clements qualified for the 100 yds. final, but in this he could only finish 4th, but Alan Law managed to gain 2nd place in the 220 final, and the big disappointment here, was the disqualification of Frank Kemp in his heat because of two false starts, a lesson to be borne in mind for the future. In the 1 mile event we had Ray Tooby and D. Maclean having a battle royal for first place, which the former won in 4 min. 41 secs. The 880 yds. saw Brian Rice making a welcome appearance in our colours and with Harry Greene they managed to finish 3rd and 4th, although we actually had two non-scorers in Doug. Briggs and R. J. Wolton finishing in front of them. With the Medley Relay to be decided we were level on points with Walton, but although we managed to gain second place in this event, the local club, assisted by one of our members, young Dan Godfrey, gained a surprise win and this then made the total points: Ealing Harriers 20; Belgrave Harriers 20; Walton A.C. 18; Maidenhead A.C. 1. It was agreed that more than the usual two a side could compete in the longer distances, but you had to nominate your scoring men and this led to the usual upsets of form, but so long as all the lads get a run, then the final results does not matter so much. items.label: No. 109
items.h: R.W.A. National 20 Miles Championship Bellingham, May 13th
items.sum: Report of the R.W.A. National 20 miles walking championship at Bellingham on 13 May, where Belgrave were second in the team race to Woodford Green.
items.s: R.W.A. National 20 Miles Championship Bellingham, May 13th Report of the R.W.A. National 20 miles walking championship at Bellingham on 13 May, where Belgrave were second in the team race to Woodford Green. Although we were beaten into second place, our boys put up a grand show and walked splendidly throughout—but stay, before we sing our own praises, let us first congratulate a very gallant team, Woodford Green, in their triumph which they achieved after fighting hard for so many years; the splendid walking of the Sheffield boys Allen and Proctor, and finally, with greatest respect, the performance of T. Lloyd Johnson on once again getting a place in his 50th year. We feel that this was the greatest performance of all and we share with all walkers our sincere compliments to this grand athlete. At the start, Allen got away very fast with Bert Clayton close on his heels and the rest of our boys well up filling various positions from George Oliver 15 to Tony Bellchamber 60. The feature of the event was the exciting team race, the lead changing hands many times. At 5 miles Belgrave were leading Sheffield. 9 miles showed us still leading with 56 points, Surrey W.C. 61, Sheffield 72 and Woodford creeping up with 75. At 10½ miles Surrey went into the lead with 47 points to our 50 and Woodford 3rd with 62. At this stage Sheffield's 3rd and 4th men had dropped back and almost out of team hopes. Another check at 13½ miles showed us leading Woodford by 58 points to 62, but it looked as if Woodford men were piling in from everywhere and so the club whips got busy. Bert Clayton was going well in 7th position and looked like catching Woodford's first man, which he eventually did. Charlie Churcher was taking a bashing but quite enjoying it and there were hopes he might catch Goodall, Woodford's 2nd man. Pat Sapcote was determinedly chasing three Woodford men and the odds seemed that he would catch them, in fact he assured us that it was in the bag, and he certainly did it. Then came Percy Wright, walking perhaps faster than anybody, and our hopes were right back again. This state of affairs caused much blood pressure, but Woodford managed to hold on to their slender lead. Meanwhile another keen duel was in progress between our lads and Woodford for the Nijmegen Shield. At 15 miles Tony Bellchamber was our 8th man and tearing along as if he had only just started and quite bucked because he had left Woodford's 8th man behind. (Mention should here be made of an incident before the race when Syd Roberts met with a street accident just before meeting Jack Bidgood and Co. at Chelsea. George Bentley stayed behind to accompany Syd to hospital, but the incident undoubtedly upset Jack and completely put him off his form. We are pleased to report that Syd is now fully recovered and would like to thank all those who kept his wife busy at the phone enquiring as to his welfare.) However, Jack fought desperately to keep in front of the 8th Woodford man, whilst Jack Rutland and Tony Bellchamber, like good team men, stayed with their vice-captain as long as they dared to keep him going. After a desperate battle, Jack reaped his reward, beating the 8th Woodford man by 20 yards to win his 6th Nijmegen medal (given by the club to members scoring in this competition), and we have good reason to believe that Jack is the only person in the country who has scored in the Nijmegen Team on six occasions. Thank you Jack for a very brave performance. Another item of interest and one which certainly deserves mention, is that all our team men, both “A” and “B” finished the very strenuous course. items.s: Surrey County Track Relays Report of the Surrey County Track Relays at Tooting Bec Track on 20 May, where Belgrave won the Youths and Junior 4 x 110 yds. relays and were third in the Senior Medley Relay. These were held at Tooting Bec Track on May 20th and we fielded teams in all except the Junior Medley Relay. In the Youths (15-17) 4 x 110 yds. our team duly won their heat in 47.4 secs., and then repeated this time when winning the final. Frank Kemp gave us a good start, which Alan Law and Don Clements kept up, so that our last runner had an easy task in coming home first. In the Senior 4 x 110 yds. we had Mike Broadbent, Gordon Lowers, Basil Walden and Jimmy Rae running for us and although we had the lead at the last change-over, Rae had to give best to Clay Gibbs, the coloured Herne Hill runner. Nevertheless our lads ran very well and with D. J. Merrett and Alan Sexton to call on we should put up a good show in the Senior Sprint Relays this season. The Junior 4 x 110 yds. Relay saw B. J. Walden, A. J. Sinton, A. M. Picton and D. E. Marshall running for us, and they all ran well to come home winners in the good time of 46.9 secs. We then came to the Senior 1 mile Medley Relay, and Ches. Walker ran the 880 yds. stage and did quite well to hand over in third place. Jim Beaumont kept up the good work by keeping this position and then Gerry Robinson and Gordon Lowers did the two 220 legs. Lowers took us up into 2nd place, but the S.L.H. man came again in the last 10 yards and Gordon was unable to hold him off, and so we finished up third. items.s: Club Meeting on May 22nd. Report of the club meeting at Tooting Track on 22 May, including a junior match won against Wallington County School and club handicap results. In this meeting, held at Tooting Track, we had a junior match against the Wallington County School, which we won by scoring 37 points to our opponents 29. In the 100 yards match Frank Kemp beat the two Wallington runners, and he was also 2nd in the 220, which was won by Dave Marshall, our junior champion. Young Dan Godfrey, many will remember his father, who was a walker in Len Fletcher's day, ran a good race in the 440 yards, but was unable to stave off the strong Wallington boy's finish in the last few yards. Ray Tooby, now 1st claim to us, won the 880 yards Junior, and Bob Wolton finished in third place. In the absence of our “ star ” junior miler, D. G. Maclean, J. E. Godfrey and Maurice Jones carried on the good work by being first and second in the 1 mile, and Jones's finishing burst had to be seen to be believed! Wallington won the 4 x 110 yards Relay in the good time of 46.5 secs., and Alan Law was 2nd in the Junior Weight, while A. J. Sinton was second in the High Jump. items.s: Police Barking to Southend Walk, May 25th. Report of the Police Barking to Southend Walk, won by vice-captain Jack Bidgood, with the Belgrave police team taking the cup to "A" Division, and placings of the club's walkers. Although this is outside the scope of Club fixtures, our police members have always figured well in this very popular event. From 1924 to 1939, a period of 16 years, the race was won eight times by Fred Rickards and four times by Fred Bentley. Now, after trying for 21 years, our vice-captain, Jack Bidgood, has added his name to the list of Belgrave successes, beating Tom Kent, the winner for the past three years, over the last mile. Congratulations Jack on this splendid achievement. We should also like to congratulate the winning team, likewise all Belgravians, on taking the cup to “A” Division for the first time since the race started in 1921. Led by Pat Sapcote (3rd), the rest of the team comprised Ted Evans (9th), George Atkinson (13th) and Hugh McGreechan (16th), one of our newest members. Incidentally, George Atkinson's father was the first individual winner in this race. Bob Readman (6th) and George Bentley (11th) gave us 7 in the first 16 out of a finishing field of 66. items.s: Match at Walton-on-Thames Report of a triangular match with Walton and Thames Valley Harriers at Stompond Lane on 27 May, where Belgrave scored 32 points, plus a 10 miles road race team second place. Held at the Stompond Lane track on May 27th, this was a Triangular match between the local club, Thames Valley Harriers, and ourselves. Once again we were rather short of numbers and only had one runner in the 2 miles, although in fairness to our distance men we had got a team in a 2 miles team race at Dartford on the same day. We were pleased to see D. J. Merrett turning out in our colours once again, and although he lost the 100 by inches to the local runner, Buchanan, he made amends by winning the 220 yards. Ches Walker ran a good race to win the 880 yards in the fast time of 2 mins. 2 secs., while Jack Brown won the 1 mile race in 4 mins. 32.3 secs. D. E. Mullen very sportingly ran a quarter for us and finished third, while in the Junior events, young Maclean was 2nd in the 1 mile, and our old friend, A. H. East, won a 2 miles walk which was included in the programme. When the points had been totalled up we found that T.V.H. had beaten Walton by the narrow margin of 1 point, 52 to 51, while we scored 32. In a 10 miles road race which started and finished on the track, our team of Steve Charlton, Tom Carter, Dick Towndrow and Roy Minahan came second in the team race which was won by the local club. It is obvious that we shall not be able to hold our own in these Inter-Club contests unless more of our best men turn out and also we must have better support in the field events. As it is usual for the first four places in each event to count even a few 4th places would help to swell our total of points, and we should like to see the away fixtures better supported. D. J. items.s: Match v. Walton A.C. and Surrey W.C. at Walton, May 27th. Short report of a triangular walking match at Walton on 27 May, where Bert East was first home but Belgrave finished third. On May 27th four of our walkers visited Walton A.C. ground for a triangular match with the home club and Surrey W.C. Owing to many other fixtures we were not very strong and although Bert East was first home, the match resulted in a win for Walton A.C., 17 pts; S.W.C., 2nd, 29 pts.; and Belgrave, 3rd, 32 pts. Winners time: 15 mins. 16 secs. Bert East Bert East first home in triangular walking match Walton Walton A.C. Surrey W.C. S.W.C.

items.sum: Round-up of Belgrave performances in the Surrey Youths, Junior and Senior championships and the Middlesex and Hants championships, including Bill Lucas winning the Surrey 3 miles.
items.s: County Championships Round-up of Belgrave performances in the Surrey Youths, Junior and Senior championships and the Middlesex and Hants championships, including Bill Lucas winning the Surrey 3 miles. In the Surrey Youths held at Tooting on May 27th we had a fair measure of success, and Frank Kemp won the 100 yards in the good time of 10.9 secs. Ian Forrester and Alan Law also ran well and the latter was fourth in the final. Alan Law also took second place in the Shot Put and B. Tillott was third in the 110 Yards Hurdles Final. Harry Greene, after doing most of the pace-making, finished 3rd in the 1 mile and it is evident that we have some very promising material in the ranks of our younger members. The Surrey Junior events were held at Motspur Park track on June 3rd and Dave Marshall did a fine double when winning the 100 and 220 yards finals. In the former race he equalled the record with a time of 10.5 secs. Mike Stearman ran a good race to finish 3rd in the 880 yards final and although D. G. Maclean and J. E. Godfrey both qualified for the 1 mile final they both found the pace a bit too hot, although “ Mac ” only dropped away over the last half-lap. In the Surrey Senior Championships we had three Club members in the 100 yards final and Basil Walden beat D. J. Merrett for 3rd place with Gordon Lowers close behind them. Basil also gained 3rd place in the 220 yards final and so managed to split the three Herne Hill runners. Ches Walker ran his best mile to date when gaining third place in the 1 mile final and he beat Jimmy Wood and also gained his Southern standard, which is of 4 mins. 28 secs. Bill Lucas, who was the holder of the Mile title, stood down from this event and ran in the 3 miles, in which the holder, Len Herbert, did not turn out. Bill ran a very fine race and although doing most of the leading he had Broughton, of Blackheath, always on his shoulder, and they gradually dropped Kerridge, of Herne Hill H. Over the final half-lap Bill came away in fine style and although his time of 14 mins. 52.2 secs. is well behind Len Herbert's record of 14.38 made last year, it was nevertheless a very sound performance. Harry Churcher won the 2 miles walk in easy fashion and D. McMullen finished second, as usual, one might say to Harry. In the Middlesex Championships, Derrick Burfitt won the 1 mile in the fast time of 4 mins. 23.4 secs., while in the Hants Championships we are pleased to see our old friend, Percy Wright, still to the fore, when winning the 2 miles walk title. items.s: Salisbury 15 Miles Road Race Report of the Whit-Monday Salisbury 15 miles road race, where Belgrave won the team race led by Les Stokell in 2nd place. On Whit-Monday our team scored a good win over Portsmouth A.C. and Thames Valley H. in the team race. Les Stokell ran well to once again finish 2nd to A. A. Robertson, the Reading International runner, and with Bert Smith and Dick Tobin coming in behind one another in 7th and 8th places, we won the team race with individuals deleted by scoring 12 pts. to Portsmouth's 20 and T.V.H. 23. Abberton and McDonald ran as individuals and finished 6th and 10th respectively and A. P. Whitehead, our other team man, finished 11th, out of about 40 starters. At the same meeting Len Adams finished 2nd in a 1 mile scratch race while Tom Carter turned out in the 3 miles but found the pace too hot for him and so retired, wise man! items.sum: Report of a match against Polytechnic Harriers and South London Harriers at the Polytechnic Stadium, Chiswick, on 31 May, where Belgrave finished third with 38 points.
items.s: Match v. Poly and S.L.H. Report of a match against Polytechnic Harriers and South London Harriers at the Polytechnic Stadium, Chiswick, on 31 May, where Belgrave finished third with 38 points. This was held at the Polytechnic Stadium, Chiswick, on May 31st, and although we had a fair turn-out we were once again not strong enough in the longer distance event. In the 100 yards we had Gordon Lowers and Basil Walden, and they both ran well to finish 2nd and 3rd in a race won in 10 seconds dead by Grieve of S.L.H. Alan Sexton, home on leave from the R.A.F., turned out in the 300 yards and although not fit, managed to finish in third place to Pugh, of S.L.H., and Pike, of the Poly, both International runners. In the 600 yards we had Bedford and Jim Beaumont and they had to be content with 4th and 5th positions. The 1,000 yards saw our real strength and here we had the first three home in Derrick Burfitt, Ches Walker and Vernon Blowfield, with Jimmy Wood, of the Poly, 4th. In the 1½ miles race we had Reg Bolam and Len Adams in 3rd and 4th positions, and we could also only finish third in the medley relay. Final points were: Poly H. 57; S.L.H. 51; Belgrave 38; and as we were not represented in the two field events we did not do too badly, but our apparent need is for some good 440 and 880 men, and also for some of our distance men, such as Len Herbert and Bill Lucas, to turn out in the longer distances. items.sum: Report of the R.W.A. 50 kilometres championship at Sheffield, where Bert Clayton finished third and Belgrave were second team to Woodford Green A.C.
items.s: R.W.A. 50 Kilos Championship—Sheffield, June 17th Report of the R.W.A. 50 kilometres championship at Sheffield, where Bert Clayton finished third and Belgrave were second team to Woodford Green A.C. A team of 9 walkers with three officials left St. Pancras Station in very good spirits and with the hopes of bringing back the 50 kilos title. Arriving at Sheffield at 12.45 p.m. they had plenty of time to relax and have a cup of tea in comfort before the race, which started at 2.30 p.m. The course was a nice hilly one with plenty of give and take. Starting with a lap of ½ mile, they went out and home over the same road in one direction for 5 miles and then out and back the other way with plenty of the Sheffield locals out on the roads. The start was a fairly fast one with Proctor, Lloyd Johnson, Martineau and Clayton well up in the lead. Proctor soon went away taking advantage of the home ground and knowing the course well. In a batch at about 5 miles were Jack Bidgood, Charlie Churcher and Fred Redman, all walking very strong. At 18 miles Charlie started to drop back and Jack Rutland came up. Jack walked a very fine and well judged race. At 22 miles Bert Clayton started to take a bashing, but with the help of Joe Coleman he picked up really well and there was no holding him. He walked in really grand to finish third and we should all congratulate him on his fine performance. Jack Bidgood was passing men and apparently had no sympathy for them. Back in the field, Don Heath, who had been walking quite well, had to retire at 27 miles. Jack Baker and Pat Sapcote also had leg trouble and they too retired. It was good to see Harry Shields coming along with a determined look on his face, subsequently finishing 44th, in his first long distance walk, over 20 miles. Harry started this walking game only in December of last year and has done practically every distance since then. Frank Jarvis, making a comeback, also walked well and finished. Our sincere thanks are due to both Joe and Len Coleman who, with cycles and plenty of back chat, got the boys second place in the Team Race. Also to Bob Dimmock, who was able to get round the course, thanks to Gerry Swan, and keep an eye on them. It is interesting to note, that as a result of this race, our Road Captain, Charlie Churcher, is the only club member to score in the team in all the three Senior National events, viz., 10 miles, 20 miles and 50 kilos. items.sum: Profile of H. E. "Bert" Footer, who joined in 1922, ran cross-country for England and won Southern, South of Thames and Surrey titles, and is now a club coach.
items.s: Did you know that— Profile of H. E. "Bert" Footer, who joined in 1922, ran cross-country for England and won Southern, South of Thames and Surrey titles, and is now a club coach. H. E. Footer (otherwise known as Our Bert) joined the Club in 1922 and is therefore one of the oldest in membership still in our active ranks. Although lacking in inches Bert makes up for this by possessing plenty of “ guts,” a good club spirit, and tons of determination, which are essential factors if you wish to rise to the top in the cross-country world. Bert gained International honours by representing England over the country in 1933 and 1934, and in both these races he finished in 4th position and so worthily upheld the prestige of the Belgrave Harriers. He was a member of our winning team in the South of Thames “ Junior ” race in 1925 when our placings were: H. E. Footer 2; A. D. Pyer 6; H. W. Bruce 7; K. B. O'Kell 9. The 1933 Southern Counties Senior C.C. race was won by H. E. Footer, while he also won the South of Thames Championship in 1930, and he won the Surrey County Senior individual title in 1930, 1935 and 1937. Bert was also a member of our winning team in the Southern Counties Senior race in 1934 and of our winning “ National ” teams in 1935 and 1939. He has represented Surrey County on numerous occasions and was once a power in Territorial running as a member of the London Irish. During the War he served in the Royal Marine Commandos and the sight of a Footer with his blood up is enough to scare even the most formidable opposition. Bert has also won both the “ Blackstaffe ” Shield and the “ Macher ” Shield and at one time his stock of medals was one of the eighth wonders of the world. He also used to run the crucial 9th stage in the London to Brighton Relay and was a member of our winning teams in 1934, 1935 and 1936. He has run for the Club in every conceivable kind of race and also did quite well over the Marathon course, being the present holder of the Club Championship at that distance. Bert was cross-country captain for many years and led the Club to their first “ National ” success. He is now one of our coaches and we strongly advise all those under his tuition to mark well his advice which he is always ready to give. H. E. Footer H. E. items.s: Entries for Club Events Committee notice that entries for club events must reach sectional secretaries at least a week beforehand. The Committee view with grave concern the haphazard manner of entering for Club events. Notice is hereby given that entries must now be sent to Sectional Secretaries at least one week before the event, preferably with entrance fee. We ask you to consider this right and proper decision reasonably and to co-operate by readily complying. There are many good reasons for this decision, ask your handicapper for one! We are sure he will give you a good one and Bill will be “ True ” in his veracity on this subject. Make a point of studying your fixture card, it is given to you for YOUR information and remember—you have been warned.

items.h: Officials for Club Events—Calling for Volunteers
items.sum: Appeal for members to volunteer as track and field officials for club meetings, with training offered.
items.s: Officials for Club Events—Calling for Volunteers Appeal for members to volunteer as track and field officials for club meetings, with training offered. It is our intention to set up a panel of Track and Field Officials, with proper Club status, for our own Club meetings, but this can only be done with your assistance. Members are required as Track Judges, Field Judges (high jump, long jump, discus, hammer, etc.) and marksmen. The work is very interesting and affords an excellent opportunity of maintaining an active interest in the Club apart from a competitive one. If you have any experience or qualifications, all the better, but if not, we shall be pleased to give you the proper training under the guidance of our existing officials both on training nights and at our regular meetings. In due time you may be given the opportunity to pass the A.A.A. examinations and thus become fully qualified judges. If you would like to take an interest in this side of Club work, send your name in to the Secretary of your Section and he will pass it on to the General Committee. We earnestly ask for your co-operation in this matter and repeat once again—ANY VOLUNTEERS.

items.sum: Club news notes on members' recent successes in walking and running, letters from members serving abroad, and family news.
items.s: News in Brief Club news notes on members' recent successes in walking and running, letters from members serving abroad, and family news. G. Warr won the London Universities 1 mile track walk in record time. D. J. Merrett has been selected to run for the A.A.A. and also won the 100 yards for London Universities in their match against an A.A.A. team recently. Tony Bellchamber finished 2nd in the Inter-Banks 7 Miles Road Walking Championship. Len Herbert ran very well to finish 2nd in the Inter-Counties 3 miles run when he clocked 14 mins. 37.8 secs. Ron Kemp won the Hampshire Constabulary 2 Miles Open Walk at Eastleigh off 250 yards. Four of our walkers, Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen, Ron Kemp and G. Gregory were invited to walk in the 10,000 metres race at the White City on July 5th, mainly a trial for the European Games. The Club has met with successes in many open meetings and our team of Walker, Sexton, Beaumont and Underwood won the Mile Medley Relay at the Charlotteville meeting on Whit-Monday. Geoff Osmint won the open 100 yards at the same meeting and “ Ginger ” Holtum was 3rd after winning the Open 100 at the Watford meeting on Whit-Saturday. It is interesting to note that the three Police Walking Championships, 2 miles, 10 miles and 34 miles have been won by “A” Division whose teams on each occasion have consisted of all Belgrave Harriers. The individual titles have also been won by our walkers, viz., Readman, Readman and Bidgood respectively. Mick Porter finished 5th in the Doncaster to Sheffield Marathon Race on Easter Monday, which was run in very bad weather conditions. Bert Clayton was 3rd in the Inter-Counties 7 Miles Track Championship. Harry Churcher won the 2 miles. or better still bring a friend with you! Thanks are due to Bert Mitchell for kindly presenting two miniature shields for this year's Marathon Championship. Doug Whitehead writes from Abusultan, M.E.A.F., that he has gained his R.A.F. Egypt “ blue ” for javelin and recently won seven events in the station sports. Also he shows the right spirit by joining two of his comrades to the Club. Sends best wishes to all and will be with us soon again. Pte. Joe Tranter (Splinter) writes from Malaya and by all accounts is doing quite well. Has recently won four cups and a medal and says he is running like a carthorse—some carthorse. Also sends good wishes to all Belgravians. We are happy to report that Frank Thompson is now quite well again and is, in fact, attending athletic meetings. Harry Churcher once again won the Business Houses 2 Miles Track Championship, with Bob McMullen 2nd and at the same meeting young Dan Godfrey won the 100 and 200 Youths' events. Vern Blowfield won the 1 mile title when beating Stan Cox, the Olympic Games runner. J. W. Brown, V. S. Blowfield, C. W. Walker and L. A. Adams gained 3rd place in the 4 x 1 mile “ Victory ” Relay at the Inter-Club Relay held at White City on June 10th. Alan Sexton has won the R.A.F. 220 Yards Championship. Congratulations to Dr. Woodard and Mrs. Woodard on the birth of their second son, Nicholas Andrew. Born June 20th. In order to create competition within the family we learn he is a member of H.H.H. We are happy to report that his elder brother, Christopher, who is a Belgrave Harrier, is now quite well after his recent serious illness. G. Warr G. items.label: No. 110
items.sum: Editorial marking the purchase of the freehold of the club hall, thanking W. G. Webb on leaving the presidency and welcoming Alf Harley as new President, with Christmas greetings.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial marking the purchase of the freehold of the club hall, thanking W. G. Webb on leaving the presidency and welcoming Alf Harley as new President, with Christmas greetings. Dear Fellow Members, It has already been said that this year, with the purchase of the freehold of our Hall, another page in the history of the Club has been turned. But in the flush of this new era let us not overlook a page which has recently been turned, one full of the hazards and hard work that made it possible for the first-mentioned page to be turned. We refer to the page of W. G. Webb, which, in the process of turning, has given us first a Treasurer and then a President. To many of us who have served long on your committee a great change has now taken place. A familiar face is missing from the head of the table at all our meetings, a face that for over fourteen years took its place on the right of the President and for the last two years has occupied the Presidential chair. How strange not to see him there now. By this we do not suggest he is taking it easy, by no means. Bill has been a really hardworking Treasurer and a popular President. His page may have been turned, but we know you will continue to see the name of W. G. Webb in future pages, and we hope, too, Bill, for many years to come. As for our new President, Alf Harley, it is difficult to find any page in the Club history over the past 20 years that has not some reference to him and certainly in our recent progress Alf's name figures most prominently. We know as a President he will be relentless in getting the best out of everybody for the good of the Club, and were we not good clubmen and eager to serve one who has served us so well, we should view the coming year with a certain amount of apprehension, for the amount of work which Alf will certainly undertake and the amount he will expect us to do. That we will serve both him as the President, and the Club as a whole, he has no doubts, and so he may command. May we hope that his term of office will see the turning of yet more vital and successful pages in our Club history. And just by the way. This issue will, of course, be the last one of 1950, so we, your Editors, take this opportunity, perhaps rather early, of wishing you all — and that includes all our supporters and friends — A VERY HAPPY CHRISTMAS AND A PROSPEROUS NEW YEAR. YOUR EDITORS. W. G. Webb W. G. Webb former Treasurer (over fourteen years) and retiring President (two years) Alf Harley Alf Harley new President

items.label: No. 110
items.sum: The new President thanks members for electing him and reviews the Belgrave Presidents who preceded him.
items.s: FROM YOUR PRESIDENT The new President thanks members for electing him and reviews the Belgrave Presidents who preceded him. May I express my humble thanks to Club members for electing me to the proud position of President of the Belgrave Harriers. It is with pride, and at the same time humility, that I follow in the steps of a distinguished and hard-working line of Belgrave Presidents, every one of whom has served the Club in a variety of ways and honoured the Club in accepting the honour bestowed on him. I think of the late Bob Ricketts, President when I joined the Club in 1926; and I know his influence and personality to be with us still. Harry Hare succeeded him. Here was a young man who was Hon. Secretary and Treasurer within 12 months of joining the Club, the first Hon. Editor of a printed "Belgravian," the prime move in initiating our Building Fund and a leader and guide in so many club activities, yet still finding time to win a Club championship and score in winning National Championship teams. Jimmy Bellchamber, an Hon. Auditor since 1912 and a Walking Captain with personality and real leadership, added lustre to the Chair, as did Jock McKay, our Hon. Treasurer for many years and later an auditor; and Ted Gordon, a tower of strength in so many ways since he joined in 1911, particularly in regard to our Building Fund. Oscar Horwood had been Hon. Secretary of the Club in the difficult days when the club's finances were very meagre and Belgrave had only been kept in existence by constant recourse to one's own pocket and hours of toil, often unrewarding. It was fitting, therefore, that he should become President in happier days. Wally Bayliss, as Captain, Assistant Hon. Secretary and Hon. Secretary, served the club supremely well for many years, and of undisputed right became our President. Harry Evans, bringing walking honours to the Club name as far back as 1909, worthily held the Presidential reins, as has Frank Thompson (elected a Life member in 1897), a former Hon. Secretary and the Club's representative on A.A.A. Committees and the man who put in more attendances at Battersea Park Track, all in the Club's interest, than any other — alive or dead. We now come to the more recent years, when the office of President has been upheld in its dignity by Dick Savage, Harry Parker, whose 38 years of Club work have most unfortunately been cut short recently, as we all know to our sorrow, and Bill Webb, 14 years an Hon. Treasurer, a former Cross Country Captain, a Trustee and our President for the last two years, to whom we offer our sincere thanks for a job well done and in line with the traditions of the past. I can only say that I am deeply conscious of all that has gone before; and with your help will try hard not to let my predecessors down. Let us all find in the traditions given us by our former Presidents, which I have tried to outline (most inadequately and in the sketchiest form only) an inspiration to go forward to even greater things than this great Club of ours has yet achieved. A. A. HARLEY, President. A. A. Harley A. A. items.sum: The new Hon. Treasurer urges members to pay subscriptions and race fees promptly and to support the Supporters' Club and social functions.
items.s: FROM THE HON. TREASURER The new Hon. Treasurer urges members to pay subscriptions and race fees promptly and to support the Supporters' Club and social functions. Those who were at the A.G.M. will need no telling of how important the matter of £ s. d. is to the Club. Running a club of our size and scope entails a continuous drain on our finances. A glance at the balance sheet will show how much is spent on items, such as team expenses, printing, postage and prizes. Throughout recent years the Club has maintained its high standard without increasing subscriptions by any large amount and by keeping Club handicap and championship fees at their pre-war level of one shilling. So it is up to everybody to make sure that they are up to date with their subs and to pay all race fees promptly. How else can you help the club finances? Are you acquainted with the Supporters' Club, which has raised so much money over recent years? Any Club official will be pleased to furnish particulars of the scheme, or Les Cohen, Hon. Secretary of the Supporters' Club, will be pleased to oblige. It is hoped that many more members will be participating in the scheme. No doubt reference is made elsewhere to Club social functions. These deserve fullest support and if you don't get value for your money it will be your own fault. If we may return to the subject of the A.G.M., my predecessor, Syd King, said that I would fill the bill for treasurer, he did not say "foot the bill," that's your job. Thank you for reading this and thank you in anticipation. G. S. DOUBLEDAY. 219, West Barnes Lane, New Malden, Surrey. G. S. Doubleday G. S. DOUBLEDAY Hon. Treasurer Les Cohen Les Cohen Hon. Secretary of the Supporters' Club Syd King Syd King previous Hon. Treasurer New Malden

items.label: No. 110
items.sum: Account of the club's Annual General Meeting of 7 October 1950, with the Treasurer's balance sheet, election of Life Members and the nomination of Alf Harley as President.
items.s: ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING, OCTOBER 7th, 1950 Account of the club's Annual General Meeting of 7 October 1950, with the Treasurer's balance sheet, election of Life Members and the nomination of Alf Harley as President. The writer of these notes was waylaid by the Editor shortly before the meeting was due to begin and asked if he would produce an account of it for the Belgravian. He was too surprised to think of a suitable excuse before the meeting started, hence this contribution. Bill Webb took the chair and opened proceedings by asking members to stand for a moment to the memory of the late Harry Parker. Minutes were read and approved and the Hon. Secretary's report, which had been previously circulated to members, was taken as read. Then came a very important item on the agenda, the presentation of the balance sheet by the Hon. Treasurer, Syd King. The balance sheet this year appeared in a most businesslike form, due, our Treasurer told us, to advice and assistance from some of our accountant members. It was so well made out that further explanation was not really necessary. The present satisfactory state of the funds is chiefly due to the efforts of the Supporters' Club. A gentle (?) reminder was given to those who had forgotten, or failed to pay their subscriptions. One or two interesting facts emerged from the balance sheet; Belgrave could run a highly successful "Open" walk and make a profit of 2/1 on it. The increased "Standards" had reduced expenditure on medals. After this came the election of Life Members. Syd King and Syd Roberts were elected. The former was proposed by Ernie Duffett and seconded by Les Cohen, and the latter proposed by Frank Elson and seconded by Gordon Doubleday. As Doub remarked, the only thing that Frank had left him to say was his ability to collect subs from walkers! The proceedings were interrupted for the President to award the "Belgrave" Cup for the Brighton Walk to A. J. Stirling Wakeley, who had to leave early. It has been customary for the retiring President to nominate his successor. Bill Webb conformed to custom and nominated Alf Harley to carry the reins for the year 1950-51. For the information of newer members, Bill gave a resumé of Alf's activities as a Belgravian since joining the Club in 1926. We were told, amongst other things, that the financial stability of our magazine in the days when Alf was Editor was ensured on the profits made on the Club ties he sold! We learnt, too, that Alf, before he retired from running (?) was the forerunner of Wint. It is, perhaps, indicative of our new President's nature that he took up walking and left Wint a clear field. The existing Vice-Presidents were elected en bloc, together with H. W. Elsey, C. Munroe and F. H. Elson. The question of who should be Club Hon. Secretary for the coming year had already been discussed in committee, and Ernie Duffett rose to propose Alf Harley, who was duly elected. Alf will continue to control the policy, but will be assisted in the more routine matters by the Assistant Hon. Secretary and various Club members. The retiring Hon. Treasurer proposed G. S. Doubleday to succeed him. Doub was unanimously elected and was seen in action during the tea interval. Election of other officials followed. J. B. Bellchamber gave some interesting details of Club finances. His first balance sheet for the year 1911-12 showed a slight deficit, which members made up. He told how Harry Hare, the originator, Tom Cotton and Frank Elson had started what, in more recent years under "Sir Stafford" Cohen (who apparently has a natural affinity for money), has developed into the Supporters' Club. Tom Carter was re-elected Hon. Social Secretary, after which names of those proposed for elected members of the committee were read out. Ballot papers were completed and handed in and whilst the count was being taken, members adjourned for tea. After tea, the "Tommy Green" cup for the year's outstanding performance by a Club member was presented to Bill Lucas for his fourth place in the A.A.A. three-mile Championship, where he returned the fastest time (14 mins. 1.6 sec.) ever done by a Club member. The meeting proper was over now and it was only a matter of waiting for votes to be counted. Whilst waiting, and in lighter vein, various questions were asked and answers given. It is encouraging to know that at some future date there will be garages available for members' cars. However, in the immediate present, accommodation for bicycles is causing the committee some concern. The meeting closed at 6.15 p.m., and I am sure the members present went away from this A.G.M. with a very satisfied feeling in the knowledge that the hall was at least 100 per cent. ours and that the Club had taken another decisive step forward in the last 12 months. items.label: No. 110
items.sum: A guest's impression of the Belgrave Club Dinner at the Corner House, Coventry Street, Piccadilly, on Friday 13th October.
items.s: THE CLUB DINNER A guest's impression of the Belgrave Club Dinner at the Corner House, Coventry Street, Piccadilly, on Friday 13th October. An impression by one of our guests, Inspr. G. Malkin, Hon. Secretary of the M.P.A.A. Whoever decided that the Belgrave Club Dinner should be held on Friday, 13th October, was obviously not superstitious. As events proved, their optimism was well founded, for the evening was a great success. When I arrived at the Corner House, Coventry Street, Piccadilly, I was immediately struck by the large gathering, far more than I had ever seen at a club dinner. Squeezing my way through the crowd near the bar, I noticed many well-known figures in the athletic world, too numerous to mention individually. There was, however, something rather strange about them, until I realised that I was seeing them behind cocktail glasses instead of the more usual pint pots. The speeches were entertaining and just the right length. The standard was set by the first speaker, Alf Harley, in proposing the toast of the "Club," and the response by H. Shields. Other speakers, Syd Roberts, who proposed the toast of the "Guests," followed by Ernie Clynes and the new President of the R.W.A., E. Kennell, all paid tribute to the ladies, rather diplomatically, I thought. Evidently with an eye to the future. Dancing which followed was to the music of Les Reeves and his band, with the M.C., H. Ellsey, doing his job most admirably. I believe that it is an axiom of the entertainment world that the customer should go away wishing the show had been a little longer. Judging by this, the whole function was one of the best, for when it was time to go, I think we all wished it had lasted another half hour. Altogether a very pleasant evening, which I shall remember for a very long time. I very nearly forgot, the meal was excellent, too. G.J.M. To add to the above report, it was unanimously voted a grand night by those attending; but we were disappointed that so many chose to stay away. To those who enjoyed this delightful evening we say "You lucky people." To those who didn't, either through superstition or apathy, we say "You silly people," and to those who found the financial aspect or other circumstances too pressing, we say "We hope you will come along next year and enjoy yourself with Belgrave Friends, as we did." items.s: A.A.A. MARATHON Belgrave finishers in the A.A.A. Marathon at Reading on 22 July, with complaints about the poor arrangements after the race. At Reading on July 22nd our first man home was Syd Ring, who finished 28th. Dick Towndrow, Dick Tobin and George Chantler did not finish the course and our actual finishers and times were as under:— 28. S. T. Ring, 2.52.50; 47, G. M. Pearson, 3.6.20; 49, A. Smith, 3.9.55; 52, J. McDonald, 3.12.15; 55, G. S. Doubleday, 3.12.55. The arrangements after the race were far from good for a race of this calibre, the washing facilities were very poor and the competitors were also unable to obtain any tea or refreshments by the time they had finished. We do think that to ask chaps to run 26 miles and then not to make any arrangements for their comfort is not very helpful as regards future entries for this race. items.sum: Report of the senior and junior triangular track matches with Cambridge Harriers and Blackheath Harriers at Charlton Park Track on 26 July.
items.s: MATCH v. CAMBRIDGE HARRIERS Report of the senior and junior triangular track matches with Cambridge Harriers and Blackheath Harriers at Charlton Park Track on 26 July. At Charlton Park Track on July 26th there were junior and senior events and these took the form of triangular matches between Blackheath H., Cambridge H. and ourselves. We did fairly well in the senior match and Lowers won the 100 yards, while Basil Walden won the 220 1st string, with Des Mullen third in the 2nd string race at this distance. Odde was third in the 440 and Jack Brown won the 880 yards in 2 mins. 1.3 secs., with Archie Bedford in fourth place. Len Bishop was third in the 1 mile, but Charlie Smart surprised the locals by winning the 2-mile race, in which he beat Broughton, of Blackheath, in the fast time of 9 mins. 29.6 secs. Bergvalds, our Latvian member, won the Discus and was second in the Shot Putt, with Bill Sutton in third place. Total points in the senior match were:—Cambridge H. 37½; Belgrave H. 34½; Blackheath H. 31. In the Junior match, Frank Kemp scored a good double by winning the 100 and 220, and Bob Wolton was second in the 440, while Maclean won the 880 yards and Ray Tooby the mile. Once again the field events saw us well behind on points scoring and the final result of the match was:—Cambridge H. 47; Belgrave H. 36; Blackheath H. 12. e: Club Hop, Step and Jump championship
items.s: COMBINED MEETING AT TOOTING TRACK—JUNE 19th Report and results of the club Hop, Step and Jump championship and club handicap events held at a combined meeting with London Olympiades A.C. at Tooting Track on 19 June. This was a combined meeting with the London Olympiades A.C. and we decided the club Hop, Step and Jump championship together with some club handicap events. There was a disappointing turn-out for the 100 yards (under 19) race and only four runners faced the starter. The winner was a newcomer to the club, H. Oulton, late of Preston Harriers. The 440 yards handicap saw three heats and the final was won by N. F. Gibson, better known as a high-jumper, with Len Bishop second and young A. C. Hanlon third. Brian Shepherd won the 2 miles walk with E. Jeffery reaping the reward of his perseverance by being placed second and Sid Jarlett who has now gone over to walking, securing third place. In the 2 miles run, Bill Lucas ran well off the back mark of 20 yards to go through his field to win in the good time of 9 min. 19.4 secs. Arthur Bruce was second with Jack Brown third. A. Machell won the Shot Putt handicap and Charlie Jones got away with first place in the Javelin event and it was interesting to see that Tom Underwood secured a couple of placings in these events whereas he does not seem to be having a very good season from the running point of view. The Hop, Step and Jump championship was won by P. Lowe with 41 ft. 4½ in., which is quite a good effort, but we are in dire need of some jumpers in the club ranks for the Triple, High and Long Jumps. So often do we take part in these Inter-Club matches and yet have the greatest difficulty in turning out men for the jump events and we hope that members will bear this in mind when signing on any new members. items.s: JUNIOR MATCH AT CROYDON Report of the junior match against Whitgift Middle School at Croydon on 22 June, won by the School 28 points to 17, with Belgrave placings. At the Whitgift Middle School's ground on June 22nd, the School were winners by 28 points to our 17. items.s: SENIOR MATCH AT ALPERTON Report of the senior match against Thames Valley Harriers at Alperton on 1 July, lost 72 points to 34. On July 1st we did not have a very good turn-out against our old friends and rivals Thames Valley Harriers. In fact one club member described it as "disgusting" and so the home club were easy winners by scoring 72 points to our 34. Geoff. Osmint and Des. Mullen turned out in the sprint events but had to be satisfied with minor placings against the local runner, E. Purver. Arthur Bruce was second in the 880 yards and Stan Davies had to run a quarter in order to gain a point for third place. Our bright "spot" was the 1 mile win of Bill Lucas in 4 min. 29 secs. and that of Les. Stokell in the 2 miles run in 9 min. 54.8 secs. The six field events were all wins for T.V.H. and although we had N. F. Gibson in the two jumping events we were poorly represented in the others and you cannot expect to do well in this class of match unless you have equal representation in both the running and field events. items.sum: Report of the 10,000 metres track walk at the White City on 5 July, a European Games trial won by Hardy, with Harry Churcher recording his fastest time for the distance.
items.s: 10,000 METRES WALK—WHITE CITY, JULY 5th Report of the 10,000 metres track walk at the White City on 5 July, a European Games trial won by Hardy, with Harry Churcher recording his fastest time for the distance. Four of our walkers were invited to compete in the 10,000 metres track walk at the White City which was a trial for the forthcoming European Games. The race was eagerly looked forward to, to see how the two Northerners, Allen and Hardy, would shape against Harry Churcher. Hardy soon went into the lead followed by Harry and Allen. Harry continued in second place for 3½ miles, when Hardy had a lead of three seconds and Allen drew level with Harry. At 4 miles Hardy's time was 28.31, with Allen 2 seconds behind and Harry third, another 2 seconds behind. Over the next mile, Harry lost a little ground and in the 21st lap Allen was disqualified. Hardy continued to increase his lead and eventually won in the very fast time of 43 min. 13 secs. Harry's time of 43.54, however, is his fastest for the distance. Bob McMullen was 4th in 48.52 and G. Gregory 9th in 50.17. Allen Allen disqualified in the 21st lap Hardy Hardy won in 43 min. 13 secs. Our usual mob match with Surrey Walking Club coincided with the A.A.A. 10,000 metres walk at the White City and in addition to Harry and Mac being invited to compete, a number of our other members were anxious to see how Hardy and Allen, of Sheffield, would shape against our 5 miles World Record Holder. e: Match v. Dorking St. Paul's A.C.
items.s: SENIOR MATCH AT DORKING Report of the senior match at Dorking St. Paul's A.C. on 8 July, lost 70–68. Held on July 8th at the pleasantly situated ground of the Dorking St. Paul's A.C. and after a very close and exciting match we finished up losers by the narrow margin of 2 points. As usual we were minus any high jumpers, but Les Christmas and our new member, Odde, very sportingly filled in, in order to score points for the third and fourth places. In the 100 yards we had first two places through Gordon Lowers and Basil Walden, and the latter also won the 220 yards with Alan Picton in second place. The 440 yards saw I. W. Odde, a newcomer to the club, who reminds us very much of J. Cooper Clark, our old club champion, and we hope that with further experience Odde will gradually improve and he may yet find that a half-mile will be his best distance. A. G. Steadman, another newcomer to our ranks, gained second place in the Long Jump and then proceeded to win the Hop, Step and Jump event. D. Childs was second in the Shot Putt and third in the Discus Throw and Terry Bateman also helped us out in these events. Alan Bishop and Archie Bedford were first home in the 880 yards and Archie also ran a good race to win the 1 mile in 4.34. In the 2 miles our only two runners were Len Bishop and Ted Stimpson, whereas Dorking had J. W. Stone, the Surrey C.C. champion, and J. Butler, the well-known Surrey A.C. runner, representing them, and needless to say they finished well in front of our lads. The last event was a four-lap relay race and our team of Underwood, Odde, Heathfield and Picton put up a fine show to win in 2 min. 44.8 secs., which was only a couple of seconds outside the ground record. Final points scoring was : Dorking St. Paul's A.C. 70; Belgrave Harriers 68; and we thank the home club for providing our members with some refreshments after the match. items.sum: Report of the senior match against Herne Hill Harriers at Tooting on 10 July, lost 70–43 owing to weakness in the field events.
items.s: SENIOR MATCH v. HERNE HILL H. Report of the senior match against Herne Hill Harriers at Tooting on 10 July, lost 70–43 owing to weakness in the field events. This match, held at Tooting on July 10th, consisted of 12 events with 6 running and 6 field. To stand any chance of winning such a match you must have a sound bunch of field event performers and this is where we are lacking compared with other clubs that we meet. In four of the six field events Herne Hill secured maximum points, thus giving them 8 to 1 margins in each, and the two others were 6 to 3 in their favour. The 100 yards saw Basil Walden and Gordon Lowers in front and Basil also won the 220 with Alan Picton in third place. Ches Walker won the 880 and Bob Taylor filled fourth place to score a point for us, but in the 440 yards Herne Hill had the first three home with Jim Heathfield first of our runners. Len Herbert won the 1 mile in 4 min. 35.2 secs. and we also won the 4 x 110 yards relay in 46.1 secs. Final points were : Herne Hill H. 70; Belgrave H. 43. SHAFTESBURY HARRIERS Report of the match against Shaftesbury Harriers at Parliament Hill on 12 July, won 30–29 after sprints and the 2 miles were cancelled for lack of Belgrave runners. Held at Parliament Hill Track on July 12th and we are sorry to say that as none of our sprinters were in attendance the sprint races had to be cancelled. Young D. G. Maclean ran for us in the 1 mile and did well to finish second to D. J. Thompson, the international runner, and " Mac " clocked 4 min. 33.8 secs., which is good going for a lad of his age. Ches Walker won the 440 yards, with Odde in second place, and Jack Brown won the 880, with Archie Bedford fourth. Bill Sutton, D. Childs and A. C. Allen helped us out in the field events and with the match being reduced to six events only, we came out winners with 30 points to Shaftesbury's 29. Another startling feature was the fact that as we had no distance men present, the 2 miles race was also off, and we must apologise to the home club for our members' poor support of this fixture. It may have been due to the fact that we had already had a match two nights earlier, but in a club of our size one would think that we could easily turn out teams twice in a week. D. G. Maclean D. G. items.s: THE A.A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report on Belgrave members at the A.A.A. Championships at White City on 14–15 July, with notes on the Southern Championships, All-Ireland Championships and A.A.A. 2 miles walk. At the White City Stadium on July 14th-15th, we had quite a number of members entered and, on the whole, they performed very creditably. In the 100 yards heats we had M. H. Broadbent, G. R. Lowers, D. J. Merrett and B. F. Walden, and of these, Merrett was placed second in his heat and so qualified for the semi-finals. G. H. Jarvis, our old member who is now first claim to the Milocarian A.C., won his heat in the 440 yards hurdles, and so qualified for the final of that event. We had no entries in the 880 or 440 yards, which gives a clear indication of our present weakness at these distances. In the 220 yards we had Walden and Merrett and the former was third in his heat won in 21.8 and the latter won his heat in the good time of 22.4 secs. Merrett thus qualified for both sprint semi-finals and I think it is a long time since we had a club member in this position. The heats of the 1 mile saw Jack Brown and Ches Walker competing and a notable absentee was Derrick Burfitt. Brown ran quite well to finish inside the standard time of 4 min. 25 secs., and Walker also gained standard and actually finished a very close fourth in his heat with the first three only going forward to the final. In the six miles race we had Charlie Smart as our only representative, but Charlie put up a fine display and gained as many cheers from the crowd as did the winner, F. Aaron. He was just beaten on the tape for 4th place by D. C. Birch, and as the second and third men home were foreigners, Charlie missed a fine chance of being the second Englishman to finish. Our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, competed in the Discus event but failed to reach the standard of 125 feet. In the 7 miles walk Harry Churcher, the holder, was a non-starter and our only finisher was A. Readman in fifth place with a time of 56 min. 18.6 secs., which was just outside standard time. The 3 miles saw Vern Blowfield, Bill Lucas, Len Herbert and Charlie Smart running in our colours and at one stage of the race the Belgrave vests were in the two leading positions. Len Herbert dropped back, however, but Bill Lucas still kept with the leading bunch and looked full of running. At the bell he was on the shoulder of Theys, the Belgian, but when the latter made his effort, Bill was forced to drop back and Olney then came by him to gain second place. Bill was striding comfortably down the home straight in third place when Ferguson, of Highgate, came with a late burst to beat him by inches and so another chance of being the second Englishman home was lost. Bill's time was 14 min. 11.6 secs., which is easily the fastest 3 miles ever run by a club member. Len Herbert also beat the standard time of 14.50, as did Charlie Smart, who ran well after his previous effort. On June 24th in the Southern Championships at Southampton, Derrick Burfitt was second in the 1 mile and Ches Walker third, which is the first time we have ever had two men placed in this event. At the same meeting we had the first three home in the 2 miles walk in Harry Churcher, Percy Wright and our new member, R. S. Kemp. In the All-Ireland Championships at Dublin on July 8th, D. E. Mullen, running in our name, finished second in the 220 yards and so gained selection for the Triangular International. The A.A.A. 2 miles walk championship was held at Reading on July 22nd and Percy Wright finished second, but as there were only two competitors it was rather an empty honour, although Percy is to be complimented on turning out against an opponent who evidently frightened all other opposition away. items.h: INTER CLUB TRACK WALKS—TOOTING BEC., JULY 19th
items.sum: Report and judge W. Atkinson's comments on the inter-club track walks promoted by Belgrave at Tooting Bec on 19 July, won by Belgrave Harriers, with results.
items.s: INTER CLUB TRACK WALKS—TOOTING BEC., JULY 19th Report and judge W. Atkinson's comments on the inter-club track walks promoted by Belgrave at Tooting Bec on 19 July, won by Belgrave Harriers, with results. The popularity of this meeting was clearly emphasised, both by the entries and the support it was given on the night. No fewer than 64 walkers competed in the four races, which were witnessed by a crowd of at least 2,000 people. Five clubs out of the ten entered, fielded a full team of eight walkers and after a close contest between Belgrave, Highgate and Surrey W.C. we came out on top nine points in front of Highgate and eleven in front of Surrey. Woodford Green, last year's winners, were fourth. Mr. W. Atkinson, one of the judges at the meeting, has sent us the following comments on the evening :— On July 19th I again had the pleasure of attending and acting as a judge at the Inter-Club Walking Contest promoted by Belgrave Harriers at Tooting Bec Track. For those interested in walking I consider this one of the best events of the year. At most sports meetings we only see one walking event and that usually takes place late in the programme. Here we have four races, all walking events, and most if not all, the best walkers in the country can be seen. The organisers are to be congratulated on the manner in which the " show " was conducted. The events were well up to time and although it had to be a late evening meeting, we were able to get away bfore dusk. This was quite an improvement on the last time we had been asked to attend this track. We were timed to be there at 3.30 p.m., only to find that the 7 miles walk had started at 3.15 p.m. However, someone made up for this lost quarter of an hour a few days later when we were asked to be at Motspur Park at 3.30 p.m. for a meeting which was not timed to commence until 6.30 p.m. with the walk at 7.45 p.m. The results of the four races are given below and very little comment can be made on them. The walking was good and most of the results as expected. After a flying start by one of the competitors in the five miles, the race developed into a procession and some of the walkers looked as though they were training for the Brighton. I think McMullen, in the four miles, walked the best I have seen him do. The three and two miles were interesting races and the results remained in doubt until the last lap. Some newcomers to walking were seen and with proper training should develop into good walkers next year. I will only mention one—B. Shepherd, of the Walton Club. I have seen this young man win two races recently and he improves each time he turns out. I went away pleased to think that no walker had been disqualified but I now learn there was one offender. I always look upon disqualifications in walking as a serious matter and that you are telling the walker he is cheating. At the same time I would like to mention that I am strongly in favour of the English definition., i.e., maintaining contact with the ground. There are many walkers who appear to be running rather than walking until one carefully looks at their feet and the feet are all that should be looked at when judging. Provided the man is maintaining contact, he is complying with the definition, if not, he is running and should be disqualified. There can be no half way between the two. W. ATKINSON. items.s: MATCH AT TADWORTH Report of the inter-club match at Tadworth Green on 19 July against Epsom & Ewell, Banstead and Redhill & Reigate, won easily by Belgrave. At Tadworth Green on July 19th was held an Inter-Club affair, the clubs competing being Epsom & Ewell H., Banstead H., Redhill & Reigate A.C. and ourselves. We had quite a good turn-out, the attraction probably being the " free " beer which had been promised after the meeting was over, and we were easy winners of the Inter-Club contest. Basil Walden won the senior 100 yards and Frank Kemp followed suit in the junior event at this distance. Odde was second in the quarter and Gerry Trower won the junior 880 in good style and Ches Walker was also first home in the senior half-mile. The senior 220 was run in two races and we had first home in each race through Basil Walden and Alan Picton. The junior 220 was run on similar lines and once again Belgrave had the two winners in Dave Marshall and Alan Law. Len Herbert and Bill Lucas had a nice comfortable run in the 1 mile and came in together, but Bill was running for his second claim club, Redhill, and so we shared points in this event. In the medley relay, Epsom were first home with the Bels. second and Redhill third, but our juniors proved best in the junior relay and so ended a very pleasant evening's sport. We must thank the local Committee for providing the aforementioned " free " beer and eats afterwards and a good time was had by all, including the club officials. items.sum: Extracts from Bert Clayton's newspaper article on the Nijmegen Marches (the four days), in which he and Jack Stirling-Wakeley took part.
items.s: DE VIERDAAGSCHE, 1950 Extracts from Bert Clayton's newspaper article on the Nijmegen Marches (the four days), in which he and Jack Stirling-Wakeley took part. (The four days) Two members of the club, Bert Clayton and Jack Stirling-Wakeley, took part in this year's Nijmegen Marches and we produce some extracts from an article by Bert Clayton published in an Eastleigh newspaper. Three British teams took part in the Marches this year, two from the R.W.A. and one from the R.A.F., the latter walking in full kit with rifles. At 5 a.m., on Tuesday, July 25th, the two R.W.A. teams moved off for the first day's journey. Before the 10 miles mark had been reached, I was suffering from blisters rather badly, so Harold Whitlock stopped behind and doctored. By the end of the day we were just beginning to appreciate the difference between racing and marching. We passed all the other teams and finished an hour ahead on each of the four days, because our natural pace was faster, although 11 hours were allowed to cover the distance. The remarkable feature of the whole affair was the terrific enthusiasm shown by spectators all along the routes. At one village we were hailed as " liberators." The second and third days were a repetition of the first, but the routes being different we saw quite a lot of Holland. At one point we marched along a road, the right side being Germany and the left Holland. At another time we had a good look at the Reichwald Forest, where so many violent tank battles were fought. On the second day we passed by the scene of the Arnhem conflict. Friday was a grand day and for the English team a most welcome one. Beginning at 5 a.m., the crowds were already then forming and about 6 miles from the finish the roads were packed on both sides with [illegible]00,000 people all armed with bouquets and floral gifts to present to the marchers. Various bands were coming out to escort marchers and the general effect of flowers and music was reminiscent of the " Battle of flowers." At the conclusion of the marching on Friday the medals were presented and on Friday evening a grand dance was held at the Town Hall. Most of the English team were there, not because the dancing in such a huge crowd was enjoyable, but because the ability or willingness to dance after four days marching was an unofficial test of further endurance.
