items.s: MATCH AT CHARLTON PARK Report of the 1 August senior and junior matches with Cambridge Harriers at Charlton Park; Cambridge won the senior match and Belgrave the junior. On August 1st we had senior and junior matches with the local club—Cambridge Harriers. Once again our numbers were not too many and we only had one runner in the two miles run, which was supposed to be a team event ! Gordon Lowers ran second in the 100 yards, with Eric Bishop gaining third place in the 440 yards. In the middle-distance events we did better, with Ian Badiali winning the quarter, Jack Brown the half-mile and Bill Lucas the mile, a very creditable trio of wins. A. Bergvalds won the Discus and was second in the Weight, while D. G. Maclean jumped for us in the High Jump and Gordon Lowers turned out in the Long Jump and Javelin events. We fared much better in the junior match, with Frank Kemp having a dual sprint victory, as did P. J. Casselton in the 440 and 880 yards. Don Maclean won the one mile and Alan Law won both the Weight and Discus events, and was second in the Javelin, and then he won the Long Jump to round off a very busy evening. Points in the senior match were : Cambridge H., 72; Belgrave H., 32; and for the junior match : Belgrave H., 56; Cambridge H., 39. items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP MEETING Report and results of the club championship meeting at Tooting on 4 August, with new club records by Jack Brown (mile), E. M. Bare (high jump) and A. Bergvalds (discus and weight). At Tooting, on August 4th, a good crowd was present to witness a very good afternoon's sport and one which saw several new club records established. The 100 yards saw a new title-holder in Frank Craft, who has now gone to Australia, worse luck, and he beat " Ginger " Holtum, with Alan Sexton in third place. The holder, Denis Merrett, was unable to run owing to injury. Frank Kemp retained his 100 yards junior title with P. J. Casselton second and Ian Forrester third. The 100 yards boys' race saw Ken Eales score an easy win and it was interesting to see the sons of Jack and Joe Flower, two old club champions, competing in this event. D. A. Wise scored a good win in the junior 880 and Ian Badiali, our new member from India, scored a popular win in the senior half-mile. His time of 1 min. 59.4 secs. was the second best time ever recorded and he is a decided asset to our ranks. G. H. Gregory won the two miles walk, with D. McMullen second and E. A. Smith third, and it seems rather rough on " Mac " that with Harry Churcher not competing we have yet another fine walker to step into his shoes and so keep " Mac " in his usual second position in these events. Frank Kemp again won the 220 yards junior, with J. Thomas second and Alan Law third, while Alan Sexton regained the senior 220 title, with Frank Craft second and Basil Walden third. Derek Godfrey lost his junior 440 title to Peter Casselton, but it was a very good race and both these lads are champions of the future. The senior 440 saw Ian Badiali gain a second title in quite fast time, and Jim Heathfield was a good second with Bob Wolton a plucky third. Don Maclean won the junior mile, as expected, and from the way he went off he seemed quite determined to make sure that Geoff Goode had no reserves of speed left. Brian Trower was third and here again the time was very good for juniors. The one mile senior was the race of the afternoon, with a very strong field turning out, but Jack Brown, the holder, ran a well-judged race to come away over the last 200 yards to beat Len Herbert and Chas. Walker. His time of 4 mins. 18 secs. was a new club record and must make some of the " ancients " think a bit when they consider the times we used to do in the old days. The field events saw a new club record set up in the High Jump when E. M. Bare cleared 6 feet. A. Bergvalds also set up a new club record in the Discus Throw and again in the Weight and he is a most consistent performer and deserves his successes. Jim Purdy in the junior High Jump set up new figures and Doug. Whitehead in the Javelin also did well. Complete results and times are given below :— 100 yds. Senior.—1, Craft; 2, Holtum; 3, Sexton. items.s: HAZELL TROPHY CONTEST Report of the Hazell Trophy contest at Aylesbury on August Monday, where Belgrave finished second to the Polytechnic in both the senior trophy and the junior inter-club contest. This was held at Aylesbury on August Monday and we did quite well in finishing second to the Polytechnic and only lost by 3 points. In the 100 yards we had " Ginger " Holtum second and Alan Sexton third, while Chas. Walker was third in the 1 mile, and then Len Herbert was first home in the 2 miles run. In the team event for the latter race we were second to the Poly, and our team in the medley relay finished third to the Poly and Walton A.C. As the trophy events were held in the evening, in order that the Poly and Walton " cracks " could get down from the White City meeting, it can be readily understood that had the events been held in the afternoon we should have scored an easy if somewhat " hollow " victory. Final points for the trophy were : Polytechnic H., 30; Belgrave H., 27; Walton A.C., 24; Thames Valley H., 21; Finchley H., 8; Woodford Green A.C., 4. Also on the programme was a Junior Inter-Club contest, and here again we finished second to the Polytechnic team. Frank Kemp won the 100 yards, with Ian Forrester third, and Frank was also second in the 220 yards. Don Maclean was second in the 880 and Geoff Goode occupied a similar position in the 1 mile. Our medley relay team scored a great win in 3 mins. 51 secs., and the final match points were : Polytechnic H., 28; Belgrave H., 25; Thames Valley H., 13; St. Alban's A.C., 5; Victoria Park H., 4; Vale of Aylesbury A.C., 4; Woodford Green A.C., 3; North London H., 2. items.s: CLUB HANDICAP MEETING Report of the August club handicap meeting held on the 13th, including a 440 yards for unattached novices. Our usual August handicap meeting was held on the 13th and once again entries were not up to standard and one wonders if it is worth while putting on so many handicap events, when they are so poorly supported by our members. We had two heats in the 100 yards, and the final was won by D. Goodchild, a fairly new member, with Ian Forrester second and Gordon Lowers third. Alan Picton won the 600 yards with Maurice Jones second and Eddie Lacey third, while Arthur Bruce won the 3 miles run, with Archie Bedford second and Ken Stimpson third. In the 880 yards (under 19) handicap, the winner was a new member in S. G. Boreham, while the two back-markers, Maclean and Wright, filled the other placed positions. The 2 miles walk was won by E. Hall with Syd Jarlett second and A. Wesson third, while first prize in the Javelin Throw went to a junior member in R. K. Woodley. Also on the programme was a 440 yards open to unattached novices, and this was won by J. Murphy, with Coxon second and Roffey third. items.label: No. 113
items.sum: Report on two floodlit meetings at the White City Stadium, including the London v. Gothenburg match.
items.s: FLOODLIT ATHLETICS Report on two floodlit meetings at the White City Stadium, including the London v. Gothenburg match. Quite recently we have had two of these meetings held at the White City Stadium, and both have proved that there is a good public for this form of meeting and it would appear that we shall have many more such meetings in future seasons. We were interested in both these meetings, as quite a number of our members were competing and in the first one held by the City Charity people, Denis Merrett was in both sprint finals, being fourth in the 100 and third in the 220 yards. In the 1 mile event we saw Jack Brown run a fine race to win in the new record time for this contest of 4 mins. 18.8 secs., and then in the 2 miles team race the individual winner proved to be young Ray Tooby, in the fast time of 9 mins. 17.2 secs. Tooby ran a really great race and as he beat Harry Hicks and Bill Lucas, both international runners, it would seem that next season Ray will be knocking on the door for international honours. Also at this meeting we saw Harry Churcher walk away from his field in the 2 miles walk and Harry showed that he is still a power to be reckoned with in this branch of the sport. The second meeting was the London v. Gothenburg match and the first event was a 7 miles walk and once again Harry Churcher gave the large crowd a thrill by keeping off the Swedish walker until just over the half-distance, when Harry had to give his much younger opponent best. Harry, however, held on to second position and his time of 52 mins. 28 secs. proves how well he walked. Then came what was for the Belgrave members who were present, a very proud moment, when Len Herbert fought out a most thrilling finish with the Swedish runner to gain a fine victory in the 2 miles run with a time of 9 mins. 18.4 secs. This was the third time that Len has competed in this annual contest and now at the age of 38 he scored his first win in really magnificent style. In the 1 mile match we saw Chas. Walker running as second string for London and right well did he do this when he beat the Swedish second string in an inches finish for third place. Also on the programme was a 3,000 metres steeplechase, and John Bromley received an invite to compete in this and was running well up with the field when he came a cropper at the water jump on about the fifth lap and then gradually fell back. We might say how pleased we were to see John Disley come into his own at last in this event and this just goes to prove how right his coach was. items.s: London Vidarians 25 miles Walk—August 25th Report and result of the London Vidarians 25 miles Walk on 25 August, a "Belgrave Benefit" in which H. Clayton won and Belgrave took the scratch and handicap team races. This proved to be a proper " Belgrave Benefit," since our walkers took the biggest part of the prizes. We had a very good entry, which no doubt was accounted for by the fact that we were concentrating on another Brighton success and right from the outset practically all our men walked exceptionally well, with the exception of Harry Shields, who unfortunately displeased a certain judge, and was ruled out. Hugh McGreechan once again showed how to go through the field on the second half of a long race and we finished with three scoring members in the first six. The same three also took first handicap team prizes, whilst our " B " team were third; added to this, Bert Clayton was third in the individual handicap, as well as winning the individual scratch race. items.sum: Report and Belgrave placings from the 8 September Brighton walk, where Belgrave were third (32 points) to Highgate Harriers (29) and Poly (30), and H. McGreechan won the "Belgrave" Cup in fifth place.
items.s: THE BRIGHTON WALK—SEPTEMBER 8th Report and Belgrave placings from the 8 September Brighton walk, where Belgrave were third (32 points) to Highgate Harriers (29) and Poly (30), and H. McGreechan won the "Belgrave" Cup in fifth place. Of all the " near misses " which we have experienced in team races, the " Brighton " of 1951 will surely go down as the nearest of them all. With four men in the first twelve and the first team to finish, we had to be content with third place, only three points separating us from the winners. With the exception of Bert Clayton, who was previously a doubtful starter, all our " A " Team turned up at Westminster on the morning of September 8th, plus a very plucky " B " Team, who hoped to gain nothing more than a few blisters, and everything looked fairly well set for us to bring the shield back once gain. All our walkers settled down to steady walking, with Hugh McGreechan as our first man. Close behind were Jack Rutland, Jack Bidgood, Jack Wakeley and Harry Shields. As early as Croydon, Jack Wakeley showed signs of trouble with his shoes and soon began losing ground. The other four kept going well and a check at Horley showed us a slight lead over Highgate, with Poly also quite close. Hugh then started putting the pressure on and rapidly gained places, but this was offset by McSweeney of Highgate and Bailey of Poly, who were also moving up very fast. Meanwhile, our next scoring three were hanging close together and undoubtedly helping each other along. A further check at Peas Pottage disclosed that we were then tying with Highgate at 35 points each, whilst Poly were third with 39 points. McSweeney and Bailey, however, still continued to make up a number of places and although Hugh McGreechan was increasing his speed and overtook three men, as two of them were individuals this did not affect the score to any great extent and at the Castle Hickstead, Highgate had a clear lead of about 10 points, with Poly second and us third. Hugh was then told to try and make up a couple more places, and walking at a pace, probably faster than anyone in the race he proceeded to overtake first Leveridge of the Beagles and then Megnin of Highgate, two very valuable points. In the meantime, the other three still kept well together and succeeded in overtaking one of the Poly men. Their efforts, however, did not reap the full reward, although the result remained in doubt until after our four scoring members had finished. With Poly's fourth man in, their score was 2 points less than ours, which meant we had lost the shield, but we still had to wait for Highgate's fourth man, who eventually scored in 16th position to give Highgate team honours with 29 points, Poly second, with 30 points, and us third, with 32 points. Hugh continued his fast pace and finished in fifth position in the excellent time of 8 hrs. 46 mins. 25 secs., thus winning the " Belgrave " Cup at his second attempt. Second and third places were shared by Jack Bidgood and Jack Rutland, whilst Harry Shields was only a couple of places behind. Our other " A " Team men, Dick Frazer, Fred Rolfe and Joe Wilson, all finished in the thirties. A most surprising race was walked by John Downs, a member who we have seen but little of. After only having a couple of strolls, he tackled his first Brighton and completed the course in under 10 hours, finishing perfectly fit and without one blister. Congratulations, John, on a good show. Our remaining walkers, Alan Robins, Syd Spencer and Gordon Doubleday, all finished the course, whilst Ron Fairman was obliged to retire with blistered feet. A good number of supporters and a grand team of attendants accompanied the walkers and it is quite certain, had much to do with the progress of our lads. The reinstitution of a double-decker bus worked exceptionally well and provided good transport for the cycles on the return journey. In congratulating all the walkers on their splendid efforts, I think we should add a word of sympathy on their near success. items.sum: Report and results of the final track meeting at Tooting on 15 September, where L. W. Herbert won the club 3 miles track championship in a new club record, with handicap events.
items.s: FINAL TRACK MEETING Report and results of the final track meeting at Tooting on 15 September, where L. W. Herbert won the club 3 miles track championship in a new club record, with handicap events. This was held at Tooting on September 15th, and we had the club 3 miles track championship with a number of handicap events. The latter were again not too well supported, but we had a big field for the 3 miles and this probably affected the entries for some of the other events. Jack Brown, the holder, was a non-starter, but a small bunch of runners soon detached themselves from the rest of the field with Lucas, Herbert, Tooby, Bromley, Stokell, Bruce and Stearman more or less together. Herbert then went in front and gradually drew away from the rest, with Bromley and Lucas having a battle for the other placed positions. The time was a new club record for this event and showed that all our lads were running well for so late in the season. The 880 yards handicap saw two new members out in front and both Murphy and Coxon are very useful additions to our ranks. Doug Briggs managed to gain third place in a fast-run race. In the 220 yards handicap we had two heats and the final was won by J. D. Benstead with P. Cornish second and Frank Kemp third. The latter ran well off a back mark but is considering taking it easy for the next season or two. The 1 mile (under 19) event saw the limit man retain his lead throughout, with Harry Greene making a good effort to overtake him. Peter Courtney was third and Don Maclean, who was the scratch man, seemed to be having a training run only. In the 2 miles walk we saw our old friend Colin Sutton getting among the prizes once again and his trip abroad has evidently not impaired his speed. We put on a 120 Hurdles event, but this only drew three competitors and John Briggs just failed to catch his limit man. B. Miska won the Discus handicap from George Powell and the Hop, Step and Jump handicap was won by Ian Forrester. Also on the programme was an 880 yards novices race, open to unattached competitors, but we only had three starters for this and one wonders if there are any unattached athletes about, especially as most lads seem to join a club while still at school. items.s: SURREY COUNTY ROAD RELAY Report of the Surrey County Road Relay, won by Belgrave for the fourth time to take the "John Underhill" Memorial Trophy, ahead of Herne Hill Harriers. This was the fourth race to be held and once again we managed to win the " John Underhill " Memorial Trophy for the fourth time. Our team was minus Len Herbert and Len Adams, not to mention Jack Braughton and Jimmy Wood, who are eligible for this event, so that although we were pressed rather closely by Herne Hill Harriers, who had Greene, of Reading, assisting them, we can be quite satisfied with the actual result. John Bromley handed over in third place on the first " leg " and then Arthur Bruce took us into the lead with a really fine run and he did the fastest time of our team and indeed the third fastest of the afternoon. The rest of our team managed to keep in front, although Chas. Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race. Times of our runners were : Bromley, 14.31; Bruce, 14.20; Walker, 14.32; Bedford, 14.35; Short, 14.40; Lucas, 14.25. On September 29th a field of 73 runners faced the starter. As there were also many others out for training spins this meant that we had over a hundred club members attending Belgrave Hall for the opening run of the winter season, which is a very healthy sign. George Still was first away as the limit man and he also finished the course in good style and it is really remarkable how George keeps going for year after year, seeing that he was in a " National " winning team in 1904. The winner of the handicap race proved to be Mick Tween, with Peter Courtney close behind and Eddie Short just beating Len Adams for third place. items.s: R.W.A. JUNIOR FIVE MILES CHAMPIONSHIP—SEPTEMBER 29th Report of the R.W.A. junior five miles walk championship, where Belgrave did not close in a team and second-claim member Brian Shepherd was second. Although we had entered a team for this race, which is confined to the age group of 17-21, Gerry Warr unfortunately was unable to compete, thus leaving us with a bare three. Of these Michael Parks came under the judges ruling and was disqualified. Eric Hall finished in 15th position and George Beecham 24th, but we did not close in a team. It is hoped that some more youngsters will be recruited for this championship next year. Brian Shepherd, a second claim member, walked exceedingly well to finish 2nd to N. Read of Steyning A.C. items.s: SOUTHERN BRIGHTON ROAD RELAY Stage-by-stage report of the Southern Brighton Road Relay promoted by the "News of the World", won by Belgrave from Blackheath, with club records for Arthur Bruce, Ray Tooby and Len Herbert. This was the second race under the heading of " Southern " and it was a pity that the holders of the trophy, Thames Valley Harriers, saw fit not to enter a team for this year's contest. However, there was an entry of 20 clubs for this race promoted by the " News of the World " and although he protested, the ribboned baton was handed to our representative, Bill Lucas, at the start. At the first change-over it was carried, however, by the Blackheath runner Jack Braughton, who is second-claim to us, and Bill Lucas was in 4th place although his time of 29 min. 43 secs., compared well with previous times done by our runners on this rather long and difficult stage. Chas Walker ran a good race on the next stage to take us up into 2nd place and was only 1 second slower that Morley of Blackheath who were still in the lead. A change of lead then took place when the Aylesford man went in front to be followed by Archie Bedford with Blackheath now in third place. Arthur Bruce was our next runner and he did well to beat the previous club record for this stage although Blackheath had now taken the lead again with Aylesford lying third behind us. On the fifth stage Blackheath kept their lead and Les Stokell ran a dogged race to hang on to 2nd place and here again his time compared well with previous times recorded by our men, although nearly a minute slower than Charlie Smart's record breaking run for this " leg " last April. Ray Tooby was on the short sixth stage and he cut into Blackheath's lead and his time of 10 min. 35 secs., was also a new club record for this 2 miles run. On the long 7th stage we had Len Herbert and as we had expected, and also hoped, he overtook the Blackheath runner and gave us a lead of 25 seconds. Len's time of 30 min. 23 secs. beat the previous best club time by Tom Carter by three seconds. Len Adams and Eddie Short maintained our lead on the 8th and 9th stages, although the latter had a bad time near the end of his run and the Blackheath man was only 9 seconds behind at the change-over. On the last " leg " Jack Brown was really in form and he went right away from the rest of the field to give us our fifth win out of the last six races on the Brighton Road. His time of 17 min. 23 secs. was only three seconds behind Pat Parker's fine run in 1938, and was the fastest of the day beating Nankeville's time by 3 seconds. Result :—1, Belgrave H., 3.52.48; 2, Blackheath H., 3.54.30; 3, Polytechnic H., 3.56.36; 4, Reading A.C., 3.57.34; 5, Herne Hill H., 3.59.11; 6, Walton A.C., 3.59.56. items.s: WITH OUR ROAD MEN Round-up of Belgrave results in summer road races at the Kent County 20 miles, Ryde, Mitcham, Hadleigh, Watford, Swindon, the Peterborough Marathon and Oxted. We had some of our lads competing in the Kent County 20 Miles Road Race, which has an open team race in conjunction, and the placings and times were—14, A. Whitehead, 2.7.57; 26, A. Smith, 2.13.41; 30, A. Penstone, 2.15.26; Bert Jordan also started but retired at about 12 miles. We had a team go over to Ryde in the Isle of Wight for a 15 miles road race and they finished second to Mitcham A.C. in the team race. Positions of our men were—4, Tobin; 5, McDonald; 8, Stimpson; 10, Whitehead; 14, Penstone. In the Mitcham A.C. 15 miles open road race we had quite a good number of our members competing and B. L. Hudson was first man home for us in 11th position, which was quite a good performance. Other placings were—18, C. Abberton; 21, McDonald; 23, E. Stimpson; 25, Footer; 34, A. Smith; 37, A. Jordan; 39, F. Mitchell; 43, Penstone; 44, T. Mitchell. At Hadleigh on July 21st, Charlie Smart was first home in a 6 miles road race, and our team was second to Southend A.C. in the team race. Ted Stimpson was 8th, McDonald 12th, Tobin 13th, Footer 14th, and Bert Smith 18th. Then at Watford on the 28th July, Ted Stimpson was third in a 10 miles open event and was unlucky in the fact that although he was in the lead when they entered the sports ground, he lost two places in the final lap of the track due mainly to being almost out on his feet owing to the hot weather conditions. Dick Tobin was 4th, Bert Footer 6th and Bert Smith 7th. Ted Stimpson also ran a good race at Swindon in a 15 miles road race, when he finished second to A. A. Robertson, the International runner. With good support from McDonald and Tobin we took second team prizes to Reading A.C. Some of our lads also went to the Peterborough Marathon on August 6th, and the placings were—9, C. Abberton 2.50.59; 19, A. Penstone, 3.7.2; 25, A. Whitehead, 3.37.54. Team result was—1, Blackheath H., 18; 2, Belgrave H., 53; 3, Hull H. & A.C., 56. On the same day we had a team at Oxted in the 7 miles road handicap and they won the team event by finishing 4-5-6 to score 15 points as against the local club's 22, with Kent A.C. 26, and Mitcham A.C. 37. items.sum: Article urging Belgrave cross-country runners to train harder and build stamina for the coming season and the National.
items.s: " BELGRAVE FOR THE NATIONAL " Article urging Belgrave cross-country runners to train harder and build stamina for the coming season and the National. The cross-country season is now well advanced and we shall soon be holding the first of our club championships, which should give us an indication as to the strength of our teams for the coming " open " races. It is from this time that we must really get down to hard work, as the courses are becoming heavier with the winter rain, etc., and we can no longer depend on the speed we attained during the track season to carry us through. We must increase our distance and slowly build up additional stamina in order to cope with the harder courses and more rigorous conditions. It is now that the real cross-country runner shows his worth but unless he is prepared to train harder and more systematically he will find that his progress is impaired and that the more determined and stronger minded of his club-mates are leaving him behind. It is no easy matter to forsake the comfort of the fireside on a winter's evening, especially in these days of television, to put in a five or seven miles or even longer training run but to those who may feel like giving way to an evening in an armchair I would commend the thought that this is to be Belgrave's year and that every evening or Saturday wasted, may mean just that one place in a major event which would make the difference between victory or defeat. I want all club members, youths, juniors and seniors, to try to find time to put in at least one more training session each week, than you have done in previous years, and to pledge yourself to do all within your power to improve on your previous best placing in these major competitions. I know that we have sufficient promise in our younger members for them to win their respective championships, and also know that Micky Pyer has confidence in them to do this. When that feeling of apathy comes upon you and you cannot make up your mind whether to go out training or to turn up for that club fixture, please remember that without perfect team work we cannot expect to win races. No one man can take us to victory—it depends upon you all for even though you may not be in the scoring team you can still do your bit to help to peg back the opposition by backing up as close to the rest of the team as possible. The club officials will give you every encouragement in your quest for team selection and even if you do not make the grade this season, you are building up the stamina, speed and experience for forthcoming years. From now onwards I want you to have one slogan in mind " Belgrave for the National," and whether you are running in our team or giving vocal support, to have no doubts about the capabilities of the club to win this event, as we have done in the past. If any of you have any difficulties about your training or require information of any sort, how to placate the wife, etc., please see me and I will endeavour to put you on the right track. A word in the right direction may clear up your troubles and assist you with your training methods. In conclusion, I would impress upon all members the necessity for attending all club fixtures, both home and away. They are designed to help you to reach a peak of fitness at the right time and are spaced at intervals so that no harm can be done by over-racing. Don't leave it to only a few members to keep the club to the fore, remember our slogan and give your utmost support to the club at all times. BILL LUCAS (C.C. Captain). Bill Lucas BILL LUCAS C.C. items.s: THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW Club notices: rebuilding Belgrave Hall, club clothing for sale, the Boxing Day meeting, a social dance, Alf Harley and Ernie Duffett elected presidents, fixture cards and the Children's Party. Belgrave Hall The new " House " Sub-Committee again crave your indulgence for conditions prevailing at the Hall. Every effort is being made to obtain the necessary licences for rebuilding. We ask, therefore, that you bear with us and hope that by the winter season of 1952 we will have reached at least part of our objective, i.e., completely rebuilding the hall. Meanwhile your committee are willing to discuss any suggestions offered by you to improve the amenities at Wimbledon. Come now, don't keep your grumbles to yourselves, let us share in them. In this way we hope to be able to please everybody. I would ask all members to make full use of the telephone now installed in the outside lobby. The charge is now 3d. and the number WIM. 6857. TOM MORRELL, Hon. Sec., House Sub-Committee. Clothing Section I would like to bring to your notice a marked decline in the sale of club clothing. This is very much in evidence at Club meetings both on the track and over the country. I always regard it as an honour to wear the club colours and do so on every possible occasion. Imagine my amazement when a few weeks ago at Wimbledon, a member asked " Where did you get that tie? " Well, when I got up, I told him in no uncertain manner that club ties, unique in colour and design are 10/6 each and real value for money. They can be worn with any style of suiting and can be purchased from me. Look around the hall any Saturday and what do you see? You don't know? Then I will tell you. The strangest collection of vests ever worn by a bunch of athletes. Let's get together and put this matter right. Club vests can be obtained from me in YOUR SIZE. Chest measurements 34-36-38 and 40. Badges for vests and track suits are 2/6 each. Two further articles of club wear are metal badges, 2/- each, and sets of letters for track suits at 5/6 per set. I am now operating payment cards for any member wishing to use them. These will be treated in strict confidence and I hope you will not hesitate to take advantage of the facilities offered. The only stipulation is that the goods cannot be delivered until payment is complete. Any of the above mentioned articles can be had direct from me, by post if necessary, providing you enclose the extra for postage. T. MORRELL (Asst. Hon. Treasurer), 3, Florian Road, Putney, S.W.15. Boxing Day Meeting This traditional meeting of ours will be held as usual this year. This meeting is unique for the attraction it holds for both old and young and some of our very old and enthusiastic members. So if you wish to renew old friendships, come along and, in addition, enjoy some good racing. Social Our new Social Hon. Secretary Jack Lacey has arranged a Dance at the Chenil Galleries, Chelsea, on Saturday, January 12th, 1952. Tickets 3/6 each. Come along and support this Dance and your hard working Social Secretary—and bring your OWN girl friend. We are pleased to report that our President, Alf Harley, has been elected President of the R.W.A. for the current year. We know Alf will be a worthy addition to the famous names which have previously graced this office. At the A.G.M. of the South of Thames C.C.A. Ernie Duffett was elected President for the current year and so follows in the path of two former Belgrave Presidents, Harry Hare and the late Harry Parker. Fixture Cards HAVE YOU GOT YOURS?—The treasurer has already explained to you the new system of issuing gummed receipts. There are hundreds of books waiting to be sent out. The quickest way to get yours is to send your subs into the Treasurer straight away and in return you will receive a new handbook complete with receipt on the back. If you are fortunate enough to have got your handbook without paying your subs, remember that it is not complete WITHOUT THAT RECEIPT. So—PAY UP—LICK UP—AND STICK UP. Children's Party The Children's Party will again be held at Belgrave Hall on Sunday, December 30th. Donations towards the cost of the Party should be sent to J. A. Lacey. Tom Morrell TOM MORRELL Hon. items.sum: Club news column: walking and running successes, members abroad and in hospital, the "News of the World" plinth presented to Belgrave, and family news.
items.s: Here and There Club news column: walking and running successes, members abroad and in hospital, the "News of the World" plinth presented to Belgrave, and family news. Those members who knew the late Bob Martin, one of our foremost distance walkers will be pleased to hear that his daughter Sheila is following in his footsteps and on November 3rd was 2nd in the Women's 2 miles National Junior Championship at Regents Park. On July 21st Geoff. Gregory won the Amesbury Carnival 2 miles handicap in 14.33.2. On August 18th Bert Clayton was 2nd in the Old Basing 2 miles Open Handicap. Congratulations to Alan Sexton on his brilliant running in Rome for British Services in International Events and more recently his successes in Cambridge University Freshmen's Sports. We hope and expect him to gain his " blue " in a few months time and we hope his studies will permit him to turn out for us in the more important inter-club and other meetings of the year. Teddy Gordon sends best wishes to all members. We regret to report the illness of Oscar Horwood and we send wishes for a speedy recovery and assure him we do still remember his wonderful work for the Club thirty years ago. An interesting and pleasing presentation was made at the finish of the recent Southern London to Brighton road relay when the " News of the World " very kindly presented to the " Bels," the plinth of the old Gold Cup, which is now awarded for the " National " event. On this plinth are the names of such famous clubs as Birchfield H. (5 times), Hallamshire H. (twice), Salford H. (twice), Mitcham A.C. (3 times), while Belgrave appears on it 6 times. It was for this latter reason that the " News of the World " decided to hand us the plinth for safe keeping and we shall treasure it with the respect it deserves. We are glad to know that Bob Duffett, the son of our Running Hon. Secretary has now fully recovered from his flying accident, when he and a friend crashed in an " Auster " 'plane, while on a trip to Amsterdam to see his parents, who were over there on holiday. We were pleased to hear from Brian Rice, one of our promising junior members, who is now with the Training Battalion R.A.S.C. and he says that he hopes to be able to turn out for the club during the present cross-country season. At our Club Dinner we were pleased to see " Splinter " Tranter now home from Singapore, and hope that we shall see him turning out on the track next season. Congratulations to Les Stokell and Mrs. Stokell on the birth of a daughter and if we get many more female additions to the club strength, we shall have to consider starting a ladies' section, shades of Footer! Jack Shotter, Captain in the Regular Army, is now in Middle East and sends best wishes to all his friends at " Belgrave Hall." items.sum: Editorial mourning the deaths of vice-president Joe Turner and club auditor Jimmy Bellchamber.
items.s: Editorial Editorial mourning the deaths of vice-president Joe Turner and club auditor Jimmy Bellchamber. Dear Fellow Belgravians, It is with a note of sadness that we open the pages of this issue of the Belgravian. Two English gentlemen and true Sportsmen have gone from us and we mourn their passing deeply. Joe Turner, a Vice President and lifelong friend of our club, a wise counsellor to all participating in athletics, an enthusiastic and extremely efficient official, and our own dear Jimmy Bellchambei who was all that a Belgravian should be and in fact the originator of the word "Belgravian." Our President, Alf Harley writes an obituary on both our dear departed friends. Whilst our sorrow is manifest, it must also be borne in mind that we have lost two very valuable officials. Their places in athletics will be hard to fill, but those to whom they pass the torch, by reason of the splendid and unselfish example they both showed, must fill these places, and so on to perpetuity. Adieu—Joe Turner and Jimmy Bellchamber. YOUR EDITORS. items.s: J. B. Bellchamber Obituary of Jimmy Bellchamber, club member from 1911/12 and Hon. Auditor for forty years, who died on 28 February 1952 aged 66. February 28th, 1952, was a very sad day indeed for it brought news of the death of Jimmy Bellchamber at the age of 66 years, following a three months' illness which had been bravely borne with typical fortitude. Our sympathetic condolences are extended to Mrs. Bellchamber and her three sons. A number of Jimmy's club mates and friends in Walking and Athletics attended the Requiem Mass and funeral on March 5th, paying their final tribute to one they were proud to have known. To have been honoured by his friendship during his life time, as have so many of us, is something positive we shall remember with pleasure all our lives. We mourn his passing—we honour his memory. Jimmy came to the Club in 1911/12 as a runner and the late Bob Ricketts quickly noted his abilities and loyalty to the Club and invited him to become our honorary auditor, for finances in those days, although small, needed expert supervision, and Jimmy has told us with a smile on many an occasion of how the balance in hand at the 1912 audit was 11/5d. and of its gradual increase throughout the years (always with Jimmy as the Hon. Auditor—forty years of real service) until the club's assets are now well within measurable reach of £10,000. An accountant by profession, Jimmy's sound knowledge and able guidance was always of the greatest help and a very great debt of gratitude is owed to him. His outstanding services to the club were recognised by the conferment of Life Membership many years ago, and in 1931/32 he became President. In earlier years he had been a Club Captain and Vice Captain and we have known him in recent years as a first class sprint and walking judge, and absolutely dependable in all he undertook on behalf of the club. He will always be remembered for his personal influence and leadership in building up the walking side of the club to the grand position it now occupies. In the 1912 era we had a few walkers but the prevailing idea then was that seven miles was just about the limit if a man wished to retain his speed. Jimmy had very different thoughts and set about demonstrating his own ideas and building up that basis of solid team work which is part of the inheritance we owe so largely to him. After a training walk one evening with Bob Ricketts (who in his time was sprinter, middle distance runner, boxer and walker—all with some distinction), from the Flood Street, Chelsea, quarters of the club, it was decided that Jimmy should henceforth remain a walker and that every endeavour should be made to build up a team. This was done to some purpose and the club began to show up well and in a Junior League Competition finished: unplaced, 3rd, 2nd and 1st in the four races held. During the summer of 1914, Jimmy began training for the Brighton Walk, but the outbreak of war in August, 1914, put paid to his ideas—temporarily at all events. In 1919 Bob Ricketts, Harry Evans, Bill Hawker and Jimmy were quickly together again and were soon reinforced by further strength. In fact Belgrave accounted for every scratch team race held in the Metropolitan area during the season 1919/20 and in the 1919 A.A.A. Championship our 6th man finished 13th or 14th and one of our best, W. J. Hawker, did not start. In 1920 the R.W.A. Junior Championship was won with a team of four post-war members and the foundations laid for the many successes that have since followed. So the Bellchamber influence and example was at work—and so it continued for many years. In the spring of 1914, Jimmy had been the first Belgrave walker to attain first-class standard (then 3 hrs. 10 mins.) in the R.W.A. 20 miles Championship. In 1920 he was placed third in the A.A.A. 7 miles Championship—the first Belgravian to do so in modern times. In 1921 he was the first Belgravian to beat the present R.W.A. First Class Standard at 20 miles and Captain of the first Club team ever to finish in a 20 miles Championship. He was the first Belgrave Harrier to be placed in the Brighton Walk and the first Club man to beat 9 hours for the journey. He was the first Belgrave Walker to do the double journey and become a Centurion. All these actual performances have been surpassed by Club members subsequently, but the force of Jimmy's great personal example will always live on. He had to break down the prejudice that racing at 10 miles and over was inimical to track speed; he had to inculcate the ideas of team work, for individual effort was the greatest motivating force at one time. But these things he did and great was the victory and the record books bear testimony to his work through the many championship and Brighton Walk team wins and placings since 1920. Jimmy was the first winner (in 1923) of the Sussex 10 miles Championship. In September, 1920, he was third in the Brighton Walk and followed up this grand performance in the years that followed in this manner: Sept., 1922—4th; May, 1923—4th; Sept., 1923—5th; Sept., 1924—4th. No wonder that we have built up a great tradition in the Brighton Walks and have recorded more team wins than any other club. In 1921 Jimmy did not compete in the Brighton Walk, having concentrated on the London to Brighton and back (104 miles) in which he finished second. This was an outstanding performance, for the day journey took place in one of the highest temperatures ever recorded in this country, and by contrast the night had been extremely cold. Bellchamber as a Walking Judge and as a man commanded the greatest respect and he had officiated at hundreds of races including the Olympic Games, A.A.A. and R.W.A. Championships, Area and County Championships, etc., always competently, conscientiously and with credit to the Club and himself. Perhaps it was as a moral force—as the personification of the innate good things in life on the spiritual plane that those of us who were close to Jimmy will best remember him. We shall recall his unassuming, dignified, friendly approach combined with intense loyalty, strength of character and an ever present desire to help. And always we shall remember his devotion to Belgrave, his work through forty years to enhance the position and reputation, his dependability, his love for his Club and his fellow members. Jimmy has delighted many of us with his articles and pen sketches of Club personalities in the Belgravian, and the Belgrave News Letter. In doing so he greatly enriched our knowledge and also revealed himself to us. As a native of Sussex (his name comes from the same derivation as BALCOMBE, and probably indicated Norman ancestry) he was never happier than when he was within its borders, although disgusted with "London by the Sea" and the injury the town had wreaked on some parts of his beloved county. He had read widely and his articles were bespattered with appropriate quotations and with some finely expressed sentiments of his own. This he writes of a stroll to Brighton: "Sunrise and the immaculate hours have the same indescribable charm that was theirs in a younger and fresher world. Right before us Wolstenbury still pushes up an enormous head from out a sea of clinging mist just as he did when Roman Legionaries were encamped upon his brow; whilst away in the west we see the sun's long fingers playing lovingly with the dark tresses of Chanctonbury's curl crowned head before that giant has wakened and pushed aside his pearly coverlet. Eastwards Ditchling Beacon greets us with a face bathed in smiles. Surely there is recognition in his warm Sussex Welcome." How contemptuous he was of "The sacrifices the modern Moloch demands." Let us re-read his verses:— THE BYE-PASS Now the motor horn hoots where the nightingale sang, And a petrol pump stands where his low notes out rang From the delicate twigs of his glorified perch, When the soft June morn gleamed on the silvery birch. And a stark straight road runs where thick low leaves amid And emitting faint fragrance, the violets hid Whilst the multiformed beauty of lichened oak boles Is replaced by the sameness of telegraph poles. And the meadow where buttercups mirrored the stars Is now open all night as a garage for cars, Whilst there's jazz for the jaded and tea for the dry In a spic and span jerry-built bungalow by. And the poppies' red flame no more grows on the seas Of the billowing wheat overswept by the breeze. Gone the use and the beauty! whilst ignorant pride Crashes over the land on a juggernaut ride. And the chattering streamlet that winded and strayed Between banks blossom jewelled when springtime displayed Its pale primroses, windflowers and daffodils gay, Through a pipe neath the road is now making its way. Yes, where sometimes was seen like a flash of blue light That the eye could scarce follow, a kingfisher's flight, Blatant road hogs rush past with their poisonous smell, Changing England's fair garden from Eden to hell. We have indeed lost a great Belgravian. Whilst lying in hospital he told the writer that although a member of the Club for forty years he had never realised until that time everything the Club had meant to him and the number of friends he had within its ranks. Their letters and calls helped him tremendously and he was extremely grateful. Much more could be written of this great friend of ours and his influence and example will help us in the years that follow. If we can be but loyal to the ideals that were his, we need have no fears for the Club he loved so well, nor for ourselves. R.I.P. A.A.H. J. B. Bellchamber J. B. items.sum: Obituary of Joe Turner, Belgrave vice-president and honorary timekeeper, a respected official for over sixty years.
items.s: J. Turner Obituary of Joe Turner, Belgrave vice-president and honorary timekeeper, a respected official for over sixty years. We also mourn the passing of Joe Turner, a Vice-President and Honorary Timekeeper for many years past. Joe's unassuming and unaffected personality had endeared him to us all. His reputation as a first-class timekeeper was known wherever athletics was enjoyed and he had officiated at all the principal track, cross-country and walking championships and at record attempts by the shoal. But delightfully, he also found pleasure in working at the humble school or inter-club meetings. In over sixty years of athletics he had never let anyone down. If Joe said (sometimes twelve months before) that he would come along to a particular meeting, he did so. He was absolutely dependable. He did not just mix with his fellow officials, but was approachable by everyone, known to everyone. He was a familiar figure at Belgrave Hall and at our track meetings and we are going to miss him tremendously. We can ill afford to lose such stalwarts as Joe—a grand sportsman and friend, a great worker for Belgrave as well as athletics generally, and a man we've been proud to know for so long. J. Turner J. items.sum: Congratulations to Frank M. Stone, Metropolitan policeman and former Belgrave distance walker, on his award of the George Medal.
items.s: F. M. Stone Congratulations to Frank M. Stone, Metropolitan policeman and former Belgrave distance walker, on his award of the George Medal. Following upon the article published in our last issue, our very sincere congratulations are extended to Frank M. Stone (also known as Mark and Rodney) on the recent award of the "George" Medal. He is undoubtedly the bravest Metropolitan policeman ever, and has received (at the hands of three monarchs) the King's Police Medal (the Police V.C.), the British Empire Medal, and now the "George" Medal—all awarded for gallantry; in addition to which he has received the Royal Humane Society's Medal for saving life. Many years ago Frank was a member of our distance walking teams and in the London to Brighton Walk of 1921 finished 12th and won the open handicap then held in conjunction. He has helped considerably in the matter of raising Club finances in days gone by and his visits to training quarters were always very welcome and of the cheeriest nature. He has always been very versatile in sport with interests in boxing, wrestling (he served on the Council of the A.W.A. for several years), Soccer, Rugby football, etc., etc., whilst Belgrave has always meant a great deal to him. We are very proud of his achievements and look forward to seeing him at our gatherings as of yore, now that injuries sustained in the incident which led to the recent award have compelled his retirement from the Police Force. F. M. Stone F. M. STONE awarded the George Medal Frank M. Stone Frank M. items.sum: News of sick members and others, including Jack Shields' recovery from polio and his message of thanks.
items.s: Our Invalids News of sick members and others, including Jack Shields' recovery from polio and his message of thanks. We are pleased to learn that Oscar Horwood is a little better. We hope the coming fine weather will help him on a bit more. All Belgravians are thinking kindly of him. Jack Shields, who has been suffering from polio for many weeks, and has lived during that time in an iron lung, is now improving. Many Belgravians have already visited him at Grove Hospital, Tooting, and he will be pleased to see any of his Club mates to help him along his uphill fight towards full recovery. However, Jack is so much improved that he had sent us a message which he would like to be published in the Belgravian, and here it is:— "I wonder whether you could find space in the Belgravian to put in a word of thanks to all the members who have been so kind to me by visits, letters, messages and enquiries, to say nothing of all the gifts, both individual and those which Tom Carter has brought on behalf of others. I have been greatly heartened by all this kind consideration. Please thank everyone. Jack Shields." Albert Macher, who was recently in hospital, is now well and out again. Of other people's invalids. We are very happy to report that Charlie Smith, the well-known official and member of Thames Valley Harriers, is progressing favourably in hospital. Derek Pugh, the international quarter-miler, who was also stricken with polio, is very much better. It is interesting to note that Derek has been under the treatment of our own Dr. E. M. McKenzie. items.sum: Report of Finance Sub-Committee proposals to raise programme prices, club event entry fees and probably subscriptions.
items.s: The Belgrave Budget Report of Finance Sub-Committee proposals to raise programme prices, club event entry fees and probably subscriptions. The Finance Sub-Committee, at a recent meeting, made proposals which were subsequently endorsed by the full Club Committee. These proposals are designed to bring our income closer to our expenditure and, in view of general price increases over the past few years, they cannot be regarded as severe. The charge for programmes at our meetings is to be increased from 3d. to 4d. Our printed programmes have been very much admired by people outside the Club and it is our policy to continue with them. If every programme could be sold at each meeting it would go a long way towards reducing the loss on programmes which we report each year. Anyone who can help to sell programmes at meetings will be welcome. Now that we are going back to Battersea Park for some of our meetings we think of the days before the war when spectators had to get there early before the programmes were all sold. The next item will affect active members. As from 1st January the entry fees for Club events for Seniors will be 1s. 6d. for the first event and 1s. for each additional event per meeting. Juniors and Youths will pay 1s. per event as previously. Cross-country and Road Walking events will remain at 1s. Last year's Balance Sheet showed that entry fees were well below the cost of handicap prizes alone, not to mention Championship and Standard medals. I have no doubt that the Section Hon. Secretaries will be exhorting you to give greater support to Club handicaps, so I'll leave it to them. The next item concerns subscriptions. It is agreed that our income from subscriptions is not big enough to meet our increasing expenditure and it is probable that subscriptions will have to be raised. This will be considered at a future meeting when new rates will be suggested. Once again I must thank the many who have written to me regarding their subscriptions, particularly those in the Forces. We hope that members in the Forces have been receiving Club literature and are getting opportunities for training. Many have given their demob. dates; these have been noted and we hope to welcome them back to the Club life in due course. Some lucky ones are doing their service locally and we see them often. Others are far afield and send their best wishes to the Club. They can rest assured that we often think of them and wish them the best of luck. ONE LAST REMINDER—HAVE YOU PAID YOUR SUBS? If not, why not? G. S. DOUBLEDAY. G. S. Doubleday G. S. DOUBLEDAY Hon. Treasurer Battersea Park

items.sum: Report of Belgrave retaining the Sidney Taylor Memorial Trophy in the Chelmsford road relay in a course record 94 mins. 43 secs., with leg times and team result.
items.s: Chelmsford Road Relay Race Report of Belgrave retaining the Sidney Taylor Memorial Trophy in the Chelmsford road relay in a course record 94 mins. 43 secs., with leg times and team result. This was held on October 27th and we retained our hold on the "Sidney Taylor Memorial Trophy" in no uncertain manner. Our time of 94 mins. 43 secs. was a new course record and we won quite comfortably from the Aylesford Paper Mills with Essex Beagles in third place. Chas Walker, although suffering from the after-effects of a cold, ran a good first "leg" which was inside the previous lap record time, held by Bill Lucas, but even so could only hand over in second place to Cook, of Hadleigh A.C. Archie Bedford, however, soon caught the leader and from then on we were always out in front. Len Adams kept up the good work and increased our lead and Bill Lucas took us further ahead to hand over to Mike Stearman 68 secs. to the good. Mike ran steadily and well and lost only a few seconds, despite being chased by Reg Robins of Essex Beagles, an experienced performer. Len Herbert was on the final relay and he took no chances as Sando of Aylesford, was running the last "leg" for the Paper Mills, who had been having a battle-royal with Essex Beagles. Incidentally, Jim Peters of Essex Beagles, the A.A.A. Marathon champion set up a new course record of 15 mins. 22 secs., which was 13 seconds inside the old figures set up by Bill Lucas in last year's race. Our team's individual times were—Walker, 15.33; Bedford, 15.46; Adams, 15.53; Lucas, 15.46; Stearman, 16.10; Herbert, 15.35. items.s: Club 5 Miles C.C. Handicap Report and full placings of the club 5 miles cross-country handicap at Wimbledon on 27 October, won outright by Ray Tooby, with Courtney winning the handicap. At Wimbledon on October 27th we had some of the Mitcham A.C. lads together with members of the Veterans A.C. as visitors to our quarters. The scratch race was won in easy fashion by Ray Tooby, and his time was quite good for our 5 miles' course. He was followed home by Eddie Short and "Ginger" Newell with Hudson and Peter Courtney also running well. Courtney won the handicap held in conjunction, with Hudson and A. Housego in third place. There was quite a tussle for the minor placings with a few seconds separating the first half dozen, but the winner was away out in front and definitely caught the handicapper "napping." We had a 10 aside match with Mitcham A.C. but as they only had one man in the first 12 home, we scored a hollow win by 60 points against 150. The Vets A.C. also held a handicap in conjunction with our race and this was won by our old friend Bert Footer who is still going strong although in his 29th season with the club. items.s: South of Thames "Junior" Race Report of the South of Thames junior cross-country race at Farningham on 10 November, won by Herne Hill, with placings of Belgrave's five teams. A record entry of 54 teams for the South of Thames "Junior" race held at Farningham on November 10th, and a field of 317 runners faced the starter. The course was very heavy after recent rain and included quite a bit of plough and in the words of one competitor, it had "everything." At the end of the first lap Don MacL[illegible]an was our first man with the others quite a long way back and already the Herne Hill lads seemed comfortable winners of the team race. "Ginger" Newell and Mick Porter came through well on the second lap with Maclean dropping back a bit and Hudson and Mike Stearman were too far back for us to stand a chance of getting placed. Peter Courtney ran quite well in his first senior race, for although this is known as a Junior event, the word junior applies to ability and not to age. We had entered five teams as we believe in giving all our members a chance of representing the club in open competition, and as they all closed in, it was evident that our policy was justified. items.s: Enfield A.C. 7 Miles Open, 10-11-51 Report and placings of the Enfield A.C. 7 miles open walk on 10 November 1951, won by Barrett from Gerry Gregory, with Belgrave "A" winning the scratch team; the text puts Jack Rutland 26th but the table prints 21 J. Rutland. Enfield A.C. reverted to their old course for their Open this year and once again we had a very big entry. Gerry Gregory took an early lead on the uphill climb over the first mile and gradually increased it on the outward journey being followed by Barrett and Harry Churcher. Barrett, however, made a great effort on the return journey and succeeded in catching Gregory at about 5½ miles and gaining a 10 yards' lead. Over the last mile Gerry tried hard to close the gap but Barrett held on and won by the narrow margin of 8 yards. With Harry Churcher 3rd and Dave McMullen 4th we had another scratch team win despite the fact that we lost George Checkley who was well up at about 3 miles and had to wait until 26th position was filled by Jack Rutland. Although Charlie Churcher finished 19th, he was walking in the "B" team which did well to finish 6th. items.s: Belgrave Harriers Open 7 Miles, Wimbledon, 24-11-51 Report and placings of Belgrave's own open 7 miles walk at Wimbledon, won by Harry Churcher, with Belgrave regaining the Berman Trophy and the "C" team winning the team handicap. For the first time for four years we were favoured with fine weather for our own big race of the season. Following the advice that latecomers would not be waited for, almost everyone turned up early and the race was off to a sharp start at 3 p.m. and it was obvious that Harry Churcher was out to show them the way round over the home course. At the halfway stage, Barrett, winner of the two previous opens, was lying third and was never able to make up any leeway. Once again we had our first scoring three in the first five and with Charlie Churcher back in the "A" Team, 10th making our fourth man, we thus regained possession of the Berman Trophy, winning by the wide margin of 15 points. Although none of our walkers figured in the individual handicap, our "C" team completed the team double by winning the team handicap race, less than one minute separating the first three teams. Our thanks are once again due to the generous support given to the prize fund and also to the band of helpers, particularly the recorders whose excellent work enabled us to have the result completed in what must have been record time. items.s: ROCHESTER ROAD RACE Belgrave were second in the team race of the Rochester Road Race, with Vern Blowfield returning to the club's colours. On November 24th this annual race was well supported. This time we sent down a team and had the satisfaction of securing second place. We were pleased to see Vern Blowfield once more appearing in our colours, and although he seemed rather short of training we are sure he will soon get back to the form which gained him second place in the English cross-country championship in 1948 at Sheffield. Our first man to finish was John Bromley 5th, then came Archie Bedford 9th, Len Adams 12th with Vern Blowfield 21st. items.sum: Report and results of the club's Boxing Day track meeting at Battersea Park, including the "Grandfathers" sprint won by George Still in his 74th year.
items.s: CLUB BOXING DAY MEETING Report and results of the club's Boxing Day track meeting at Battersea Park, including the "Grandfathers" sprint won by George Still in his 74th year. Our annual track meeting on Boxing Day morning was held this year at Battersea Park, so reverting to our pre-war custom of holding meetings at this track. It has now been re-laid into a 4 lap affair as against the old 3 lap track which many of our older members will no doubt remember so well. The meeting commenced with the heats of the club 120 yds. sprint handicap and Denis Merrett ran well to win the first heat off the scratch mark. Alan Sexton was also present but was unable to get up off 1 yard in a slightly faster run heat. One of the high-lights of the meeting, which attracted a good crowd, was the " Grandfathers " sprint over 100 yards, and the winner was none other than our old friend George Still now in his 74th year. The winner of the 3 miles' walk was young G. Beecham and he walked very well to beat E. A. Smith with R. Ferguson third. A large field turned out for the 2 miles' run and Ray Tooby ran well off a back mark to thread his way through to gain third place. Alan Bishop put in a fast finish to beat E. T. Paterson for first place and Jack Brown was another to finish well up. The Shot Putt handicap was won by Les Stokell who is now taking up field events, he has ideas about becoming a decathion performer, and he certainly did well to take first place in the handicap with Frank Kemp second and a new member in R. J. Harris third. Full results are given below:— " Grandfathers " race—1, G. Still (30); 2, E. Glover (9); 3, R. W. Best (15). Time: 11.8 secs. 120 Yards—1, P. Cornish (8); 2, J. Benstead (7); 3, G. items.sum: Report of the Surrey County cross-country championships at Oxted, where Belgrave retained the "Pickett" Cup with a record 37 points, plus Belgrave runners for Cadogan A.C. in the Middlesex Championships at Trent Park.
items.s: THE COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the Surrey County cross-country championships at Oxted, where Belgrave retained the "Pickett" Cup with a record 37 points, plus Belgrave runners for Cadogan A.C. in the Middlesex Championships at Trent Park. The Surrey County Senior and Junior events were held at Oxted but although the locals had done their best as regards arrangements, it was a far from satisfactory venue. This was mainly due to the fact that the start of the race was some distance from the finish, and in consequence all the runners' track suits, sweaters, etc., had to be carried from one place to another. Also the course was laid out in such a manner that the spectators saw practically nothing of the actual race apart from the start and finish. In the Junior event our first man home was Don Maclean in 6th place and Peter Courtney also ran well to finish 14th. Mike Stearman was unlucky in the fact that owing to arriving a bit late he missed the start and trailed the field along and so can be said to have done well to finish 41st out of the 63 who completed the course. Our seniors made no mistake in retaining the " Pickett " Cup for the senior championship and actually set up a new record by scoring only 37 points for our six counters. Chas. Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A. Cockram 5th in the Wilts. championship, will also be running in this event and this must be almost a record for any club to have seven representatives in such a race. In the Middlesex Championships at Trent Park, our lads who were running for Cadogan A.C. did not do too well, although " Ginger " Newell ran his best race to date in finishing 16th in the senior race. Vern Blowfield was 25th, Tony Snoad 26th, Bob Taylor 37th, Ken Stimpson 50th and Ted Stimpson 53rd. Others to finish were—Steve Charlton 54th, J. MacDonald 89th, A. Housego 94th, A. W. Saville 111th and Bert Smith 121st. items.s: METROPOLITAN POLICE OPEN, 12-1-52 Report and Belgrave placings from the Metropolitan Police Open at Imber Court, won by Surrey A.C., with George Beecham taking the individual handicap and Belgrave "C" the team handicap. The absence of Dave McMullen and Gerry Gregory no doubt accounted for Surrey A.C.'s first scratch team win for many years, and with Paddy Woods narrowly beating Harry Churcher for individual honours, the Surrey boys are to be congratulated on their dual win. As will be seen from the times it was generally a very fast race, our own walkers being no exception. George Beecham is to be heartily congratulated on his excellent performance which gave him the individual handicap. A bigger surprise awaited George when he received his prize later in the evening at the Club Dance (having left Imber Court before the awards were presented). Rumour has it that he thought it was an infernal machine which might blow up any minute, but was eventually convinced that it was in fact a pressure cooker. Following our recent successes in team handicaps, the resulting win for our " C " team was further proof of our lads' performances. items.s: EALING YOUTH CROSS-COUNTRY RACE Northolt Youth Centre, made up mainly of Belgrave Harriers, won the Ealing Youths Cross-Country Race again, led home by John Smith. For the second year in succession Northolt Youth Centre, whose team consists mainly of Belgrave Harriers, won the Ealing Youths Cross-Country Race and once again in no uncertain manner. The first man home was John Smith of Northolt and Belgrave. John is a very versatile athlete and has without a doubt a very promising future. Adept at high and long jumping and 220 yards, he now turns temporarily to cross-country and literally " cake walks " the race. M. Kirkby, another Northolt Belgravian was 3rd. Final result shows that Northolt finished 5 men in the first six places and most of them wearing Belgrave colours. Why don't some of our coaches pay Northolt a visit? Reported by F. H. items.s: JUNIOR C.C. MATCH A Belgrave youths' team beat the Oxford and Bermondsey Club in the junior cross-country match, Geoff Goode, Frank Wright and G. Lines finishing together. This was against the Oxford and Bermondsey Club on January 19th and owing to the fact that our visitors were late in arriving, it was actually a Youths' team that we fielded. Geoff Goode, Frank Wright and G. Lines came home together in first place followed by V. Baker of O. and B., then came K. C. Whitaker and the rest of the Bermondsey boys. The question of altering the course is now being seriously considered and it is hoped that we shall be able to avoid any such mishap in the future. items.s: "MACHER" SHIELD RACE Report and full result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship for the "Macher" Shield, won by J. W. Brown, with a triple dead-heat in the sealed handicap and a team race against Cadogan A.C. The club 10 miles cross-country championship was held on January 26th and the race was started by Albert Macher, who we were pleased to see out and about once again. A good field of 38 runners faced the starter on a snow covered course of two laps, and at the half-distance Charlie Walker was out in front being about 60 yards ahead of Bill Lucas and Jack Brown who were together. Next came Vern Blowfield, making a welcome re-appearance together with Eddie Short who was finding the going a bit too hard for him, as I think he prefers more muddy conditions. When they came in sight of the finish, Jack Brown was well ahead and he must have made up a good bit of ground over the second lap. Bill Lucas still retained third place and the other placings had not altered much, and for our first eight men to finish within 4 minutes is I think a good sign for the more serious races to come. Len Herbert was obviously short of training and we were pleased to see his brother Eric coming back to the form which gained him a place in our Southern team last season. Alan Bishop ran very well but he often does better over our own course than he does on a course where the going is more difficult. Incidentally, there was a triple dead-heat for first place in the sealed handicap and this is the first time we can remember such a happening in a club race. items.sum: Report of the Garnet Cup 10-mile walk at Sheffield, where many walkers were disqualified and Belgrave finished fourth by one point as Sheffield won the cup for the 8th time.
items.s: GARNET CUP RACE, 2nd FEBRUARY, 1952 Report of the Garnet Cup 10-mile walk at Sheffield, where many walkers were disqualified and Belgrave finished fourth by one point as Sheffield won the cup for the 8th time. Sporting columnists seeking sensational copy would have headed their reports of the Garnet Cup Race at Sheffield:— " The debacle at Sheffield—were the judges too hard?" 106 walkers, comprising sixteen teams, started this ten mile race on a good day over a two lap course that appeared to be reasonable. Only 76 walkers finished with Surrey W.C. the only club finishing a complete team of 8. Sheffield had 9 men pulled with their " A " Team reduced to 4, their " B " Team to 3. Three clubs failed to finish a team of 4 and like the rest we suffered too. Immediately, from a fast start, Paddy Woods took the lead, surrounded by five members of the Sheffield team, obviously meaning business in the team race, but soon after the first mile post was passed two Sheffield lads were " pulled " and five of their men were out in the first four miles. But what happened to the " Bels "? Early in the race, Syd Jarlett, although suffering from a very heavy cold was leading our team in the 12th position. Then came Ron Kemp closely followed by five others with Alan Robins starting steadily in the rear. A quick check at 5 miles showed leading teams to be 1, Sheffield 32; 2, Highgate 47; 3, Met. W.C. 53; 4, Belgrave 78. Already we had suffered our first reverse. Gerry Warr had been pulled 50 yards short of the 5 mile post. The team were informed quickly, but worse was to follow when Tony Bellchamber was pulled at 5½ miles. Then the whips came out and the lads were pushed on. Syd was still leading with Ron Kemp, Ted Smith and the two Georges (Checkley and Beecham) working their way forward. At 6¼ miles George West (Highgate) then in 16th position was pulled, a sorry blow to them. Team positions at this point shows:—Sheffield 35, Met. W.C. 48, Highgate 62, Belgrave 73, and the fight was really on. Our lads, urged forward by Charlie Churcher and the " horrible handicapper " (yes, he was watching form) now made their big effort and at 9 miles team points were Sheffield 41, Met. W.C. 51, Highgate 60, Belgrave 63,—showed that anything could happen. Nobly our lads responded to our urging, Sid Jarlet (what a race he walked) found a little more effort and pulled up two places. Ron Kemp (walking above form) went up three more and George Beecham hung on to George Checkley in a final grand effort to give us a placed team. But all in vain, we were beaten into 4th place by one point. 1, Sheffield U.H. 42; 2, Met. W.C. 48; 3, Highgate H. 56; 4, Belgrave 57. Finally congratulations to Sheffield on winning the Garnet Cup for the 8th time, and so beating our record of 7 wins. Junior Walkers!! We shall have to put this right next year. 1 W. Woods 79.41 3 B. items.sum: Belgrave youths won the Aylesbury Youths' Road Relay, cutting over 4 minutes off the previous winning time.
items.s: AYLESBURY YOUTHS' ROAD RELAY Belgrave youths won the Aylesbury Youths' Road Relay, cutting over 4 minutes off the previous winning time. On February 2nd our team not only won the race but knocked over 4 minutes off the previous winning time. Geoff Goode ran the first stage of about 3 miles in 18.15 and gave us a good lead from Highgate, Wycombe & Finchley H. Gerry Lines was our next runner and he kept the lead and did 18.54, with Ron Linstead going next and he clocked 19 mins. dead and we were still ahead of Wycombe, Highgate and Finchley. Frank Wright our fourth and last runner did 18.22 to come home an easy winner and our total time was 74.31. We also started a " B " team and after the following had run—J. Hills 19.33 (9th), P. F. Hayden 20.36 (10th) and C. W. Rodgers 22.06 (13th) we were forced to retire owing to our other runner being unable to travel owing to a damaged leg. It was interesting to note that the Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe, who dead-heated for first place in last year's Southern Youths c.c. championship, could only finish 5th in the above race. Wycombe Phoenix H. were 2nd, Finchley H. 3rd and Highgate H. 4th, with Watford H. 6th, and 20 teams closed in. items.sum: A Belgrave "B" team lost narrowly, 55 points to 51, to Surrey Beagles at Caterham, with Pete Newell first home.
items.s: MATCH v. SURREY BEAGLES A Belgrave "B" team lost narrowly, 55 points to 51, to Surrey Beagles at Caterham, with Pete Newell first home. At Caterham on February 2nd we fielded what was more or less a " B " team and the local club beat us with 51 pts. to our 55. Pete Newell was first man home followed by a couple of the Beagles, then came Len Herbert who is also a local but he scored for us on this occasion. Doug Briggs also ran well to finish in 5th place, with Alan Bishop 9th, Ken Cuff 11th, Eric Bishop 12th, Jack Lacey 13th and Mick Tween 14th. We scored seven a side and with Len Bishop having to retire owing to shoe trouble this meant that nearly all our men had to count. However, the result is not the thing, so long as a good run was had by all then we are well satisfied and we would like to thank the home club for providing refreshments. items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP South of Thames cross-country championship at Aylesford, where a weakened Belgrave team was 7th and Reading A.C. won the "Colman" Cup. This was held at Aylesford on February 9th from the local Paper Mills sports ground. The dressing facilities were of the best and tea was also provided, not only in the dressing rooms at the finish of the race, but also a sit-down affair when the awards were made. The club was honoured by the fact that this year's President of the Association, was none other than Ernie Duffett, our Running Hon. Sec. Having had winning teams four times out of the last six races, this meant that we had at least 24 chaps barred from competing not forgetting our Southern and National successes, which also bars you from competing in this race. In the circumstances, our 7th position in the team race was quite good and 22 clubs closed in. items.sum: Southern Counties cross-country championships at Hadleigh, where Belgrave won the senior team race, regaining the Frank Wynne Challenge Cup and winning the Odling-Smee Cup.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Southern Counties cross-country championships at Hadleigh, where Belgrave won the senior team race, regaining the Frank Wynne Challenge Cup and winning the Odling-Smee Cup. These were held at Hadleigh, Essex, on February 23rd, over fairly rough country which included a climb up and around the ruins of Hadleigh Castle. In the Youths' event our lads got away to a good start with Wright and Goode up in the first half-dozen. Then came tragedy in the fact that they were wrongly directed and by the time they got back on the right course they had lost quite a lot of ground and places. Frank Wright managed to get up with the leaders once again but Geoff Goode found the effort too much for him and was our 4th scoring man. This race is certainly a " hoodoo " for Geoff and Micky Pyer must have been disappointed at our 4th place in the team race, but we hope for better luck next year. The senior race came next and at the end of the first lap of the country it looked as if Aylesford Paper Mills would retain their team title, as they had three men in the first dozen runners. Our lads were running well together but seemed too far back although Vern Blowfield was going great guns and Eddie Short was also well up. On the second lap we saw Charlie Walker, Eddie Short, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford running well together with Bill Lucas, our captain, acting as the whipper-in. At the finish we saw Vern Blowfield, who had truly made a come-back and had run himself out in the progress, being placed 11th, then we had four in the 20's and although Bill Lucas had dropped about ten places, we still had 10 points to spare over the holders. The rest of our team had also run well with special mention for Hudson and Len Bishop and it seemed strange to see Len Herbert back so far, but he has not done a great deal of racing this season. John Bromley had damaged a foot in an Army race a few days previously but pluckily kept going to the end in order that we could win the " Odling-Smee " Cup, which is awarded to the first Surrey club to finish its complete team of 12 men. We thus regained the " Frank Wynne " Challenge Cup which is awarded to the winners of the senior race, and so repeated our previous wins in 1934, 1946, 1948 and 1949. The Junior race was last on the " card " and as we had expected Ray Tooby was well up with the field but felt the effects of a Service race in mid-week and so could only finish in 7th place. Mike Stearman was next home followed by Doug Briggs and Don Maclean, and don't think it was the latter's type of country. Placings of our members in the various races were:— Youths—3, F. J.
