items.label: No. 119
items.h: LONDON TO BRIGHTON NATIONAL RELAY RACE
items.sum: Stage-by-stage account of the London to Brighton National Relay of 10 April 1954, run again from Westminster, in which Belgrave finished second to South London Harriers.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON NATIONAL RELAY RACE Stage-by-stage account of the London to Brighton National Relay of 10 April 1954, run again from Westminster, in which Belgrave finished second to South London Harriers. SATURDAY APRIL 10TH 1954 By Olympian. This Classic race promoted by the "News of the World" has come to be recognised as one of the major events in the Athletic Calendar and on this occasion history was again made when the course from Westminster to Brighton as instituted in 1924 when the race was originally staged was once more experimentally adopted for the first time since 19[illegible]. In the intervening years the start has been from Mitcham but it is hoped that by the restriction of supporters coaches that the full distance of 54¾ miles can be reinstated as the recognised route for future races. The race started at 10am. precisely by the first stroke of Big Ben and after the twenty runners had sorted themselves out from the conglomeration of press cameramen, who had formed an almost impassable barrier in the first twenty yards, the battle was on in earnest. A fast start along the embankment to Chelsea Bridge soon strung out the field which was led by Wood of Sheffield United Harriers who had recently performed creditably in the International Cross Country closely followed by Parmenter of Birchfield and Wood of Surrey A.C. Our own Bill Lucas was not far away in 10th position The three leading teams remained unchanged to Clapham Common where we were seventh, some fifty seconds behind the Sheffield Club with all but Birchfield of the favoured clubs behind us. John Bromley on the second leg to Mitcham maintained the position with a steady run but Blackheath and Essex Beagles had come more into the picture and Sheffield were over a minute ahead with Bolton also prominent. Jack Brown on his favourite stage from Mitcham to Purley produced another of his excellent performances on this leg and with a well judged effort took Belgrave into a very valuable lead of twenty one seconds from Surrey A.C. and Sheffield. The lead was held by Archie Bedford on the fourth stage to Merstham at which point we had 16 seconds over Essex Beagles and 28 over South London who had been slowly moving through the field. The remainder of the teams had begun to fall away - Birchfield had not maintained their earlier promise and Thames Valley, a well fancied team, had not made up for their poor start. Our Cross Country Captain Dennis Brickwood, who in 1937 had started Mitcham A.C. on a winning sequence in this event by an inches decision over our own Arthur Allum, was performing for the first time in this race in Belgrave colours and although chased by two very promising runners in the shape of Douglas of Essex Beagles and Lyne of S.L.H. retained our lead by a small margin over the latter club. Another veteran, Len Herbert, who is now 40 years of age took over at Earlswood with the Beagles and South London Harriers breathing down his neck, but with a nicely judged effort and one of his well renowned sprint finishes opened up a few seconds gap from those clubs. Now began one of the crucial stages of the race the newly arranged leg of well over six miles which constituted the combined Nos. 5 and 6 stages of the old course. Charlie Smart who at the age of 44 is running better than ever set off with the Belgrave baton with Gordon Pirie of S.L.H. some 15 seconds behind. As one would expect it was not long before Gordon caught Charlie ,but it was not without a fight that he eventually got away. In fact Charles actually repassed Pirie twice before having to relinquish his lead and by finishing only a minute behind at Handcross,can be said to have put up an excellent performance. The Beagles were still in third place but had lost a little ground. The next stage was another vital long leg over which many battles have been fought in the past. S.L.H. had given it to Peter Driver another of their young but very talented members and he set up for them what proved to be an unassailable lead with a time of 28.52 which beat by 17 seconds the October effort of Pirie and Olney which it will be remembered was considered to be an almost fantastic effort. However even Driver's time was not unbeatable, for first Jim Peters lowered it by 10 seconds and in doing so passed Charlie Walker and took Essex Beagles into 2nd place, and later by Alec Olney who reduced it by another 7 seconds without bringing his club T.V.H. anywhere near the front. The race by this time had definitely resolved itself into a battle between the leading three clubs with S. L. H. almost certain winners. Bob Taylor set about reducing the lead and with the fastest time of the day on his leg gained 43secs. on the Beagles but made only a small impression on S.L.H. who were still some 2½ minutes ahead. Stan Gawler carried on the good work and also returned the fastest time of the day on his stage and in so doing he brought us back to second place. S.L.H. were still keeping up the pace and with only the last leg to be run had over two minutes to spare. Dave Baulch a newcomer to Belgrave and on his first Brighton run put up a creditable performance which kept us in second place and also gave him the second fastest time for the stage.This member has definitely come to stay and should be an asset to our teams for some time to come Although we had to be content with only second place on this occasion the team performance was extremely good and it will take an exceptionally fast team to defeat S.L.H. in this type of race over the next few years. Providing Belgrave can produce two runners to undertake the vital 7th and 8th stages which now more than ever are the crucial points of the race, I feel that we can match South London's strength. In Jack Brown we have one of those runners but at present it is difficult to see who else can bear this mantle to combat S.L.H.'s Pirie and Driver. It is time our younger runners trained hard enough to keep our ageing athletes out of the team - this is not a race for the over 35's, yet in this year's team we had five in that group and without doubt were the oldest team on the road. We cannot much longer depend on these runners who have carried the long distance, track and road running on their shoulders since the war ended. In passing it should be mentioned that the old record for the full course which had stood since 1932 was beaten by no less than 8 minutes by S.L.H. and six by Belgrave and the Mitcham/Brighton time made by Mitcham A.C. in 1938 by approximately two minutes by both clubs. items.sum: Report of the National cross-country championships at Arrowe Park, Birkenhead, where Belgrave youths were eighth, seniors ninth and juniors sixteenth, with team placings.
items.s: NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the National cross-country championships at Arrowe Park, Birkenhead, where Belgrave youths were eighth, seniors ninth and juniors sixteenth, with team placings. This year Arrowe Park, Birkenhead was the venue for the Championships which were held on March 13th. The course which everyone had expected to be easy, turned out to be quite sticky. The first event was the Youths' race over 3 Miles. There, our lads expected to do well, bearing in mind their surprise 2nd place in the "Southern". This was not to be however, for Ron Linstead and Jim Edgar never seemed to get going and, finishing together in 30th and 31st places, were a minute down on the winner. D. Pettican did not seem at home on the sticky ground and was 85th G. Flanagan, 99th failed to produce his Southern form but nevertheless ran well for an athlete of only three months experience. When the team positions had been worked out it was found that we had come eighth. The Senior Race over a course of just under 10 miles was the next on. Our team was weakened by Jack Brown's absence and it is interesting to note that G. Olding, our Second Claim member, who was beaten by Jack in the Club "7", finished 19th. Although we did not expect anything brilliant from our runners, they did not run too badly and certainly bettered their "Southern" performance In coming 31st, Chas Walker certainly pulled one out of the bag and so becomes holder of the "Harry Parker" Memorial Trophy, for the ensuing year. Not far behind Chas. was "[illegible]umbo" Masters in 41st place, a good performance especially in view of his recent foot injury. Dennis Brickwood running in his usual steady manner, was our next man to finish coming 73rd. Doug Briggs came in 20 places later. Our next two home were Stan Gawler 98th, and Eddie Short 128th.Both these runners were further back than expected, although in fairness to Eddie Short it must be stated that his training has been interrupted this winter. Lastly came the Juniors who once more had to perform on a course churned up by nearly a thousand others. Here we came only 16th, but Dave Baulch's 21st place was especially encouraging for it was only his sixth race since he joined us in November. Peter Courtney ran well and finishe 38th. We had to go back to 125th position for our next scorer, B. Trower, who was ten places in front of Frank Wright whose running seems to have been upset by an Army P.T.I. Course he is on at present. And finally a word about our supporters. There is no doubt the efforts of our runners were matched by the few Club supporters who turned up. Particular mention must be made of Charlie Poulter and his two lads who carried a vast quantity of tea from London to Arrowe Park, where he was soon relieved of it by three teams of thirsty and grateful runners. Arthur Whitehead and Mickey Pyer did what was expected of them as Team Managers and Recorders, but found a flaw in the Northern Officials organisation. Arthur is particularly suited however, to overcoming diplomatically other peoples' inefficiency. Finally Eric Bishop motor cycled all the way with his wife, and adquately made up for the very poor support our runners received from the Club generally. items.h: A FEW WORDS FROM THE HON. TREASURER
items.sum: The Hon. Treasurer thanks members who paid arrears and asks the rest to send their 2/- magazine and current-year subscriptions at once, with a note for members on National Service.
items.s: A FEW WORDS FROM THE HON. TREASURER The Hon. Treasurer thanks members who paid arrears and asks the rest to send their 2/- magazine and current-year subscriptions at once, with a note for members on National Service. I should like to thank all those who so promptly replied to the letters I sent out a few weeks ago regarding arrears of subscriptions, also those who paid without a reminder. Our rebuilding programme is now in progress, which means we shall be spending the whole of our funds, so I would once again, through the medium of the magazine, ask all those who have not done so, to send in their subscriptions for the current year AT ONCE. You have an excellent opportunity of killing two birds with one stone, by not only completing the enclosed form,that is assuming you want to get the next issue of the Belgravian, and returning it to me with the necessary 2/-, but also including in the same letter your subscription for the current year. If you are not sure whether you have paid, just glance at the back of your handbook and see if you have a receipt affixed for the current year. May I once again remind members who are engaged on the compulsory period of National Service that whilst we do not enforce payment of your subscriptions during that period, IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT YOU LET ME KNOW THAT YOU ARE SO ENGAGED. Will Service members also indicate on the form for the Belgravian, whether they would like it sent to their home or Service address. S.C.R. S.C.R. S.C.R.

items.sum: Jack Chappell's field events section notes on members' throwing and jumping form, the Sward and Brockman Trophy meetings and hopes for the Kinnaird.
items.s: WITH THE FIELD EVENTS MEN Jack Chappell's field events section notes on members' throwing and jumping form, the Sward and Brockman Trophy meetings and hopes for the Kinnaird. May I first say how pleased I am that we can once again write to all our members, particularly as far as I am concerned to those in the Field Events Section, through the medium of the Belgravian. This year, as we all know, the weather has not been too kind to us, but we have been able to train during the winter. I was surprised to see so many members turning up for training. It is quite encouraging to the Club and particularly to Frank Simmons and Percy Luxon. Up to the moment we have not had a very exciting time but one or two have started to come into form. Percy Potter's win in the Essex County Hammer Championshop with a throw of 146' 8" was a fine effort. He tells me he had a throw of 155' at Imber Court. Well done, Percy. J. Powell-Jones is giving a good account of himself. In addition to winning the Surrey County Junior Weight with 48' 10" - a County record - he is also putting the senior weight for London University at about 42'. Ted Gaworski is also coming back to form. At the Sward Trophy Meeting on 29th June he threw the discus 142', which I think is the best club performance. He is also putting the weight about 43' and the hammer 140'. A new member,Ron Liggins is also proving very useful with the javelin, his best distance to date being 178' 10" in the Middlesex County Championship which gave him 2nd place.. Percy Luxon and Ken Key are showing improvement in both the Long Jump and Triple Jump. Dennis Fleming had an operation on his arm during the winter but should soon be back in form. Young Day is jumping well and we are pleased to see him when on leave. Other new members are beginning to take their place in teams. We did not do too good at the Brockman Trophy Meeting, but in the Sward Meeting we were better than last year. We had a competitor in each event except the pole vault which certainly shows the growth of the section. Eddie Short was 3rd in the 3000 metres steeplechase. I am now looking forward to the Kinnaird and hope we shall again make a good show. Alan Law is at Oxford but recovering from a strained back. I wish him well as we can do with him. Finally, the most important thing is to keep hard at training and make full use of the coaches who are ready to help. Wishing you all many successes. Jack Chappell. items.s: THE COUNTY TRACK CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of Belgrave successes at the Surrey, Kent, Middlesex and Essex county track championships, including J. Powell-Jones's Surrey shot record. Our members met with many successes in the various County Championships which were held on Saturday, 22nd May, and in all gained 7 firsts, 7 seconds and 7 thirds, in addition to which a recently joined second claim member, J. Butterfield, won no fewer than three Kent titles, viz; shot, discus and hammer throw,the last with a new County record of 135' 2". At Motspur Park the most outstanding performance was undoubtedly that of our Junior, J. Powell-Jones who set up a new Surrey County record in the shot put with a put of 48' 10". Despite a recent injury, Alan Sexton won the 440yds in 49.4secs. with A. Picton 3rd. The sprinters did well with Basil Walden defeating the holder C. Gibbs, to win the 100 yards, with D Merrett 3rd and J. Benstead 5th. In the 220 yards Merrett was 2nd to Gibbs and Benstead again 5th. C. Walker was third in a fast race over three miles and T. Gaworski 2nd in the shot put with 41ft.2ins and third in the hammer with 137ft. 6ins. R. Phillips won the two miles walk in 14mins. 57.8 secs with Eric Hall 3rd and Syd James 5th The best junior performance was that of J.Powell-Jones who won the shot put with a new County record of 48ft.10ins. H. Powell wo was third in the javelin and B. Windley who cleared 20ft to finish 3rd in the long jump, both achieved Southern Standard. In the Middlesex Championships Bob Taylor was second in the 880 yards for the third year in succession. He equalled Arthur Wint's County record in his heat, but a slow first lap in the final prevented a fast time, and he was beaten by R. Day in 1 min. 57 secs. A. Cameron won the 440 yards and R. Wolton was third. In the 100 yards I Mayers was 2nd and R. Holtum 4th. P. Luxon missed 1st place in the long jump by three inches and was fifth in the hop step and jump with K. Key 4th. In the Kent Championships Jack Brown won the mile in 4 mins. 19.6secs and R. Liggins was 2nd in the javelin with 178ft. Forces in Egypt send news of his activities in "Sphinxland". In the Station Sports he competed in the Long Jump, Triple Jump, 100 yards and 220 yards with the following results:- L.J. 19' 6", H.S.& J. 41'6"" (1st) 100 yards 10.3sec. (2nd) and 220 yards, 23.5secs. (2nd). In the R.A.F. Championships, he improved on this by gaining 1st in the two jumps, both with record distances, viz; Long Jump 20' 5", Triple Jump, 42' 7", and was second in the 100 yards in 10.2secs. Later in the Inter-Services Championships, he was 4th in the Long Jump with 19' 10", 1st in the Triple Jump with 41' 7", 2nd in the 100 yards in 10.4secs. and 2nd in the 220 yards in 23.2. He mentions that all the track events take place on a sand track and the run up for the jumps is bone hard bumpy mud. Contrary to what he understands is the opinion over here, the temperature and general conditions do not tend to make for faster times in fact he has it on the authority of a A.A.A. Coach that there is a difference of about .1 - .2 in the 100 yards and .3 in the 220 yards. Congratulations! Charles, we certainly hope your times were correctly recorded and we wish you more successes. C.R. Jones C.R. Jones serving in H.M. Forces in Egypt; won long and triple jump at R.A.F. items.sum: Dave Shepherd's social section notice on the Annual Dinner and Dance at Oxford Street Corner House on 25th September, coach seats for the Brighton Relay, and winter socials at the improved Belgrave Hall.
items.s: SOCIAL Dave Shepherd's social section notice on the Annual Dinner and Dance at Oxford Street Corner House on 25th September, coach seats for the Brighton Relay, and winter socials at the improved Belgrave Hall. The most important date in the Club's Social Section is the ANNUAL DINNER AND DANCE which will be held this year on 25th September, a date which you should make a note of straight away. As the attendance last year was not as great as was expected, it has been decided to hold this year's function at Oxford Street Corner House, (corner of Tottenham Court Road, where there is accommodation for not more than 200 so you are advised to book early to avoid disappointment. As the number is limited, all applications for tickets MUST be accompanied by the cash,(17/6d each)and although the tickets are not yet available, you can send your applications in as early as you please. Those who have attended during the past few years need no recommendation as it is really a first class night. So once again, don't leave it too late. Another important function, and one in which you will get full value for your money, is the Brighton Relay in October. Here again, if you would only realise the immense pleasure and excitement which can be gained from this day out, I am sure I should be inundated with applications for seats on the coaches. With the completion of the improvements at Belgrave Hall, the socials during the coming winter season, should be a great improvement on previous years. We need to recapture some of the pre-war enthusiasm for these very enjoyable socials and I hope that the improved amenities at our hall will have this effect. Look out for the dates in our next issue and come along and give your support. Dave Shepherd. Dave Shepherd Dave Shepherd London to Brighton Relay Oxford Street Corner House Tottenham Court Road Belgrave Hall

items.sum: Jack Goswell's walking section notes on winter progress, the win in the National 20, all-day strolls, coaching at Battersea Track and hopes for the National 50 Kilos after the Northern 50 Kilos win.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Jack Goswell's walking section notes on winter progress, the win in the National 20, all-day strolls, coaching at Battersea Track and hopes for the National 50 Kilos after the Northern 50 Kilos win. This being the first issue of the Belgravian for some months, the activities of the Walking Section have had to be tightly compressed, so if I have inadvertently overlooked any of the unusually good performances, my humble apologies. We can be pleased with our progress,during the winter we made continued improvement in the "Open" sevens and some of our younger members began to show their paces. I hope it will continue during the track season. Our distance walkers are going from strength to strength. To gauge the spirit, one only needs to go on one of our trips away from home, a better days outing you could not wish for.The biggest triumph of all was, of course, our win in the National 20, a big surprise for many and a credit to the Club. Our all day strolls are thoroughly enjoyed by all who take part, even if "Big head" will argue with the Captain (alias Fog horn), over the birth and names of trees. Those who want to improve their knowledge of Natural History or English History would always be most welcome and would soon learn something about "Silent pools" "Good Queen Bess", "Old manors", etc. Last Whitsun we learnt that they feed the north on rhubarb - acres and acres of it, in fact the country outside Leeds is covered with it. There is a very good attendance at Battersea Track on Tuesday evenings and I am sure the lads will benefit from the advice and assistance of our coaches Len Fletcher and Don Brown.Unfortunately Len is now working quite a bit outside London and is not able to spend so much time at the track as last year and whilst we miss you Len,we are fortunate to have one of your pupils in Don Brown. We must endeavour to enrol more youngsters to keep our strength going and I should like to see a good field battling for the "Olympic" Cup next year. By the time this is being read, the Inter-Club meeting at Battersea will be over and I am sure we can look for a good result. The National 50 Kilos will also have been held at Sheffield and I hope will result in another National Win.The lads are all fighting fit, particularly after their win at Bradford in the Northern 50 Kilos on Whit Monday and I am sure we all wish them luck, and continued progress in the coming months. May the name of Belgrave be seen many times in our National papers. Yours sincerely Jack Goswell. items.h: RACE WALKING NEWS SINCE THE LAST ISSUE
items.sum: Race walking news from August and September: Norman Guilmant's win in the Hastings to Brighton race and second in the London to Brighton Walk, his collapse at Milan, and the St. Dunstan's Hour Walks.
items.s: RACE WALKING NEWS SINCE THE LAST ISSUE Race walking news from August and September: Norman Guilmant's win in the Hastings to Brighton race and second in the London to Brighton Walk, his collapse at Milan, and the St. Dunstan's Hour Walks. Before starting on the winter season's results, some mention should be made of the efforts of our distance walkers during August and September last. In the Hastings to Brighton race on 15th August last Norman Guilmant put up a grand performance by winning the race in a new record time and to crown it, won the handicap also. The team were second in the team race, our best performance for many years. In the following month, Norman again excelled himself by gaining second place in the London to Brighton Walk and of course won the Club Long Distance Championship. Hugh McGreechan and Harry Shields walked their best distances to date, both being inside 8. 40. but unfortunately Fred Rolfe had shoe trouble and was obliged to fall out at Dale Hill. However Jack Wakeley who had only intended making it a stroll, being his first long walk following his operation, made a great effort to push through and finish as our fourth man to make us second in the team race, only five points behind the winners. Our other walkers, Bernard Eglington, Joe Wilson, Percy Wilson, all gave a good account of themselves. The usual enthusiastic support was in evidence and much appreciated by the walkers. Following Norman's fine performance in the Brighton Walk we were very pleased to hear that he had been selected to go to Milan for an International 100 kilometres race. After lying 6th at 80 kilometres, he suddenly collapsed and of course was out of the race. He was subsequently taken to hospital, and our old friend of Surrey Walking Club, Timber Woodcock, who was acting as manager, in order to stay with Norman, was obliged to become a casualty also, and be put to bed with "flu". Fortunately Norman has suffered no serious after effects and is now almost back to last year's form. Hard luck Norman and better luck next time. In the St. Dunstan's Hour Walks at Parliament Hill Fields, 23 of our lads competed, six of whom qualified for "Six mile" badges and no doubt they are all now striving for the "Seven". This was virtually the end of the summer season and we now go over to Wimbledon. items.s: BELGRAVE OPEN 7 - November 28th Report of the Belgrave Open 7 walk with a record 332 entries, Belgrave 3rd in the scratch team race and B and A teams 2nd and 3rd in the handicap. Our own Open created a record programme entry of no less than 332. 220 started and for the first time over 200 finished, 203 to be exact. It was a busy day and a hard one for the recorders and it is certain that the whole day reflected credit on the Club. The scratch team race developed into a neck and neck struggle, and it was very difficult to forecast who was going to come out winners until the very end, eventually 3 points separated the first 3 teams with us taking 3rd place.. Bob McMullen once again led the lads home in 5th position with George Checkley 8th, Hugh McGreechan 15th and E. Hall 16th. All the handicap team prizes stopped over our side of the water as Surrey W.C. took 1st place, our "B" team (Demmon, Middleton Wilson,Doubleday) were 2nd and the "A" Team (Hall,Checkley,Eglington McMullen) were 3rd. The result showed a decided improvement in all our walkers and hopes of greater successes in the future. In addition Len Demmon was third in the individual handicap. items.s: SOUTHERN GARNET CUP CHAMPIONSHIP - February 6th Report of the Southern Garnet Cup walking championship at Eltham, where Belgrave finished third after Bob Phillips was disqualified, behind winners Surrey Walking Club. This was held at Eltham on February 6th and we were unfortunately short of two of our qualified members, so that when Bob Phillips came under the judges' ban after the first mile our hopes of a place looked very slender. However this setback rather than deter the rest of the team, seemed to make them more enthusiastic, and so well did they walk, that we finished third in the Championship. Considering we had an entirely different team from last year when we won, this was an excellent performance and says much for the younger members. With all these walkers eligible for next year we have very high hopes of regaining the championship. Congratulations to Surrey Walking Club on their win. The team was led home by Eric Hall 12th, 84mins.4sec. 13th R. Newson 84.37, 24th J. Scamell 87.0[illegible], and 36th R. Garwood, 89.29. Surrey Walking Club scored 58 points to our 76. items.sum: Report of the club 20 miles walking championship for the Ricketts Shield on a new course, won by Hugh McGreechan for the third time, with the junior 5 miles Olympic Cup a walk-over for Ray Middleton.
items.s: CLUB 20 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP - April 17th Report of the club 20 miles walking championship for the Ricketts Shield on a new course, won by Hugh McGreechan for the third time, with the junior 5 miles Olympic Cup a walk-over for Ray Middleton. A new course was used for the race for the Ricketts Shield this year at the suggestion of the walkers themselves. Owing to traffic conditions at various crossings, and the opening of new blocks of flats adjacent to the course it was felt that the existing course was too dangerous for the walkers and the Committee therefore agreed to use the same course as that used for the 20 miles road run. This consists of three equal laps, turning left with traffic the whole way and with no crossings. After the race the general opinion of all the walkers was that the course was an improvement on the old one. Hugh McGreechan and George Beecham led the field for the first two laps at a very fast pace and one began to wonder who would be the first to crack. Eventually George began to drop back and soon lost a number of places. Hugh continued to hold the lead, but by this time George Checkley was storming ahead and making up a lot of ground but not quite sufficient to catch McGreechan who thus won for the third time running in the time of 2hrs. 57mins. 19secs. George Checkley was a good second in 2hrs. 58mins. 23secs., Bernard Eglington coming next nearly 7 minutes behind in 3hrs. 5mins. 14sec. Norman Guilmant, 4th, Bob Newson, 5th, George Beecham 6th and Fred Rolfe 7th all completed the course inside 3hrs. 15mins. Outstanding performance was that of Bob Newson on his first 20. He is certainly going to be one of our leading distance men in the near future. The handicap was deservedly won by George Checkley with Bob Newson 2nd, and Bernard Eglington 3rd. Our thanks are due to all the helpers, the ladies who manned a sponge and drink station at the bottom of the hill, to Ron Garwood, Arthur Skinner and their ladies at the top of Kingston Hill, the helpers at the top of Lauriston Road and all those who assisted with cars and enabled the judges to get round the course. As last year, we arranged to hold our Junior 5 miles race on the same day, for the "Olympic" Cup. Unfortunately Johnny Haynes was unable to get away from duty to defend his title and only Ray Middleton turned up and had a walk over for this very fine cup. This shows the necessity for enrolling some more junior members and thus ensure that next year we shall have a proper race. Hugh McGreechan Hugh McGreechan won Ricketts Shield for third time running, 2hrs. 57mins. 19secs. items.s: NATIONAL 20 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP - May 8th. Report of Belgrave's team win in the National 20 miles walking championship at Birmingham, with tables of the team's positions and team scores, near-miss for the Nimegen Shield and thanks to helpers. The Championship was held at Birmingham this year and what a grand day it turned out to be for the Club. Once again we are holders of a National title and it was grand to see in a weekly paper "Belgrave National Champions". It was quite a good field which faced the starter on a fair two lap course although there was fairly heavy traffic in many places. From the start the lads were content to settle down and the following table shows the positions of the team throughout the race. As one can see, not only did the lads consolidate their positions, but gradually improved on them, although Geogge Checkley did drop one place in the last stages. Sheffield made a dashing start and were only 29 points at 3 miles, whilst we were then 78 and thereafter at every check we were improving our position. The last few miles was a drive to strengthen our position and this we certainly did. The only real disappointment was that we did not win the Nimegen Shield, although we had seven men.in before Woodford's 5th man, but unfortunately Fred Rolfe developed a bad spell as will be seen from the table above between 9 and 14 miles otherwise we should certainly have scored the double, in fact we only missed it by one place, the shield going to the first team to close in their full team of 8. Our heartiest congratulations to all, particularly to George Checkley who celebrated his birthday by gaining his Honours badge. Bernard Eglington, 13th, missed his by one position. George Beecham gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan the Sydney Bayliss Cup and Bob Newson his first (2nd Class) National Standard medal. In fact the four members of the winning team were all inside first class standard and three out of the remaining founr were inside 2nd class. To Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday, Len Demmon and Billie True and the ladies who came along to give their help and support ,we say thank you very much. Needless to say the hard working Hon. Sec. Jack Goswell, covered quite 50 miles on his iron horse dashing from one end of the field to the other to attend to the wants of the men. items.s: ON THE TRACK Walking notes on the club two miles track handicaps, Johnny Haynes's resignation, members' news, the Police Barking to Southend Walk and the team's prizes in the Northern 50 Kilometres Walk at Bradford. Our two miles track handicaps held to date have been well supported. The first was won by "Pothunter" Harry Shields, with Eric Hall 2nd and Doub 3rd. The second was won by Maurice Nye who we had not seen since the early winter, but who must have been doing plenty of secret training. We look forward to seeing him more with the lads in the future. Doub improved on his first effort by coming 2nd and Percy Wilson was third, slowly getting back to fitness after a spell of ill health. We were also pleased to see Charlie Speechley having a go again after a period in hospital. One minute covered fourteen competitors in this race - good marks to the handicapper. News has just been received that Johnny Haynes has made up his mind to resign from the club as he is now permanently posted a long way away and is hoping to join another club nearer at hand. We can ill afford to lose our younger members but thank him for his help in the past and wish him well in the future. We understand the "Baron" has bought a nice big car. We have missed him out racing this past winter, but when he is qualified to drive we feel sure he will be out regularly particularly on the distance walks when he can be of great help. Gerry Warr has gone back to rejoin our Southampton-cum-Eastleigh contingent having taken up residence at Southampton, so we hope he will be seeing something of Percy Wright. For many years Belgrave Walkers have been trying to win the Police Barking to Southend Walk for four years in succession, and this year we hoped Hugh McGreechan would be the first to do it. Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and Hugh have all won on three successive occasions and Hugh looked all set for it this year. However that very improved young walker, McFarlane of the Poly, who incidentally seems to spend more time with us than his own club, beat Mc.to it and so the battle for this honour still goes on. A piece of news concerning our long distance walkers has just come to hand and whilst we hope to give a fuller report of the race in the next issue, we feel that brief details should be included here. Four walkers and the usual hard working Jack Goswell went up to Bradford for the Northern 50 Kilometres Walk on Whit Monday and came away well loaded up with prizes. Hugh McGreechan was 3rd in the race, Norman Guilmant 5th, Bernard Eglington 9th and Harry Shields 10th, all inside 5 hours. In addition Harry took the second handicap prize and Norman the 3rd. It looks well for the R.W.A.50 Kilometres. items.sum: Editorial on subscriptions to the magazine, the election of Tom Morrell as President, the completion of the Belgrave Hall rebuilding and the walkers' London to Brighton success.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial on subscriptions to the magazine, the election of Tom Morrell as President, the completion of the Belgrave Hall rebuilding and the walkers' London to Brighton success. Fellow Members, The response to the invitation to members to subscribe towards the cost of the Belgravian was not as great as I expected, but forms are still coming in and I feel sure that as time goes on, the majority of our members will become subscribers. This issue marks the beginning of a new Belgrave Year and judging by the enthusiasm displayed by members at the Annual General Meeting, there is every prospect of it proving a very successful one. The unanimous election of Tom Morrell as our new President will add in no small measure to our efforts to maintain our reputation as one of the leading clubs in the country. There is no doubt that Tom is fully deserving of the honour conferred on him and we offer our hearty congratulations to him on attaining his present office. For many years his work as Assistant Hon. Treasurer, in particular in dealing with the supplies of Club vests, etc., has brought him into close contact with almost every member, and his willingness to carry on with this work during his year of Presidency, is a typical example of his enthusiastic and generous disposition. Another landmark in the history of the Club has been reached in the completion of our rebuilding programme at Belgrave Hall. Much work has been put into this project by members over a long period of years to make Belgrave Hall one of the finest Club Headquarters in the country and it is up to every member to see that every possible care is taken of the new amenities which have been provided. Our long distance walkers rounded off a successful summer season by very decisively winning both the individual and team titles in the classic race of the year, the London to Brighton Walk, the team event being won in a new record low score of 16 points. Fuller details will be found elsewhere. As this event actually took place in the Club's new year, let us look on it as a good omen for the events which are to come. Your Editor. Tom Morrell Tom Morrell elected President; Assistant Hon. Treasurer London to Brighton Walk Belgrave Hall

items.label: No. 120
items.sum: Report of the Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall: tributes, the Hon. Secretary's and Treasurer's reports, election of Tom Morrell as President, presentations and proposed subscription increases.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING Report of the Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall: tributes, the Hon. Secretary's and Treasurer's reports, election of Tom Morrell as President, presentations and proposed subscription increases. Our Annual General Meeting, held at Belgrave Hall on Monday 20th September, gave members an opportunity to see the progress which is being made with the building programme and the attendance of over 100 was remarkably good. Harry Evans, the interim President, took the chair and after a few well chosen words, the assembly stood for a few moments as a token of respect to our late President Frank Elson, and a Life Member H. Goodfellow who had passed away since our last meeting. In presenting the Annual Report the Hon. Secretary, Alf Harley apologised for the omission of a paragraph referring to our second placings in the Brighton "Southern" and "National" Relays and it was unanimously agreed that it should be inserted. The Report, which included a vote of thanks to Ernie Duffett who was not seeking re-election as Running Hon. Secretary, having held that office for many years, was then adopted. The Hon. Treasurer then gave the financial report, starting by thanking the Assistant Hon. Treasurer, Tom Morrell, Eric Bishop, and A. Pyer for the help they had given him and Also Les Cohen for the work he had put in for the Supporters Club. He then compared the income and expenditure with the previous year pointing out the large decrease of £140 on the cost of printing which was mainly due to the fact that only one issue of the Belgravian had been made, and that, with the new photo-type process. The cost of social events was also considerably reduced and with a little more support for the Annual Dinner this could have been reduced further still. On the income side, subscriptions were down a little but donations from Life Members, Past Presidents, etc. was up. He informed the meeting that there were still a number of members in arrears and hoped they would promptly pay their dues. Handicap fees remained fairly steady but there was plenty of room for improvement by better support to club promotions. A 25% increase in entries would produce a much larger revenue from this source and would make for keener competition. The Inter-City Meeting at the White City last year resulted in our funds benefiting to the extent of £55 and provided a very good reason for our members giving it their support. The final item of income, which for many years has been the biggest, was the donation from the Supporters Club, and was actually less then the total subscriptions. With the exception of the first payment of £660 towards the rebuilding, there was nothing outstanding about the Building Fund Account, but the Hon. Treasurer pointed out that as the whole of our investments would be utilised on this project, we should be losing a valuable source of income of £140 or more per annum in interest. Before the report was adopted, Eric Bishop, one of our Hon. Auditors, expressed his satisfaction with the accounts. The meeting then proceeded to elect the officers for the year. Harry Evans proposed Tom Morrell as President. Alf Harley seconded and gave a short review of Tom's services to the Club over 27 years and his election was carried unanimously. It was then proposed, seconded and carried that the names of A. Readman and G.P. Powell be added to the list of Vice-Presidents. The principle officers, Hon. Secretary and Assistant, Hon. Treasurer and Assistant were re-elected and the election of Section Secretaries, Captains, Vice Captains, etc. began. It was agreed to split the office of Running Hon. Secretary Denis Brickwood being elected for Cross Country and Ron. Holtum for the track. A full list of the officers will be included in the new handbook which will probably have reached you by now. A number of presentations were then made. Harry Evans presented the new Jimmy Bellchamber Trophy (50 kilometres Walk) to the first holder Hugh McGreechan. Ted Gaworski presented a cup to Peter Porter for the best throwing performance of the year (156ft6in) with the hammer. The President presented a cup, from the Club, to Percy Luxon for the best jumping performance of the year (45ft 5ins. triple jump and 23ft. 2ins. long jump). The proposed new rules governing the Trustees and powers to borrow were moved by Alf Harley, seconded by Syd Roberts and carried. The Hon. Treasurer then proposed that subscriptions be increased to £1 for seniors, 10/- for juniors, 5/- for boys and 10/- for Hon. members. He outlined the future liabilities of the club which would include repaying money borrowed from the bank to complete our building programme and increased cost of maintaining the hall. The motion was seconded by the Hon. Secretary who gave a brief description of the new amenities at the hall. A number of members stated that they felt the new rates would still be giving good value and the amendment to the rules was carried unanimously. It was made apparent from the points raised both in the Hon. Treasurer's report and the facts put forward in proposing the amendment to rules that we must keep the money flowing in. This can be done by being up to date with subscriptions, supporting the subscription list for the "Belgravian", supporting club events, taking tickets in the Supporters Club and making voluntary donations similar to the old "halfpenny in a box" scheme or sixpence a week until our funds are built up again. Under any other business, a vote of thanks was given to Frank Webb for his work in connection with the disposal of tickets for the White City. Might I end by asking all members to study their handbooks well. Make yourselves acquainted with the Section Officers, keep in touch with them and above all GIVE THEM YOUR SUPPORT. G.S.D. items.sum: The Hon. Treasurer asks members to pay their subscriptions at the new rate early and invites donations towards the Building Fund debt.
items.s: HON. TREASURER'S NOTE The Hon. Treasurer asks members to pay their subscriptions at the new rate early and invites donations towards the Building Fund debt. Those of you who attended the Annual General Meeting will need no further enlightenment of the fact that the annual subscriptions have been advanced. Quite a number of conscientious members have already paid their subscriptions for the current year, but at the old rate, and I hope they will at the first opportunity, forward to me the balance. To the remainder I would say as I did at the A.G.M. - please pay your subscriptions EARLY. I shall endeavour to be at Wimbledon as often as possible, but it can be handed to Tom Morrell and of course there are such things as postal orders and 2½d stamps. Donations, large and small, will be welcomed from our Past Presidents and Life Members as the more money we can accumulate, the sooner we shall be able to pay off our debt on the Building Fund. Tom Morrell Tom Morrell Wimbledon

items.s: THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and results of the club track championships at Battersea Park on Saturday 7 August. The Club Championships, the highlight of the track season were held as usual at Battersea Park on Saturday, August 7th. The meeting opened up with fairly good weather and everyone was keeping their fingers crossed that it would continue throughout the afternoon. Unfortunately the rain arrived just before the childrens' races and somewhat affected the entries, but generally speaking the meeting went off very successfully. Entries were not quite so good as last year, notable non-appearances being from Alan Sextion, Bob Taylor who we regret to say is in hospital and J. Brown. It is also interesting to note that only 12 standards were gained as against 37 last year and one wonders whether the raising the standards since last year had any effect on the number of entries. items.sum: Report of Belgrave's first win in the AAA relay championships, the 4 x 110 yards in 42.6 sec at Birmingham, and John Powell-Jones's junior shot record.
items.s: A.A.A. RELAYS Report of Belgrave's first win in the AAA relay championships, the 4 x 110 yards in 42.6 sec at Birmingham, and John Powell-Jones's junior shot record. On 31st July we took two teams to Birmingham for the AAA. Relay Championships which were being held in conjunction with the Junior Championships. Our main hope was in the 4 x 110 yards relay, whilst we thought we had an outside chance in the 4 x 440 yards. I was quietly confident that we would pull off the short distance relay and my confidence was increased when our team won their heat in 42.9s The 4 x 440 team gave of their best and although they were knocked out in their heat, with a little more luck they would have been in the final. Meanwhile J. Powell Jones was performing in the Junior Shot put and was leading when the final of the short relay was announced. We had drawn lane No. 4 and our lads were prepared to do or die. At the start Dennis Merrett went away well, held his own and indeed gained a trifle to hand over to Ron Holtum who, although he had a bad cold, ran well to catch Ferguson of Notts. A.C. and the T.V.H. runner. Ron handed over to Basil Walden who put in a terrific challenge to hand over to Ivan Mayers about 1½ yards up. T.V.H. had Downs on the last leg and I thought he might rob us of our first win in this event but with 50 yards to go I saw Ivan's face break into a grin and I knew that it was ours. Ivan came away to win by four clear yards and we had registered our first win in the A.A.A. Team Championships in the creditable time of 42.6secs., the second fastest time by a British Team. After I had recovered my equilibrium, I whispered a quiet word in John Powell-Jones ear and he hurled the shot 53feet 1 inch to end a good day's work and establish a new Junior record. Needless to say we celebrated our win in the proper manner on our return to London. Heartiest congratulations must go to D. Merrett, R. Holtum, B. Walden, and I. Mayers. They worked very hard for a well deserved victory, also to Powell Jones who no doubt, took inspiration from their victory. J. Powell Jones J. items.sum: Report of the Waddilove Trophy and Grenville Cup meeting at Birmingham, where Belgrave finished fourth.
items.s: WADDILOVE TROPHY Report of the Waddilove Trophy and Grenville Cup meeting at Birmingham, where Belgrave finished fourth. On July 24th we met at Euston and entrained for Birmingham for the Waddilove Trophy and Grenville Cup. I had hoped we would win the first mentioned trophy as on paper we had a good team but owing to injuries and other commitments we were not at full strength. However our lads acquitted themselves quite well and managed to gain fourth place in the competition. The outstanding performances were D.Merrett who returned 51.4secs for the quarter mile, J. Masters 9mins.28secs 2 miles run in 5th position and R. Holtum who reached the final of the 100 yards. We were accompanied by members of the L.O.A.C. who travelled with our party both ways and John Burr spent a good evenings entertainment with them learning to play cards. F.S. D. items.sum: A.D. Pyer reports on the boys' and youths' coaching scheme at Battersea Park, names promising boys, thanks the coaches, and gives the boys' and youths' medal competition score sheets.
items.s: BOYS' AND YOUTHS' COACHING SCHEME AND MEDAL COMPETITION A.D. Pyer reports on the boys' and youths' coaching scheme at Battersea Park, names promising boys, thanks the coaches, and gives the boys' and youths' medal competition score sheets. This scheme was inaugurated last year for the purpose of giving encouragement, advice and coaching to those of our younger members for whom there is little competition and who have a fundamental aptitude and liking for athletics. In particular, boys between the ages of 12 and 15 can be accepted for special coaching at Battersea Park on Sunday mornings at 11am. In this connection I should like to see the fathers of some of our boys, as I feel that if they too are interested, the boys will have that extra bit of encouragement to train and improve. So bring your fathers along with you as I would like to meet them. The future of the club depends largely on the success of this scheme as the boys of today will be our senior runners of to-morrow and with perseverance they can help to build up a section which will be second to none. Where a boy shows special ability over a period of time for a particular event, he will be passed on to Franz Stampfl our most able professional coach - a coach of champions and a champion of coaches. So far as the scheme has gone, it has been a pleasure to coach those who show real interest and I must say that we now have several boys showing promise of great things to come, most of them being school champions. Geoffrey Hall, 12 years, has good prospects as a middle distance runner having style, balance and for one so young, a remarkable sense of pace judgment as could be noticed when he won the boys' 880 yards on April 24th. A. English, 13½, is a natural long jumper and a promising high jumper. Malcolm Draper 13½, has aspirations to being a hurdler, following in his father's footsteps. John Martin, 12 years, is quite a performer in his age group and a tower of strength for his school, virtually winning the points cup on his own. Colin Clair, 13½, the winner of the boys' competition, a lad of forward development for his age, may well prove to be a good all rounder. K. Kirkman, winner of the Youths' competition, shows promise of developing in the jumps and javelin. To those who did not fare too well in the competition, I say keep at it, for some boys develop later than others. I would like to see more youths giving support to the competitions and I look forward to much better entries next year. A special word of thanks to the coaches who assisted in the scheme. To Franz Stampfl for his explanation of basic fundamentals of field events and advice on primary instruction. To George Isaacs for taking over the youths middle distance runners. To Cecil Brodie and Frank Simmons for sprint starts. To Charlie Jones for coaching in hurdling and to Jack Chappel for obtaining the shots and javelin. my apologies to the lads who were medal winners in the competitions that the medals were not available on Championship day The following results show that 9 youths and 11 boys took part in the competitions. This is about 25% of the eligible members of the club, so it is obvious that a large number of you are not taking advantage of the facilities offered. It is up to you to turn up on Sunday mornings during the winter and get yourselves fit for the next season when I look forward to much better entries. Remember, if you are not quite sure which branch of athletics you are fitted for, these competitions are designed to bring out the best in you. A.D.Pyer Age 880yds Shot L.J. H.J. 100yds. Jav. items.sum: First-person account of the Nijmegen Marches, with five Belgrave members in the Police team and the writer in the R.W.A. team.
items.s: NIJMEGEN MARCHES - 27TH - 30TH JULY 1954 First-person account of the Nijmegen Marches, with five Belgrave members in the Police team and the writer in the R.W.A. team. Belgrave were well represented in the Marches with five members in the Police team (Bob Readman, Syd Spencer, Len Demmon, Charlie McLennan and Don Fotheringham) and myself in the R.W.A. Team. Although at the time of writing, a couple of months have passed, I am still filled with awe and amazement at the wonderful organisation which made it possible for approximately 10,000 people young, old, military and civilian of all nationalities to be housed and made to feel as a huge family in a great concourse of good fellowship. I am sure these reactions must have been similarly experienced by our Police members. The enthusiastic way in which the whole of the surrounding population co-operate to make these walks a success and create the comradeship which is the keynote of this vast international assembly is something never to be forgotten. For general information there were about 600 British in the 10,000 taking part this year, consisting mainly of Army and RAF. units with two teams from the Metropolitan Police and one womens' and two mens' teams from the R.W.A., one consisting of S.W.C. and Stock Exchange members. Walks are graduated from 30 K.M. to 55 K.M. and the courses are roughly similar with detours to make up the varying distances. The Police do 50 K.M. and walk in semi-uniform while the R.W.A. teams do 55 K.M. per day for four days. Walks must start between set times and finish between certain limits which is arranged so that the total distance must be done inside 11 hours. In common with England it was pouring with rain when we arrived in Nijmegen, 11 o'clock at night, and taken by bus to our allotted digs where we were warmly welcomed by our Dutch hosts. The next day was spent in sightseeing and watching the arrival of the various units, the parachute detachments dropped from planes on to the river banks. In the evening we assembled and marched to the stadium where a magnificent and colourful march past and physical culture display was arranged. For most, to some degree this was marred by the rain but certain of our Police colleagues protecting a Policewoman under his cape seemed to think it had compensations. Each day of the walks was broadly similar. Up at 3 o'clock in the morning, wash, breakfast and wander through the town for 4 o'clock start. Cover about 25 K.M. to first break of ½ hour at a village cafe for sandwiches and drinks. March another 18 K.M. for a similar break and then on to finish. These are the bare elements to which must be added the natural interest of the country, the greetings of the teams, the cheers of the people, the village bands the flags and bunting, the obvious sincerity with which we and our troops were greeted and the wonderful colour and sound as girls, troops, etc. went along in their national colours and uniforms singing. We were soon known as the mad English on account of our many weird tastes for drinks and the distances we covered without stopping. Coupled with all this were the solemn memories of our paratroops as one crosses the great tributaries of the Rhine at Nijmegen and Arnhem. Needless to say each day we were the first civilian teams to finish, which enabled us to get a couple of hours sleep before dinner and the sightseeing in the evening. The events of the last day are nearly indescribable. The last five miles of route is lined many deep with people who carry bunches of flowers. The streets are decorated with flags and bunting while bands are playing all along the route. All traffic is stopped. To meet this enthusiasm everyone stops about 10 K.M. out, brightens up, puts on full uniforms, etc. unfurls their National flags and does their best, whatever their feet may feel like, to march as someone proud of themselves. I felt grand to be British and I feel that our troops lived up to the high esteem with which we are obviously held by the Dutch people. Needless to say both ourselves and the Police teams finished up looking like flower gardens. I hope the picture I have tried to give might encourage others to go next year so that we might even get a Belgrave team together, but although I found it a great experience I must add a word of warning. Do not attempt the Marches without you are a good stroller, perfectly fit and assured in your ability to do 34 miles at 4½ miles per hour for 4 days. Without this the Marches can become a sheer misery as they are on a team basis and the R.W.A. has a wonderful record that no man in any team sponsored by them has ever dropped out. In conclusion a word of praise must be given for the grand leadership and organisation of the R.W.A. President, Alf McSweeney who by his untiring efforts and judge of pace made the walks so enjoyable. H.W.Shields. items.s: OUR OPEN 20 MILES ROAD RUN Report of Belgrave's third annual open 20 miles road race at Wimbledon, won again by Geoff Iden, with Victoria Park Harriers taking the team race, Belgrave third, and Eric Gebbett winning the first Club 20 Miles Championship. Highlights of our third Annual Open 20 miles road running race were the thrilling finish when Geoff Iden raced past Bob Pape in the run in on the South Side retaining his title by three seconds, the very close team race in which the holders Victoria Park Harriers managed to beat Walton A.C. by a single point and the excellent performance of our long distance captain Eric Gebbett, who finished 8th in a strong field of exactly 100 competitors. The Mayor of Wimbledon, Councillor A. Withall, to whom we are deeply indebted for his keen interest in the race, started the runners off and Ford of Shaftesbury took the lead passing the five miles point closely followed by Pape and Goodsell in 27m. 51s. Geoff Iden, Harry Dennis and Waller of Coventry were 13 seconds back and our second claim member Byford - later to retire - followed in 28m. 37s. At this stage another second claim member, Jack Braughton, was just ahead of a large group of runners checked in at 29m.10s. which included Eric Gebbett, Len Adams, Ken Stimpson, Bert Jordan, and about another dozen runner. At Copse Hill Ford was forced to give way to Pape who hung on to the lead for the remainder of the race passing the 10 miles mark in 55mins. 51secs. and the 15 in 1hr. 24m. 15s. Pete Goodsell hung on to him for most of the second lap but Pape opened up a gap of nearly half a minute up Copse Hill. Iden was now moving up and was only one second behind Goodsell at 15 miles. Waller was also running magnificently, only to lose a considerable amount of ground in the last three or four miles. Eric, running with the Flowers twins and Ted Hefford of Woodford Green was showing excellent form and judgment and at 15 miles was well ahead of the next club runner. Len Adams however, running his first 20, was still moving very well and Ken Stimpson, running his first long distance race, was surprising everyone by his excellent showing and was still more than a minute ahead of Dennis Brickwood at 15. Dennis had, however, been hanging back, feeling that he lacked sufficient training, and moved up in the last few miles of the race. Wal Wortley showed a most welcome return to form and it was pleasing to see our late member Mick Porter, now of Manchester, in such good shape. we did however, suffer a severe misfortune when Bert Jordan retired with tendon trouble after 15 miles. Bert has been running really well this year and might well have assisted our team which was also without the support of Bob Plummer and Geoff Pearson. It was not quite clear what happened to Steve Charlton who, after a very restrained start, put in a terrific burst and then retired hurt. In the team race Goodsell was well backed by Ken Honney who finished 4th and Addington, but the Flowers at 6th and 7th just gained the victory for Victoria Park. Our own team was third and it gave us particular pleasure to see them placed in this, our own event. Held in conjunction with the Open race this year was our first Club 20 Miles Championship and the shield presented by Lady Fell in recognition of the close association of the race with Lauriston House, was won by Eric Gebbett, a first class effort for a young runner, in his first season of road racing. items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Walking notes celebrating Belgrave as national team champions, congratulating Norman Guilmant, Hugh McGreechan and George Checkley, urging winter training, welcoming new members and appealing for help with the Open Walk on 27 November. "BELGRAVE NATIONAL CHAMPIONS" With no apologies I start my notes with the above heading. by a combination of grand team work and individual effort, the lads have earned that title. For the first time since 1938 we hold the R.W.A. 20 miles and 50 kilometres Team Championships and during the summer have annexed every team award in distance events, finishing a grand and glorious season by winning the London - Brighton Walk with a record low score of 16 points. To Norman Guilmant our heartiest congratulations on winning the Manchester - Blackpool, 51¾ miles in a new record time and the London - Brighton Walk in 8hrs. 20. 44s, a time worth more than it seems in view of the prevailing weather conditions. To Hugh McGreechan we send the same greetings for a grand all round season capped by a splendid win in the Hastings - Brighton and a fourth in the London - Brighton, only just missing selection for the European Games. Also to George Checkley for his superb Dover-Canterbury and back win in a new record time for the 28 miles under atrocious weather conditions and his excellent first Brighton. These are only a few of the highlights which I am sure everyone - walkers and supporters - would not have missed for anything and what is more, enjoyed every minute of it. More anon of the races, but I hope and trust that the season just finished will inspire our younger members to follow, and equal, all that has been attained. Team work is the secret, without this we could not have attained such heights; hard work and success go hand in hand. The good fellowship, the helping hand and the leg pulling we have enjoyed are ample compensations for the trials and tribulations that come along. So I say, turn up on Tuesdays and Saturdays and enjoy training with the pack. Meet your fellow clubmen and I am sure you will capture the same feeling of TEAM SPIRIT besides helping youself to attain your own goal of a first class walker and a stylist. We have had a good attendance at Battersea Park during the summer and now that we have the finest athletic quarters of any London athletic club let us all take a share in its blessings. The Garnet Championshop and the National 10 will be won by training early and consistently together around Wimbledon this winter and once we start let us keep together and the enjoyment will be great. So all short distance men, come along on Tuesdays and Saturdays and prove that you can be equal to the distance men, they will be there to help you along. We also look to Don Brown who has fully earned a hearty vote of thanks for his work at Battersea during the summer. May he continue and benefit the lads during the winter at Wimbledon. At our A.G.M. the Road and Track Captains and Vice-Captains, with the exception of Eric Hall, were re-elected. Eric is a little uncertain of his business movements and Bill True was elected in his stead. All they need is your support during the next few months. By the time you are reading these notes we hope to have a winter strolling programme in full swing and we welcome each and everyone of you to join in. Your own counties will all be visited in turn to even out the travelling, so do come along and enjoy them, long and short ones, they are good - strolls, I mean. Besides strengthening up, they even further the education, if that is possible with some of us. Even I have learnt, by kind permission of H.M.Stationery Office, types and species of rhubarb and by the end of the winter I hope to be an authority on trees considering the lectures I receive. So do come along and join in, your comments and suggestions will be welcome. Since our last issue we welcome new lads to our fold; Ian Boss, Harold Burton, Dennis Ives, Patrick Maloney, Gordon Smith and Harry Stallard, also the return of Alf Joels who has resumed his membership. To all we say, may you enjoy your athletic career and cherish the day you joined our ranks. We still need to enrol more youngsters and I look forward to a good field for our "Olympic Cup" this year. Our 35th Open Walk will be held on 27th November and I appeal to everybody for help on this day. Those of you who are fortunate enough to possess cars can give invaluable assistance to enable judges and pointsmen to move round the course and I would be glad if all those who are willing to assist would let me know as soon as possible. For this great event, our PRIZE FUND is now open. It was started on the night of the Club Dinner by a very worthy member, and I welcome donations, large and small, to help us maintain our high standard of prizes. May I have many letters of acknowledgement to write, it will be a welcome task. Bernard Eglington was unfortunately sent abroad just a week before the Brighton Walk. We shall miss you Bernard. It was bad luck having to go a week before the Brighton after having scored in most of our team wins and I know you had set your heart on a 1st Class. We look forward to having you again with us on the road and until then we say "All the best". May I through these notes say a very sincere "thank you" to both distance and track men for your help and co-operation during the past year - a year of pleasant memories. I'm always emptying your pockets, I'm called all manner of names, but nevertheless I do appreciate your support and co-operation and so I say "My thanks to you all" Jack. This popular mid-week feature in the track programme was held on 14th June. Thirteen London Clubs entered a team and there were 85 starters in the four races, an excellent turn out for an evening meeting. Again we must congratulate Metropolitan W.C. on winning the team event with 158 points to Highgate's 156 and Belgrave 139. No club finished their eight starters, but as we lost Mcgreechan in the 5 miles and Bob Phillips in the 2, we were severely handicapped. George Checkley was 2nd in the 5 miles, Syd James 2nd in 4 miles, George Beecham 5th in 4 miles, up and coming Ray Middleton 4th and George Oliver 6th in the 3 miles and Len Demmon 4th in the 2 miles. This made up our total and we congratulate them on a fine effort. items.sum: Report of the National 50 kilometres walking championship at Hillsborough, Sheffield, where Belgrave won the team title.
items.s: NATIONAL 50 KILOS CHAMPIONSHIP - JUNE 17TH Report of the National 50 kilometres walking championship at Hillsborough, Sheffield, where Belgrave won the team title. This championship was held from Sheffield Wednesday F.C. ground at Hillsborough and this year there were four Swedish competitors. We were out to annexe the team title to go with our 20 miles title to make the double and right well did we do it. We started and finished a full team of eight, plus one individual out of a field of 61 finishers. With a long climb out of Sheffield, the lads set about consolidating their positions. At 5 kilos. Hugh McGreechan was 4th with the leading bunch, Norman Guilmant, George Checkley, George Beecham, Harry Shields and Bernard Eglington, in that order, not far behind. At 15 kilometres, Mac was in the lead in 81m.7s. with a whole bunch in close attendance, the other lads all going strongly, and at that time lying second in the team race with 43 points to Poly's 26, with Woodford 56, but our 5th and 6th men were in 17th and 18th positions respectively, packing for later stages as it turned out to be. After 20 K.M. Mac relinquished the lead and at 25 K.m. was 4th. Hereabouts, Norman had a bad bout of sickness and it says much for the way he came back and went right through the field again to finish a very creditable 14th to be our 2nd man home after being our 6th at one time. From 25 K.m. our lads all went through, making positions where others were dropping away and it was then we could see our second championship coming along. Looked after and urged on by a grand bunch of supporters - Bob Newson, Len Demmon, Billy True - they consolidated their positions and the scoring four of Mac, Norman, Bernard and Harry were ably backed up by George Checkley, George Beecham, Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday and Fred Rolfe, finishing positions being 6th, 14th, 17th, 19th, 26th, 30th 37th, 44th and 45th. With the elimination of the four Swedes from the individual positions, the result was:- Belgrave - 3.7.9.11. 30 points Poly H. - 2.6.14.18 40 " Woodford - 4.12.13.21 50 " A grand day followed by a late reception in Sheffield for the Swedish visitors and then the midnight train back to town. No one slept - that was not allowed - on a pleasant journey home to arrive at Kings Cross at 5am and wend our various ways home by various means. A day worth remembering, even at the loss of a pair of trousers. items.sum: Report of the Birmingham Outer Circle 25 miles walk, where Hugh McGreechan was second and Belgrave won the team race.
items.s: BIRMINGHAM OUTER CIRCLE 25 MILES - JULY 10TH Report of the Birmingham Outer Circle 25 miles walk, where Hugh McGreechan was second and Belgrave won the team race. Hugh McGreechan, Bernard Eglington, George Checkley and Harry Shields - just a bare team - plus myself as general factotum, travelled up to Birmingham for this popular event. The field was not so large as in previous years but the traffic was just as bad. After leaving Aston Villa Footbal ground, A. Johnson of Sheffield, went straight into the lead closely followed by Mac who stopped just behind him the whole way, never being more than 300 yards in arrears, and at the finish, a lap of the football pitch at Aston Villa, Mac had made ground to finish only 16 seconds behind in 3hrs. 48m. 3s. and 5mins. 19 secs in front of Bailey of the Poly. Johnson and Bailey had already been picked to go to Berne so one can see how unlucky Mac was to miss the trip, Bailey having pipped him in the last 6 miles of the 50 kilometres three weeks before. To illustrate how well he walked, after giving him a drink and sponge at 17 miles, telling him how the other lads were getting on and that he was a cert for the individual handicap, I waited for the others to come along and never caught up with him again. Bernard also had an excellent race to finish 5th in 3h.54m54s. his best time to date, a grand steady effort. George had a bad attack of tummy trouble and frightened the life out of me when I found he had disappeared for a while, but back he came to carry on and finish 9th in 4hrs. Harry had walked a steady race and although not on top of his form, finished 12th in 4h.4m.30s. The team race was always safe, at 8 miles we were 2.6.7.13; 17 miles 2,4,6,10; and at the finish 2,5,8,11, a total of 26 points, with Poly 2nd 41 points and Leicester 3rd 54 points. Mac duly obliged by winning the handicap with 15 minutes allowance and Bernard was 3rd with 25 minutes, so with 2nd in the scratch race and first team awards they collected quite a load. A fine effort which was duly celebrated on the train. It is interesting to note that in 1952 we were 3rd, 1953, 2nd and this year 1st. How's that for progress. items.s: DOVER - CANTERBURY and BACK - JULY 17TH Report of the Dover to Canterbury and back 28 miles walk in a gale, won by George Checkley in a course record. What a day, a howling gale, lashing rain the whole time the race was on and everybody agreed the worst day for some time to race in, making it even a finer performance on George Checkley's part to lead the whole way and smash the course record by over 9 minutes - 4h. 9m.42s. for 28 miles on a day like that, phew!! Norman, Harry and I had travelled in Alan (The Baron) Robin's car and the others had come down by coach - Bernard, Fred Rolfe, Doub and Percy Wilson. How thankful were the wife and I to be able to take advantage of Alan's car for looking after the lads and we all thank him most heartily for his help on such a dreadful day. From the start George cut out the pace and despite all entreaties about the homeward journey, carried on in the lead. Norman and Harry did not have a good race at all, perhaps the scrambled start had a lot to do with it as we arrived as they were getting ready to start, but with Norman plugging away and Bernard only a little behind, the team race was safe and we were able to concentrate on getting George home first now he was so near to the finish. After one stop on the homeward journey when he gave up all his lead he got going again to finish very strongly from J. Hubbard 2nd in 4.13.38 and Vic Stone 3rd in 4.15.10. At one time they were both within 200 yards of George but his strength over the windswept Barham Downs told its tale and he gradually got away. Norman finished 5th in 4.19.39, Bernard 8th, 4.24.58, Fred Rolfe 14th, 4.37.08, Harry 16th 4.38.29, Gordon 26th 4.55.46 and Percy 29th 4.59.42. Team result, three to score Belgrave 1.3.5. - 9 points, Woodford 17, Essex Beagles 27. George smashed the handicap time standard of 4h.10m with a time of 4h.9.42 and an allowance of 22 mins. This was George's score - Cup and prize for first man at turn; Cup and prize for whole distance; Individual handicap prize and shield and team prize. How he got home with them we don't know, but he deserved them for a grand effort. George Checkley George Checkley won, course record 4h. 9m.42s. for 28 miles Alan Robin Alan (The Baron) Robin drove to the race Fred Rolfe Fred Rolfe 14th, 4.37.08 Percy Wilson Percy Wilson 29th 4.59.42 J. items.s: HASTINGS TO BRIGHTON - AUGUST 14TH Report of the Hastings to Brighton walk, won by Mac with Belgrave taking the team race. This race saw the return to the Club of one of our war time members, Alf Joels and although he did not complete the distance it was obvious that with some training he can be an added strength to our distance men. Individual honours seem to be going round. First Norman's win in the Manchester to Blackpool, then George Checkley's success in the Dover - Canterbury and now it was Mac's turn. Winning by four minutes from Norman Guilmant in the time of 6h. 0m.37s. he returned the second fastest time of the race. The backing of Norman and George Checkley, 2nd and 4th positions respectively, gave us a score of 7 points, which must be practically unbeatable unless some club can finish with the first three positions. George Beecham was 9th, Bernard 10th, Fred Rolfe 14th, J. Wilson 18th, Gordon Doubleday 24th. The performances of our walkers in the earlier distance races ruled out any chance of a place in the handicap, but everyone came home well satisfied and full of confidence for the Brighton Walk. Team placings were: Belgrave 7 points, Essex Beagles 31 points, Surrey W.C. 42 points. items.sum: Report of the London to Brighton walk, won by Norman Guilmant with Belgrave winning the team race in a record low score.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON - SEPTEMBER 11TH Report of the London to Brighton walk, won by Norman Guilmant with Belgrave winning the team race in a record low score. Our confidence for success in the London Brighton Walk was amply justified for not only did we win the team race easily and in a low record score of 16 points, thus becoming the only club to win twice since the war, but also supplied the individual winner in Norman Guilmant. As stated earlier, we were without Bernard Eglington, but nevertheless we started two teams, 8 and 4 respectively backed up by a swarm of supporters at Big Ben which increased considerably as we moved towards Brighton. Our lads soon began to show their paces and there was little doubt throughout the race as to the ultimate result. Thompson of Met. W.C. only 21 years of age, set up a terrific pace and by the time Crawley was reached had open up a gap of over 8 minutes. Norman Guilmant however did not appear to be at all disturbed and gradually piling the pace on, in the next 4 miles reduced the lead by 1½ minutes. With a little gentle persuasion he then really started to move and by the time the top of Dale Hill was reached had taken a lead which he was never to lose. Thompson very pluckily kept his position and finished 2½ minutes behind Norman. Meanwhile the rest of the team were coming through remarkably well and the race developed more into a club affair as to who was going to be in the winning team. This eventually proved to be the four who had been most consistent throughout the summer, viz; Norman 1st. Hugh who had been 4th nearly all the way, in that position, George Checkley on his first Brighton 7th and Harry 9th. eliminating the individuals, their score was reduced to 16 points which looks as though it will stand for a good few years. Our "A" team which also included George Beecham (11th) Fed Rolfe 25th, Doub, 33rd and Joe Wilson 34th, had six men home before any other club had completed their four. George Beecham walked an excellent first Brighton to gain a first class standard and Rolfe, Doub, and Joe Wilson gained 2nd class standards, as also did Alf Joels who was in the "B" Team. Ron Fairman failed to finish the course so our "B" team did not close in. Final team placings were 1. Belgrave 16 points, Poly H. 45 points, Essex Beagles 75 points. Our thanks are due to the band of attendants on cycles and in cars who looked after our lads and helped them on the way.
