items.s: FIELD EVENTS Field events captain's season review: honours badges, younger members, thanks to officials and winter coaching under Franz Stampfl. Let me first congratulate the Field Events Section on the good performances during the season and the good feeling shown to one another. Your Captain P. Luxon has had a good season not only for the Club but for his County and he has also represented the AAA. Five honours badges have been won for A.A.A. standards by P. Luxon, P. Porter, R. Liggins, D. Patrick and J. Key, the latter with a Southern Youths Long Jump record of 21 feet 9 ins. a fine performance for a lad. It was very pleasing to see John Briggs come all the way from Liverpool to compete in the Club Hurdles Championship. Our younger members are progressing very rapidly, in particular Choate, Strang and Windley are all doing well. I would particularly like to thank Mr. O'Hara and all the field events officials who have given so much help. I must remind all members that arrangements are being made for coaching, under Franz Stampfl, to go on during the winter months and I sincerely hope that you will all take full advantage of it. Details are published in the Handbook and if any further information is required I know Frank Simmons will be pleased to supply it. There is still plenty of room for improvement and the winter is the time to make it and thus help to make next season more successful still than the one just finished. Jack Chappell. P. Luxon P. items.s: ROUND THE TRACKS Track season round-up, starting with the Heathfield Trophy at Stompond Lane, Walton. HEATHFIELD TROPHY - June 12th In this contest at Stompond Lane, Walton, although we proved superior to all other clubs on the track it was one of the rare occasions during the season when the field events men did not add their quota of points which enabled Walton A.C. to win by 4 points. The outstanding race of the day was no doubt the 880 yds in which Bob Taylor came up against Gordon Pirie who he had recently defeated over the same distance. This time however Pirie beat Bob by four yards in the time of 1m. 53s. both runners beating the track record of 1m55s. set up by Bill Nankeville. Bob's time of 1.53.6 was a new club record and a personal best. Another personal best time was that of Len Bishop who returned 4m. 21s. in finishing 3rd in the mile. D. Merrett finished 3rd in both sprint finals and Jock Cameron was 2nd in the 440 yards with C. Walker 4th in the 2 miles. T. Gaworski's 3rd place in the shot was the sole success of the field events men. In the Surrey Medley Relay at the same meeting, Belgrave finished 3rd behind South London and Farnham A.C. SOUTHERN COUNTIES CHAMPIONSHIPS - JUNE 19TH Our wealth of sprinters was fully demonstrated in the Southern Championships at Croydon when, out of the six competitors to reach the final of the 220 yards, three of them were Belgrave. Alan Sexton was inches behind Groves to finish 2nd although he had won his semi-final in a much faster time of 21.7s. D. Merrett was 4th and I Mayers 5th. Ivan was also 4th in the 100 yards. P.Luxon with a jump of 22 feet 4ins. in the Long Jump gained 2nd place to K. Wilmhurst the international, and T. Gaworski with a throw of 133ft 6 ins. was second to J. Savidge in the discus. Eddie Short was very unlucky in the steeplechase. He was lying second when he twisted his foot at the water jump with two laps to go and had to retire. KINNAIRD MEETING - June 28th Our field events men were very much to the fore in the Kinnaird Meeting at the Polytechnic Ground at Chiswick when two of them broke existing club records. P. Luxon cleared 22 feet 11[illegible] inches in the long jump beating the old record by 3¼ inches. T. Gaworski put the shot 44 feet 3 inches, adding 3 inches to his previous best. A.E.C. Inter-Club Trophy - July 3rd This contest between ourselves, Shaftesbury Harriers, Thames Valley Harriers, Southall A.C., Polytechnic Harriers and Finchley A.C. resulted in a win for the club with 55 points. Basil Walden won the 100 and 220 yards, Bob Walton won the 440 yards with Jock Cameron 2nd, I Badiali finished 3rd in the 880 yards and Ray Tooby was second in the three miles. P. Luxon proved his versatility by finishing 4th in this event and winning the long jump with 21ft 8ins. On the same day in the Viking Trophy 2 miles team race at Weybridge several of our leading distance runners were not available and the trophy was lost to Thames Valley Harriers. The team finished 3rd with C. Roffey in 4th position, J. Masters 5th and E. Short, running with an injured ankle, 11th. L.C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS In the South Western Area Championships held at Tooting Bec on 17th July all four finalists in the 100 yards were Belgrave members and the finishing order was R. Holtum, R. Bartlett, P.Cornish, and D. Gordon, the winner doing 10.5s. Holtum also won the 220 yards in 23secs. Bartlett being 3rd. P. Cornish gained another 3rd place in the 440 yards and Jim Heathfield was second in the 880 yards. Jim Masters ran well in the three miles but did not have sufficient speed at the finish and finished 2nd to J. Butler of Surrey A.C. Charlie Smart was third well ahead of the rest of the field. T. Gaworski and P. Luxon were successful in the shot and long jump respectively. In the junior events J. Pettican won the mile and T. Moxam was 2nd in the 100 yards. The finals were held at the new Hurlingham Track on 11th September with the added attraction of the track being officially opened by Roger Bannister. Track performances were seriously affected by the track being rain sodden. This was obvious from Jack Brown's mile which he won in 4m. 23s. Ron. Holtum did 10.3s in the 100 yards and 22.8s. in the 220 yards to finish second in each. T. Gaworski and P. Luxon continued their string of good performances by winning the Long Jump and Shot Put. DORIS SHIELD CONTEST This was held at Alperton Track on August 14th between Thames Valley Harriers, Mitcham A.C. and ourselves. The main feature of this contest was the inability of the club, with the apparent material available, to turn out two competitors for each event. Those who turned up certainly gave of their best but there is no doubt we should have done much better had we been properly represented. Ron Holtum was 4th in 100 yards and I. Mayers 3rd in the 220, whilst in the 440 yards our two runners were 5th and 6th. Alan Bishop was our only runner in the 880 yards and could not gain a point but we did better in the mile which Cliff Roffey won in 4.24.8. Jim Masters won the two miles in 9m. 46.6s. but again he had no second string to support him. Ted Gaworski won the shot with 43ft. 6ins. and was 2nd in the discus, whilst Percy Luxon won the long jump, was 2nd in the high jump and 3rd in the javelin which was won by Ron Liggins with a throw of 167ft. 3ins. Final points were Mitcham A.C. 48 points, T.V.H. 45 points and Belgrave 40 points. Mitcham had to thank Brian Hewson for winning the 440 and 880 yards and then running the final half mile in the medley relay to turn a big deficit into a handsome victory. I can well imagine what some of our runners would say if they were asked to turn out in three events, although this should never be necessary if everyone put themselves out to turn up at inter-club matches. SENIOR AND JUNIOR MATCHES v CAMBRIDGE HARRIERS SOUTH LONDON HARRIERS AND ISLE OF SHEPPEY A.C. This meeting was held at Charlton Park and a typical end of the season atmosphere prevailed. Although those athletes present gave of their best, the general attendance was poor. As a result a number of our members had to perform more than should be necessary. Noticeable absentees were amongst our milers and two milers which casts a very poor reflection on a club such as ours whose strength is reputedly mainly in our middle distance runners as emphasised by our road relay performances. Bouquets must however be handed out to our field events men who from four events gained as many points as our track members could produce from ten races and particular mention is due to Ted Gaworski who most definitely earns the title of "Belgrave's best club man" His performances are always of an excellent standard and he rarely misses a match without good reason. In the sprints Mayers pulled off a first string double and Cameron and Badiali were 2nd in the 440 and 880 respectively. Jock also ran in the second string 220 and obtained 3rd place as also did Ian in the second string 440. Eric Bishop was 3rd in the mile and George Stace was similarly placed in the 2 miles event with his best performance to date. In the latter race we had Tom Carter in action and although his speed is not of former years his style is as good as ever. Percy Luxon was able to fit in a second string 100 yards amongst his field events and gained valuable points with a second place. Bare made one of his rare appearances in the high jump with 5ft. 10ins. but in doing so badly injured his leg. Ted Gaworski won both discus and shot and was ably backed up by John Powell Jones who was 3rd in each of these events. Percy Luxon, 2nd in the long jump and 3rd in the high jump, completed our scoring positions and we eventually finished second in the match with 70 points to Cambridge Harriers 86. S.L.H. were third with 52 and Isle of Sheppey 9. The less said about the Junior match the better. Only five of our lads appeared and we scored only 20 points. Cambridge won with 69, S.L.H. followed closely with 67 and Isle of Sheppey produced 40. Stephens ran well to win the 440 yards. Ashwood was 3rd in the 880. J. Powell Jones who also competed in the senior match, won the shot put and was 4th in the discus in which Glenn finished 3rd. It is realised that this meeting was held during the holiday period but surely a club of our size could produce better support than was forthcoming on this occasion especially from our junior ranks. It is bad for our prestige, it is an insult to the organising club and it is unfair to those members who do appear and are called upon to race two or three times. Unfortunately it seems to have become a habit amongst some of our members this year to boycott away matches even though they are within easy reach of town. MATCH v MET. POLICE, T.V.H. and EALING HARRIERS This annual meeting held as usual at Imber Court, on 28th August was favoured with good weather and the track was in good condition, but sad to relate the Belgrave team again practically failed to materialise and we finished the afternoon at the bottom of the points scoring. Those members who did put in an appearance, enjoyed a good lighthearted afternoon's sport at a venue which should, and it must admitted usually does, attract a full complement of performers. The 100 yards was the first event and we had to call on Stephens, one of our juniors and incidentally a glutton for hard work. His fourth place gained a valuable point. The mile which followed was won by Ingles of T.V.H. but Ray Tooby and Don McLean, both putting in a rare appearance, finished 2nd and 3rd. The quarter gave another opportunity for young Stephens to add to our score and this he ably did by securing 3rd place. John Burr, once more in action after a leg injury, finished 3rd in the three miles in one of his best times which augurs well for a good winter season and in this race we also had Alan Bishop, Edmunds and Tom Carter, this having become a weekly effort for Tom - just like old times. The 880 yards saw Roffey our only starter but unfortunately he lacked just sufficient pace at the finish to secure a place. An unusual event, the 120 yards hurdles, gave an opportunity for Coleman to show his paces but either the hurdles were a little too high or he was a shade off form for he left a trail of upset obstacles but nevertheless finished 3rd. The track events were completed by a 8 x 110 yards relay for which we just scraped a team together. We would have performed much more creditably if the distance had been some two miles or so for at least five of the legs. Incidentally we had as a spectator Fred Clay who is in London again and he was pressed into action in borrowed kit to make up this team and showed that with a little hard work he will again be an asset to Belgrave - "Press on Fred!! In the field events Ted Gaworski was again a tower of strength and brought off his usual double - what would we do without that man?. He was backed up by Powell Jones who is fast making his mark in senior competition. The event which added to our prestige the most was the two miles walk between Belgrave and the Police in which we filled all the leading positions with Brian Shepherd, Syd James and E. Smith taking the honours, but unfortunately this did not count in the match points or we may have avoided the ignominous last place. This was our last match of the season and it can hardly be said that we ended in a blaze of glory. Let us hope that the cross country fixtures will be better supported than the track have been otherwise we may as well content ourselves with "training sessions" only. items.s: ROAD RUNNING Road running section round-up of the 1954 road races, from the Mitcham 15 onwards, with Belgrave placings and times. MITCHAM 15 This was as usual the first race of the year and was held on January 9th. Denis Brickwood running in his usual manner, took Eric Gebbett, who was making his first appearance in long distance running, with him for the first twelve miles when Eric began to tire and Denis ran on to be fairly well placed and followed by Eric who had recovered to finish within standard time. Godfrey, running for the "B" team, ran a good race to beat the third "A" team man home. Times and placings: WIGMORE 15 This was held on March 27th and in it we saw R. Plummer, still running as an individual, show us some of his old form to finish 6th and also that Eric Gebbett was going to prove quite a useful addition to the road section. The team, though not the best we could field, finished 4th. Our placings and times were: BRIDGEWATER TO TAUNTON On April 3rd a small team travelled to Taunton for this annual ten miles road race and John Bromley ran very well to finish 6th in 53m. 49s. on such a hilly course. Our other performances were 37th, E. Gebbett 58.10; 48th. P.Childs 59.10; and Dave Hooper 60.29 which gave us 6th place in the team race. EASTER MONDAY This saw us as usual at three different venues on the same afternoon the first being at Maidenhead where, in the local 10 miles we provided the winner in Chas Walker in 54m. 57s and who was fairly well backed up by Stan Gawler 6th in 56.35 and E. Gebbett 18th in 58.20. We thus finished 2nd in the team race to Herne Hill. Our other runner to finish was J. McDonald, 27th in 60.40. The second venue was at Bognor again for a ten miles road race where we had A. Bedford 3rd in 50m. 29s. and C. Smart 4th in 51.07, but no third runner to complete the team. The third run was the Doncaster to Sheffield Marathon and in this C. Abberton finished 27th in 2hrs. 50m. 4s. with A. Jordan 32nd in 2.51.7 and W. Wortley 47th in 2.59.4. FINCHLEY 20 - April 24th This was the first of the season's twenties and we had a very small turn out as the Surrey 20 was to be held on the following Saturday, but we did see another grand performance by R. Plummer who finished 4th in 1h. 54m. 53s. Our only other runners to finish were A. Penstone 2.11.8.; and S. Charlton, in his first twenty, 2.13.0. SURREY COUNTY 20 - MAY 1ST This race was held at Mitcham and we saw Eric Gebbett continue to prove that he is a useful distance runner by finishing 9th in 1hr. 59m. 10s. in his first twenty to lead our team into 2nd place. He was well backed up by A. Jordan, 10th in 2.0.14 and G. Pearson 16th in 2.3.3., all within Southern Standard. C.Manning 23rd also gained Surrey County Standard with a time of 2.14.10. Team positions were as follows:- 1. Walton A.C. 16 points. 2. Belgrave H. 29 points. CHICHESTER TO PORTSMOUTH - MAY 1ST This race as usual, was blessed by fine weather in fact it was a bit too warm for road running. L. Adams in his first long race put up a good performance to finish 13th. E. Gebbett, feeling a little tired from the previous week, did not run to form and it was not until the last six miles that he showed anything like his normal running. Our placings and times were: We were placed 5th in the team race. SOUTHERN 20 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP - MAY 15TH The Championship was held at Chislehurst in conjunction with the Kent Open 20 miles and we finished 6th in the team race. R. Plummer as an individual, was again our first man home and we are waiting for the day when he will be eligible to run for the Club. E. Gebbett returned to form to put in another creditable performance but our other runners found the course rather a tough proposition. Placings and times were as follows: WALTON A.C. "15" - JUNE 12TH R. Plummer had yet another good run to finish 8th in 1hr. 24m. 41s. Our other performances were E.Gebbett 24th, 1.27.40; L. Adams 26th, 1.27.56; S. Charlton 30th, 1.28.28; J. McDonald 44th 1.33.57; A. Whitehead 45th 1.34.07; L. Rolls 1.38.44; A Smith 66th and J. Baker 68th. POLY MARATHON - JUNE 26TH This was held as usual from Windsor to Chiswick and we held our own Marathon Championship in conjunction in which R. Plummer carried off the title in a new championship time of 2 hours 39m. 53s. with A. Jordan 2nd in 2.46.49 and G. Pearson, the holder 3rd in 2.47.29. Others to gain Club standards were J. McDonald, 2.50.59 and C. Abberton 2.54.30. Placings in the Open race in which we finished 7th team were 24th. R. Plummer; 49th A. Jordon; 52. G. Pearson; 62. J. McDonald; 68. C. Abberton; 105. A. Mitchell and 111. A. Penstone. We also finished 5th in the Southern Counties Championship which was held in conjunction. We also had teams in the Peterborough Marathon and the Kodak 10 at Whitsun in both of which there were some good performances, especially at Peterborough where C. Abberton, A. Jordon and J. McDonald ran very well. Summing up the road season, it can be said that we are definitely improving. The most essential thing is to get a full turn out in EVERY race. In addition the great thing for roadwork is training and then more training and I should like to see ALL the road runners out together all through the winter, both on Saturdays and Tuesdays. If this is done I am sure we shall do much better next year. Road Captain. 15. D. Brickwood 1h. 27m. 02s. 84. L. Bush 36. E. Gebbett 1 29 30 89. A. Jordan 37. R. Plummer 1 29 31 92. L. Rolls 76. E. items.sum: Editor's report of the club's annual dinner and dance at the Oxford Street Corner House on 25 September.
items.s: THE ANNUAL DINNER AND DANCE Editor's report of the club's annual dinner and dance at the Oxford Street Corner House on 25 September. The placing of this report at the very end of the magazine is in no way meant to minimise the importance of this club function but as it was held only just prior to the magazine going to press, it was only just possible to include it and anyway it makes a very fine finale. This annual function still does not receive the support it deserves, but nevertheless 150 members, guests and friends assembled at the Oxford Street Corner House on September 25th and spent a very enjoyable evening. The dinner was excellent, the speeches were short and the dancing rounded off a very good evening, terminating with Auld Lang Syne and the President, Tom Morrell, being carried shoulder high round the room. He really deserved better support from the club, but as it was he was left in doubt as to his popularity. Ed. Tom Morrell Tom Morrell President Oxford Street Corner House

items.sum: Editorial on the completed reconstruction of Belgrave Hall, the Tommy Green Trophy award to Percy Luxon, poor handicap entries, the Open Walk and magazine circulation.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial on the completed reconstruction of Belgrave Hall, the Tommy Green Trophy award to Percy Luxon, poor handicap entries, the Open Walk and magazine circulation. Fellow Belgravians, Xmas has come and gone, a New Year has begun and by the time this magazine reaches you, the reconstruction work at Belgrave Hall will have been completed and I think everyone will agree that the new amenities are a worthy addition to the Club. Alf Harley, who probably knows more about the growth of Belgrave Hall than most of us, has contributed an article in the following pages which should prove interesting to every member. For the first time since the inception of the "Tommy Green" Trophy, given for the best club performance of the year, the Committee have awarded it to Percy Luxon for his Long Jump of 22ft. 11½ inches. Our Field Events members have made great strides in the past few years and the award of this trophy for a field events performance should be an incentive to even better achievements Despite the appeal in the last issue of this magazine for better support for club handicaps, the entries this year so far have been slightly less than last. Handicaps whether over the country, on the road, or on the track, are held to encourage the faster men to go even faster and to give the slower men an opportunity to improve and a chance to gain some small reward for their training. I know that Ron Holtum will be looking forward to considerable improvement when the track season starts. The Open Walk again proved a great success thanks to the hard work of Jack Goswell and his enthusiastic helpers. There is still a good number of members who are not taking the Belgravian and I hope that you will do your bit towards increasing its circulation. Your Editor. items.label: No. 121
items.sum: The new club President's message thanking members for electing him after 27 years of membership.
items.s: THE PRESIDENT'S MESSAGE The new club President's message thanking members for electing him after 27 years of membership. It surely must be the objective of every true Belgravian to one day become President of this famous Athletic Club, and so, after 27 years of membership, I have gained this coveted prize. I must therefore thank you all most sincerely for electing me to the most senior office in the club for the ensuing year. My efforts in the past have been only a small part in the efficient running of the club, the results have been reflected in the successes of the past and those that will surely follow in the future. The Club's crowning glory must be the rebuilding of Belgrave Hall, which is without doubt the finest headquarters of any purely amateur club in the country, and I urge you all to make full use of these fine amenities both for training and club social activities. May I conclude by wishing you and the Club all success for the future and so make my year of office my most enjoyable year in the Club. Tom Morrell. President. Tom Morrell Tom Morrell President; 27 years a member

items.label: No. 121
items.sum: History of Belgrave Harriers' headquarters from the club's founding in 1887 at the Kings Arms, Westminster.
items.s: THE HEADQUARTERS STORY History of Belgrave Harriers' headquarters from the club's founding in 1887 at the Kings Arms, Westminster. The Belgrave Harriers were founded in 1887 at an inaugural meeting held at the "Kings Arms", Ranelagh Road, Westminster and this house continued as the Club Headquarters for 12 years. In these days it was not uncommon for the sprint finals to be held on the Embankment at an hour approaching mid-night and it is said that the bookmakers were usually present in force. In 1899 a change was made to "King William 1V" nearby in Grosvenor Road and Cross Country Headquarters were booked at the "Railway Tavern", Battersea Rise, five minutes from Clapham Junction. This was as far as it was necessary to go in those days and the lonely marshy area south of the Thames - now largely Battersea Park - was no district to traverse with your wages in your pocket and a fog coming up. In 1903 the Club still retained its Westminster quarters but cross country running was now indulged in from the "Red Lion" Hotel, Barnes. About 1908 headquarters were moved to 180, Kings Road, Chelsea, and the cross country quarters were at the "Spencer Arms", Lower Richmond Road, Barnes. The Licensee here was Tom Sullivan - a well known man in the running world - who just before World War 1 went to Germany as Chief Rowing coach and laid the foundations of this sport in Germany. He continued this work for many years and died comparatively recently at a ripe old age. His departure to Germany meant another change for the Club, and headquarters were established at the "Surprise" Tavern, Christchurch Terrace, Chelsea, with cross country quarters at the Raynes Park Hotel and track facilities were arranged at Stamford Bridge and Battersea Park Cricket Pavilion and ground. In 1919-20 we used Cain's Hall, Battersea and Pepys House, Westminster as headquarters with Raynes Park Hotel for cross country, but Ashcombe A.C. reviving after the war, asserted their right to their old premises and again we were on the move. This time we alighted on familiar ground and in 1920-21 our cross country runners and walkers stripped off in the skittle alley - now the long lounge bar - at the "Swan" in the Ridgway, Wimbledon. The following season we rented St. John's Hall, Denmark Road, around the corner, changing the name to Belgrave Hall when we acquired the leasehold in 1938. In 1922 our head-quarters were nominated as being at Wimbledon and we were fortun-ate in finding mid-week quarters at the "Rising Sun", Ebury Bridge Road, S.W.1. which were enjoyed until 1938 and contributed much to the Club's successes during this heart warming period that we enjoyed for ten years and more before war again overtook us. Many will remember the very primitive conditions prevailing at the "Rising Sun", but with much pleasure they will recall the training and the joking that went on, the comradeship and enthusiastic club spirit which was such a driving force in all our endeavours. The coming of the war restricted our activities to the Wimbledon headquarters which remained open throughout and were a rallying point for athletics and all athletes throughout those difficult six years. On resuming full scale activities, we enjoyed midweek hospitality at the Duke of Yorks Headquarters and were able to attain one of our greatest ambitions, the pur-chase of the freehold of Belgrave Hall, and contemplate the improved amenities we had so long desired. But to hark back to the days following the first World War. Gradually the Club, which had almost gone out of ex-istence for four years, gathered strength and a small cash reserve was built up. It was always thought - but it seemed so far off no one dared to mention it - that this might be the neuclus of a fund to endow our own headquarters in the far off future. Baths at Wimbledon were of the galvanized zinc variety with hot water strictly rationed and everbody contributed, midweek as well as Saturdays, to the "hot water" money appeal. In 1930 our total re-serves were about £500 and although many had shared in accumulating this sum, the late Bob Ricketts, Harry Hare and Wally Bayliss had played the major part. In 1932 Harry Hare launched the "halfpenny" saving scheme and our funds grew apace. Briefly the scheme called on members never to spend a halfpenny but to retain them and pass them over to the Club. Teddy Gordon provided some building brick money boxes in which the surplus halfpennies could be placed each evening. Frank Elson came along with a scheme based on football results which added to our funds and was succeeded by a more ambitious scheme still, organised by Frank Elson and Tom Cotton and assisted by Teddy Gordon and a host of other enthusiasts. In 1938 we acquired the leasehold of Belgrave Hall as it was now renamed and our reserves approached £2,500. In 1941 Les Cohen took over our moneymaking schemes, reframing them on even more ambitious lines and rapidly our available cash reserves increased and the funds available for our normal club activities were also supplemented. No words of praise can be too high for the work of Les Cohen (and of Mrs. Cohen who has also rendered great assistance) and of the many hundreds of willing supporters who placed us in such a strong position financially. This work, fortunately for us, still continues. In 1950 we took over the freehold of our headquarters and were then free to add to the amenities and comforts of the hall, when the necessary building permits could be obtained. The battle for licences was long sustained and eventually were in a position to go ahead. As a result we have a two storey addition at the rear end of the hall. Seven showers have been installed with the necessary water heating and storage plant, six hand basins, foot baths and adequate lavatory accommodation are there for the conven-ience of our members and visitors. A servery is supplied from a well equipped kitchen above and also on the first floor is a ladies waiting room and a committee room. An iron stairway externally leads to the first floor and an inner wooden stairway also leads to the first floor. Visitors from other clubs have commented on the splendid facilities now available to the club, as have older members who remembered the very inadequate allowance of hot water once provided, which was paid for out of pence collections and not provided gratis as now. We are not, of course, completely satisfied with the improvements made, nor is it likely that we shall ever be. In the course of time we should like to redesign and rebuild our main hall nearer to the heart's desire, but first we must pay for our present improvements. These will cost more than our total funds in reserve and will leave us in debt for a while, but we are quite confident that the old Belgrave spirit will arise and enable us to clear this off and prepare for our next step forward. The spirit which has built so much from such little beginnings is not likely to forsake us now and we certainly have something definite and visible to the eye to inspire us towards generosity and even harder work for Belgrave in the future. In conclusion it must be said that this major step forward of ours is a victory for team spirit and love of club which can scarcely be rivalled anywhere in the world. So many have shared in the effort which has been continuing for over 30 years; so many who must remain nameless have contributed to our ideals and the translations of them into reality. We are confident that our members of the present and of the future will respect their great inheritance and prove more than worthy of it and the trust reposed in them. A.A.H. A.A.H. A.A.H. items.s: UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT Notice that Ernie Duffett's team-selection work is now split between Cross Country and Track Secretaries, asking members to return a track questionnaire. For a number of years the running sections of our club have depended on Ernie Duffett's knowledge of what everyone is doing - and can do - for the naming of teams for our fixtures. We no longer have Ernie Duffett in this more than active position in the administration of the club and as you all know, his work has been split up into the duties of Cross Country and Track Running Secretaries. Over the country, team selection is simpler by virtue of the fact that on any one day there is normally only one event at the one distance. On the track the number of nominations for a meeting are often limited and it has been found that runners' names have been omitted from programmes and runners who are not available have been included. In order to avoid this sort of thing and to help your new Track Secretary and Captain, a questionnaire has been compiled. A copy is included with this Belgravian and further forms are available for members not yet subscribing to our mag-azine. From the framing of the questions, you will see what we want to know. Don't forget to use the remarks column if you have anything to add. Please fill in the form and see that it is passed to one of the following:- Track Hon.Sec. R.D.Holtum, 26, Wandsworth Bridge Road, S.W.6. Track Capt. F.Simmons, 69, Monkton Street, S.E.11. Track V/Capt. J.Burr, 46, Rylett Road, W.12. then we can from the replies received, work out an acceptable programme of fixtures for the 1955 track season - one at which teams worthy of the name "Belgrave" can be expected to attend. The track season will soon be here, don't delay, send those forms in straight away. Ron. Holtum. Ron. Holtum Ron. Holtum Ernie Duffett Ernie Duffett formerly named the club's running teams R.D. items.label: No. 121
items.sum: The Track Captain's message looking ahead to the 1955 track season and asking for support, especially from distance runners.
items.s: THE TRACK CAPTAIN'S MESSAGE The Track Captain's message looking ahead to the 1955 track season and asking for support, especially from distance runners. The track season is steadily drawing near and as Track Captain my thoughts are turning towards the summer evenings and wondering what kind of support I can count on. I know I am safe with our Field Events lads and also the sprinters, but I am not quite happy about the longer distance chaps, maybe they have thought they do not get the appreciation they deserve. Fixtures are already being arranged and it appears we will have a busy season ahead of us. There will be runs, jumps and throws for everybody, my job is to see that you get some competition at whatever you want to do. I will try very hard for this but if the referees will not allow more to run in a race than those who are nominated, I cannot do anything about it. Always turn up, even if you are a reserve, and bring your kit. Don't be disappointed if you finish last, someone has to be last and I will appreciate your running whatever you do, because I will know you have had a good try. We can't all win, but I know your turn will come. Some of our fixtures will mean a bit of travelling but as in all sports, the same thing applies to your opponents when they visit you and it is only politeness to attend your away fixtures in the strength at which you attend your home ones. You elected me as your Captain, please make it worth my while contin-uing to try and make a success of the job. I know I have a habit of saying what first comes to my mind, but that is me and I would be false to myself and to you if I tried to be different. Those of you who were at the A.G.M. know of the conditions under which I accepted the office. They still hold good as far as I am concerned. Good luck and best wishes during the coming season. F. Simmons. F. Simmons F. Simmons Track Captain

items.label: No. 121
items.sum: Report of the annual meeting of cross country enthusiasts, covering captain Eddie Short's policy, training venues and the place of youths and juniors.
items.s: CROSS COUNTRY 1954-55 Report of the annual meeting of cross country enthusiasts, covering captain Eddie Short's policy, training venues and the place of youths and juniors. What I hope will be a permanent feature of every cross country season is the annual meeting of cross country enthusiasts. To date, to my knowledge there have been two. Briefly the idea behind it is to give the Captain a chance to issue his statement of policy, to invite suggestions and to stimulate discussion. On this last item, it saves, or should do, club business becoming the property of every club within running distance of Tooting Bec or other focal points. I say that it should do, but from my experience it has not been the case. Team selections, before they have even become official, have been the common property of all and sundry. The meeting this season, held on the same day as the Club Three Miles, was better attended than the previous year. We were pleased to have the Club President with us and it was good to see a sprinkling of youths and juniors. Firstly, because it is the most important aspect of the season, the Captain, Eddie Short, gave us a concise idea of his hopes and aspirations. Club spirit was the essential quality required and how could it be resurrected?. The answer was to give the members a break; keep them informed; give them interesting programmes etc. The Captain then got down to training and it was agreed that training could not be done by everyone at the same place; there would have to be two venues, Wimbledon (Club H.Q.) and Tooting Bec Track. Method was then talked about and I found a little uncertainty here. Not by Eddie Short - he went flat out for midweek training at Tooting Bec, fast and slow, fast runs of a quarter or thereabouts and duration variable according to the season's programme. Generally it was agreed that their would be differences in members training according to their number of days training. Perhaps the issue was "miles" or "speed" - perhaps a combination of both. The question of what should be done on the Saturday run was the final matter on training. Surprisingly enough the only possible answer - a pace run - was provided by Bill Lucas, never more than a lukewarm enthusiast. Next on the agenda was the youths and juniors and what part they had to play in the club. There seemed to be a mystery of "Where do the under 21's go in the winter time". I suppose a good many of them, to the Services. The youths them-selves said a few words and how I agreed with them. They wanted interest; they wanted an experienced man to take them out on Saturdays. It was at this stage it was made known that Charlie Smart and Len Marchant were prepared to help in any connection. It had been previously mentioned that whoever took the lads out would have their hands full with a quartet such as Braine, Flanagan, Chevalier and Dabbs. Both Charlie and Len are well known and experienced, so make the most of it. The fixtures which had been circulated provision-ally, were discussed and everyone seemed agreed that they were suitable. The Secretary explained that the fixtures with Surrey A.C. and Herne Hill were planned to avoid unnecessary travelling and so encourage a big turn out. It was also mentioned that all fixtures were for seniors, juniors and youths. As the Secretary of the Cross Country, I made the plea put out by all Secretaries - PLEASE ANSWER THE CARDS WHICH ARE SENT TO YOU - please let me know what you are doing and where you are. The meeting closed with some people enlightened, some satisfied, a certain coach bewildered, but above all, every one, with one exception, confident that we were dur for a better season. items.sum: Appeal for volunteers to help Arthur Whitehead mark cross country courses on the Common, noting Gordon Biscoe's direction arrows.
items.s: MARKING CROSS COUNTRY COURSES Appeal for volunteers to help Arthur Whitehead mark cross country courses on the Common, noting Gordon Biscoe's direction arrows. Owing to the mass of tracks on the Common and the great number of people about, the task of course marking is probably more difficult than anywhere else in the country. Our members may be expected to know the routes normally used, but visiting runners cannot do so and in no race this season have we had the individual leader to guide the way. Added to these diffifulties is the fact that the marks put out are invariably tampered with by children, false trails being frequently laid and regular helpers are badly needed to assist Arthur Whitehead in this arduous task. Would volunteers please come forward? Please do not wait until you are asked. Nobody likes to worry you in case they might be trespassing too much on your good nature. Only YOU can say whether you have the inclination and opportunity to help your club in this essential way. Gordon Biscoe has done a wonderful job in making a great number of direction arrows and, with the many flags available, all that is needed is the requisite helpers. In addition to markers, pointsmen are also often needed and everyone who is not actually competing, can help by running his training round the marked course and so keeping an eye on the flags and arrows. Arthur Whitehead Arthur Whitehead course marker Gordon Biscoe Gordon Biscoe made direction arrows for course marking

items.h:
LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY - SOUTHERN CLUBS
October 9th 1954
items.sum: Report of the 1954 London to Brighton Relay for southern clubs, won by Herne Hill Harriers from Thames Valley Harriers with Belgrave third, with a leg-by-leg account of Belgrave's runners.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY - SOUTHERN CLUBS October 9th 1954 Report of the 1954 London to Brighton Relay for southern clubs, won by Herne Hill Harriers from Thames Valley Harriers with Belgrave third, with a leg-by-leg account of Belgrave's runners. Following the post war precedent of last April, this race was again started from Westminster and it would appear that unless some unforseen circumstance arises, the original full course will continue to be used. A new name, Herne Hill Harriers, was added to the ever growing list of clubs who have won this race and although their win was described by a leading journalist as being unex-pected, there can be little doubt in the minds of those who have closer contact with Herne Hill that they went to the starting post with something more than an excellent chance of success. A quick perusal of their entry was sufficient to see that they had a well balanced team with above average athletes such as Mick Maynard and Jack Heywood to weigh the balance in their favour. And so it proved for they romped home with almost two minutes to spare from Thames Valley Harriers with Belgrave third a further forty seconds behind. As far as the race itself was concerned, there was very little to cause great excitement amongst the leading positions for after the first three legs, Herne Hill had built up a reasonable lead which they continued to widen on the 6th to 9th stages until they had almost three minutes to spare. Thames Valley had run themselves into an almost certain 2nd place by the fourth stage and Belgrave never really looked like being deprived of 3rd position although first Blackheath and later Essex Beagles, caused us some anxiety. Thus it will be seen that the race had developed into a procession, with the greater battles for position amongst the lesser lights. Charlie Walker performed quite creditably on the first leg to give us third place. John Bromley kept this place on the run to Mitcham although having to give way to Herne Hill who moved up into 2nd place. I thought John looked a little slug-ish and in need of a race or two to pep up his pace. Charlie Smart on the third stage gave of his best and once again produced an excellent performance for a man of his age. Our new Cross Country Captain, Eddie Short, then took over at Purley for the long grind to Earlswood and I suppose no one could wish for a less envious task than to chase Alec Olney of T.V.H. who must be considered one of the best road runners of all time. Nevertheless Eddie stuck to his task and although losing ground on the leaders, maintained our 3rd position. Denis Brickwood, who came into the team at the last minute due to Chris Roffey being unfit, again took the Redhill stage but unfortunately had to contend with Withers of Blackheath, a very promising performer who produced the fastest time of the day on this leg and in so doing took his team into 3rd place. Ray Tooby, looking most casual in his running and no doubt obeying the orders of his coach, kept our 4th place on the sixth stage at the end of which we were over two minutes behind the leaders. We were however still hopeful of a recovery for Jack Brown had been entrusted with the long leg to Handcross. Unfortunately he was not in his usual devastating road form, perhaps due to lack of racing in the weeks prior to this race. Jack was also in the invidious position of having two first class athletes in the persons of Mick Maynard, Herne Hill, and Ingles of T.V.H. ahead of him and not even in sight. When Len Herbert took over at Handcross, we were again third, but over three minutes in arrears. Len set about his task in his usual workmanlike manner but fireworks cannot be expected from the over forties in races such as this and he had to give further ground and it was certain when he arrived at the Castle at Hickstead that 2nd was the best position for which we could hope. The 9th stage had been given to John Burr running in his first Brighton and so well did he run that he produced the best time of the day on this leg - definitely an encouraging start to what should be a long career on the Brighton Road. Archie Bedford on the 10th also did the fastest time of the day and brought us within striking distance of T.V.H. but Len Bishop on the last leg could make no impression on Eddie Ellis, T.V.H's International Steeplechaser, and the positions remained unchanged to the end. Once again it was forcibly brought home to us that we have too many old men in our team and that until we can produce at least two above average runners who can hold their own with the leading athletes on the long six mile stages, we must resign our-selves to taking lower positions. Next April when we compete in the National Relays, we shall have to contend with the star studded South London Team in addition to this rapidly improving Herne Hill side and the strong opposition of T.V.H. We must in the meantime find new blood, possibly in the form of Jumbo Masters and Ron Linstead to strengthen our team and replace our veterans who must inevitably become slower with each succeeding race and who have borne the brunt of this race for so long. items.label: No. 121
items.sum: Manager's report of Norman Guilmant and Vic Stone representing Great Britain in the international 100 km walk at Lecco, Italy, on 4 November 1954, where they finished 4th and 2nd behind Sweden's Ljunggren.
items.s: INTERNATIONAL 100 Km. WALK - ITALY 4-11-54 Manager's report of Norman Guilmant and Vic Stone representing Great Britain in the international 100 km walk at Lecco, Italy, on 4 November 1954, where they finished 4th and 2nd behind Sweden's Ljunggren. Our Long Distance Walking Champion Norman Guilmant, was once again selected to represent Great Britain in this Inter-national walking race of just over 60 miles, his co-competitor being Vic Stone of the Poly H. whilst our old friend "Timber" Woodcock of Surrey W.C. accompanied them as Manager and we are indebted to the latter for this report on the race. The party left London at mid-day on Monday, 1st of November and arrived in Milan at mid-day on Tuesday in a minor heatwave, moving on to Lecco, the venue for this year's race, the following morning. The time in Milan was spent sightseeing, coupled with Vic Stone doing his utmost to purchase a collar stud, but apparently such things are unknown in Italy. This was slightly co-incidental as just before leaving, Vic had been awarded the "Studd" Trophy. Lecco turned out to be a holiday centre on Lake Como and all agreed that it was a fine town, Norman being partic-ularly interested in the postcards (don't ask what kind). In the afternoon our two competitors attended a medical examination required by the promoters of the event. Then followed vetting of permits to compete, issuing of numbers and allocation of attendants, all quite a business. One interesting point at this stage was that each competitor had a wire fixed to his wrist with a lead seal bearing his number in the race (rather like the pigeons). This is done so that there can be no question of a substitute imper-sonating a competitor during the race. All these formalities having been completed, we returned to our hotel for a meal and linked up with Brian Morris, Met. W.C. who had taken a few days holiday to see the race. He managed to get hold of a cycle which later proved very useful. Finally we worked out a system of sign language with the two attendants allotted to Norman and Vic for the next day and turned in at an early hour as we had to be up at 2am for a 4 o'clock start. Norman proved a great asset to the party as far as food was concerned, having brought his own grape fruit and bacon for breakfast which proved to be sufficient for the whole party. We could have had porridge as well if only we could have made the locals understand what it was and how to make it. The day of the race, 4th November, we learned is the Italian Armistice Day and a national holiday. This resulted in large crowds collecting all along the route and at times causing some difficulty to the competitors, both Norman and Vic having to elbow their way through the crowd at some points, whilst at the finish there was a crowd of about 30,000 held back by crush barriers. And so to the race. There was a field of 59 competitors from six countries, Great Britain 2, France 2, Holland 1, Sweden 3, Switzerland 3 and Italy 47. The course was completely different to last year and in addition to being more difficult, the weather conditions were against the competitors. The race started at 4am in a cold damp mist which lasted seven hours but when it cleared, the temperature rose quickly to 70. At 5Km. the lead had been taken by Charriere (Switz) Norman was walking in a bunch of six in 3rd place, with Vic Stone in 15th position. Charriere continued to walk very fast and at 15 Km. led by 4 minutes. At Seregno, 33Km. the field began to open out but Charriere was still leading in 3hrs 18mins. followed by Ljunggren (Sweden), Soderland (Sweden), Mazza (Italy), Guilmant (G.B.) 3hrs. 24mins. with Vic Stone 6th in 3hrs 28mins. About this time the cold mist began to affect some of the walkers and some changes took place and at 44 Km. Ljunggren had taken the lead with Norman and Vic still in the same positions, 4th and 6th. At Monza, 59Km. Ljunggren passed in 5hrs. 58mins. and while Vic Stone had come up to 4th position in 6hrs. 13 mins. Norman had dropped considerably to 8th, 5 minutes behind Vic. Usmate, 71Km. was passed by Ljunggren in 7hrs. 25 mins. and although Soderland was still 2nd, he was troubled with cramp in his legs and was being rapidly overhauled by Vic Stone who was now in 3rd place. On reaching Airuno, 85Km. Vic had gone up to 2nd place, and Norman who had recovered from a bout of sickness, had moved up to 5th place. Over the remaining 15 Km. Ljunggren maintained his lead but Vic Stone reduced the lead by a further 8 minutes. A. Reste, Italy, came through well over the final stages to beat Norman for 3rd place. 36 competitors finished the course with the two Englishmen 2nd and 4th. Placings and times:- 1. J. items.label: No. 121
items.sum: Walking notes appealing for members' contributions, urging training on the club courses, praising Eric Hall, Bob Newson and Len Demmon, and asking for helpers for the National 20 miles to be staged from headquarters on 4th May.
e: Union of London Walking Clubs match
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Walking notes appealing for members' contributions, urging training on the club courses, praising Eric Hall, Bob Newson and Len Demmon, and asking for helpers for the National 20 miles to be staged from headquarters on 4th May. Time passes very quickly and once again I have to pen some notes for a worried editor. I am going to start with an appeal to you all, and that includes every member of the Club. Please help your Editor and the Sectional Secretaries by sending YOUR contribution to YOUR magazine. Some of you see more of the events on the road and across the country, than the officials who are organising them as they are often far too busy to take note of what is going on round the course. In addition it would make a marked addition to the variety of the magazine articles if they come from different members of the club. Also perhaps some of you would like to start a discussion on some of the aspects of the club, which could be continued or answered in a following issue. Judging by the noise that goes on in the dressing rooms and under the showers, there should be plenty of material to write about, so why not get down to it and not leave it to the few for the next issue. And now back to Walking. Since the winter pro-gramme has started our lads have taken heart from their distance successes and have really begun to show up well. Gradually they have moved up to make their presence felt in the Open 7's. With the backing of a few more, who have been conspicuous by their absence, right well will the Belgrave colours be at the front when the Championships start. I have said before that Championships will only be won by training round our own courses, so come along you lads who have been stopping at home on Saturdays and Tuesdays. The more out, the merrier. Now that we have such magnificent quarters, it is a crime not to use them. I have been elected "Tea Boy" on Tuesday evenings so come along and enjoy my poison. I shall be pleased to serve you. Eric Hall takes pride of place as the most improved walker this season so far. He annexed the Civil Service title in a new Championship record of 54m. 21s. and followed this up by winning the Horwood Cup in excellent time. Bob Newson has shown considerably improvement, so also has "The Demon King", I mean Len Demmon. With these three we have the basis of a fine "Garnet" Cup team and as I expect this Championship will be over by the time you receive this issue, I hope we shall have the cup back in our possession by that time. This year the National 10 is to be held at Southport, only 220 miles away. Let us hope the travelling arrangements will be better than they were for Macclesfield. Can we break the monotony of Sheffield United Harriers taking this Championship year after year. Of course we can, but only if you all get out together and TRAIN, TRAIN, TRAIN. Our last visit north for the Bradford 50 Kilos. was a huge success, why not this one?. The Surrey 10 Miles Championship this year is being held from Surrey W.C. headquarters, The Stag and Hounds and this should result in another dual title. Our Middlesex lads will also no doubt be out in force. It should be noted that the Regents Park 15 miles will be used as the basis of selection for the Union of London Walking Clubs match in Paris a few weeks later so its up to you to do your best if you want to go to "Gay Paree". This year, for the first time, we shall be staging a National Championship from our headquarters, the Race Walking Association having accepted our offer for the 20 miles on 4th May. We shall be using the same course of three laps as our own Championship on April 16th, which should prove of considerable advantage in helping us to retain our hard won title of last year. We shall need lots of help on this most important day, if we are to make this, our first National Championship, one to be remembered. I have already been promised the help and co-operation of Arthur Whitehead who knows the details of the course so well. Cars will be needed to transport judges and other officials round the course, so please let me have your names as early as possible so that I can be sure of a list of willing helpers, not only for transport, but for sponging and feeding stations, pointsmen and all the other incidental jobs that are necessary in an important race. This is where the runners can help and you will also be able to give encouragement to our own walkers all round the course and help them to retain their title of National Champions. They will do it more so with your moral and vocal support. Note the date - MAY 4th and let me have your names. Congratulations to Norman Guilmant on his excellent performance in Italy in the 100 Km. International Race on 4th November. A full report is given elsewhere in the magazine. Good luck to all and lots of success. Jack. items.s: 5 MILES ROAD RACE - SEPTEMBER 18TH Report of a new 5 miles road race held to help select the October Brighton Relay team, won by Len Herbert. This was a new race on our programme being put in to assist selection of the team for the October Brighton Relay. The course used was a shortened version of the usual five and was a little under the distance. The first mile round the top was taken at a reasonable pace but a bunch of about a dozen with Len Herbert on the back of it, soon detached itself from the mob. There were 56 finishers so you can see it was a popular race. By the top of Copse Hill Herbert had moved right through the field and four others, Walker, Smart, Short and Tooby went down the hill together. One of our juniors, Brian Trower, had hung on to the back of the bunch and ran well on the way back to finish 8th. Herbert was the winner in 23.56, with Smart 24.5 and Short 24.17. Charlie Walker again refused to cane himself over the last mile and was content with 4th. Following him were Tooby, Bedford, Burr, Trower, Brickwood, L. Bishop and Newell making one of his too infrequent appearances. In the first few hundred yards Brian Trower again tried to show us all the way but Bill Pawsey soon took over the lead which he held to the end. Bagnall and Walker ran well for 2nd and 3rd place, followed by the usual crowd with Masters having an easy run whipping up the end of our pack. items.s: SOUTH OF THE THAMES JUNIOR CHAMPIONSHIP - NOVEMBER 13TH Report of the South of the Thames Junior Championship at Footscray, won by R. Stonehouse of Farnham A.C., with Belgrave A team 10th. Run on a flat but muddy course at Footscray, this year's race proved to be the undoing of many of our runners who appeared to start too fast, only to fall back as the race progressed. E. Paterson, running for the "B" Team, caused a surprise by beaing the 2nd Belgrave man to finish and far ahead of many of our "A" Team members. Brian Trower, "A", ran a well judged race to finish 25th, one place ahead of Paterson. Eric Gebbett and Colin Collis both ran very soundly to finish 47th and 58th respectively. The individual winner was R. Stonehouse, Farnham A.C. which club also provided the 2nd man home. Having so many runners disqualified through the many barring clauses, it is becoming increasingly difficult to field a first class team and we look to our juniors to form the neuclus of our future teams for this event. items.s: CLUB 7 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP - DECEMBER 11TH Report and result of the club 7 miles championship combined with a match against Blackheath and Sutton & Cheam; Weeks-Pearson won the race, Charlie Walker won the Blackstaffe Shield and R. Budd the handicap. This year the seven was combined with a match event against Blackheath Harriers and Sutton and Cheam Harriers. Owing to a misunderstanding of arrangements made last July, Blackheath only arrived with eight runners instead of the usual crowd we expect from our visitors. The course was wet, particularly the stretch home from the Windmill but the fast men soon moved right away from the bulk of the field. Jack Brown was seen to be not so fit as in previous years and one of the lads running with him said "He ran down to the brook like a plum pudding". Weeks-Pearson eventually ran away with the race by over 20 seconds. Charlie Walker came in next and so won the Blackstaffe Shield but he only just held off Braughton in the straight. Jumbo Masters came next and Jack Brown only got 3rd Championship medal this year. The Club finishing 2.4.5.10.11.12, won the team race, greatly helped by Colin Collis, 9th who ran much above the form he has shown recently. In the team race Blackheath were 2nd with 48 points to our 44 and Sutton & Cheam 3rd with 79. Budd the handicap winner, was a last minute entry and although running well, must thank the handicapper for a somewhat generous allowance. Handicap. 1. R. Budd. 2. L. Bush 3. C. Walker. Result: 1. C. ST. DUNSTANS' HOUR MEETING - SEPTEMBER 25TH
items.sum: Report of the St. Dunstans' Hour Meeting, held on the day of the club's Annual Dinner and Dance, with Len Demmon first Belgrave home in the A section won by Coleman of Highgate.
items.s: WALKING RESULTS ST. DUNSTANS' HOUR MEETING - SEPTEMBER 25TH Report of the St. Dunstans' Hour Meeting, held on the day of the club's Annual Dinner and Dance, with Len Demmon first Belgrave home in the A section won by Coleman of Highgate. As this was the day of our Annual Dinner and Dance, the entry was lower than usual. We had three competitors in the "A" Section, four in the "B" ten in "C" and three in "D" and one in the Junior three miles. Denis Ives, who should not have started with the heavy cold he had, is certainly a likely prospect with steady training. Len Demmon was our first man to finish in the "A" section which was won by Coleman of Highgate who covered 8 miles, 76 yards, an excellent performance. We were pleased to see Gerry Warr and Joe Scamell junr. back on the track, they both just missed the seven miles but gave a glimpse of better things to come. Ray Middleton, who turned up too late for the Junior three, competed in the "C" Section and covered 6 miles 1561 yards. A good afternoon was enjoyed by all and then to the Dinner - WHAT A NIGHT - those who did not come certainly missed a treat and had better make a date for next November. Denis Ives Denis Ives Len Demmon Len Demmon first Belgrave finisher in "A" section Coleman Coleman won "A" section, 8 miles 76 yards Gerry Warr Gerry Warr Joe Scamell Joe Scamell junr. junr. We opened our winter season as usual with a five miles handicap and match with our Police friends. 40 competitors started and Eric Hall, carrying on his summer form, won a good race in 37m. 17s. with Hugh McGreechan 2nd and Len Demmon 3rd. Some of our new Police lads showed up well and surely one or two will be waking up some of the older ones a little later in the season. We had another good entry from the club with 37 individuals and four teams. What we lack in quality, we certainly make up for in quantity. Our lads certainly showed up better in this race, always among the leading bunch were Syd James, 11th, Eric Hall 16th, George Checkley 18th and Len Demmon 23rd. items.s: 35TH BELGRAVE OPEN 7 - NOVEMBER 27TH Report of the 35th Belgrave Open 7 walk with 203 competitors at Belgrave Hall: Belgrave finished 3rd to Woodford Green and won the handicap team race, with thanks to officials and prize donors and the Brighton Cup presented to Norman Guilmant; the printed positions (11, 16, 18, 28) do not add up to the printed 68 points. This is a day when we need elastic walls at Belgrave Hall. The programme entry of 318 makes one wonder what would happen if everyone turned up. As it was 203 competitors, plus judges, timekeepers and sundry officials filled the place to overflowing. Our thanks are due to Arthur Whitehead who once again provided accommodation for our own competitors at Lauriston House and looked after them so well after the race ably assisted by Arthur Penstone and other willing helpers. Our new accommodation was praised by many of the visitors and on the whole arrangements went according to plan. The race proved to be a battle between L. Evans of Highgate, walking as an individual, R. Goodall and Brian Hawkins. Syd James was ruled out roughly half way which seriously affected our chances of winning the Berman Cup. Not disheartened, the other lads walked exceptionally well and with Eric Hall 11th, George Checkley 16th, Len Demmon 18th and Bob Newson 28th we totalled 68 points to finish 3rd to Woodford Green 21 points, with Met. W.C. 50 points, 2nd. The handicap team race was won by our "A" Team with Demmon, Newson, Hall and Doubleday with an aggregate time of 206m.2s. Surrey W.C. were 2nd and Woodford Green 3rd. The individual handicap was won by Evans of Highgate, Shaw of Queens Park H. was 2nd and Len Demmon 3rd.. Bernard Eglington, on his last days leave from Germany, took the prize for the first Belgrave member unplaced in the scratch events. Although it started raining towards the end, in fact the recording was done in heavy rain, everything went well and we owe a hearty vote of thanks to the officials on the line who carried out a difficult job under trying conditions in such an efficient way that the result was out in just about an hour, most of the donkey work, that is working out the handicap result being done by your editor. Thanks are also due to those who came along with cars and enabled the judges to get round the course. And finally a word of thanks to our prize fund donors, Don Brown, Harry Evans, Mrs. Goswell, A.A.Harley, Senior and Junior, E. Hall, S. James, D. Logan, T. Morrell, T. Scrimshaw, H. Shields and P. Wright. Due to their generous help we were able to maintain our high standard of prizes which seemed to meet with the general approbation of the competitors. The prizes were presented by Mr. T. For the information of new members and to refresh the minds of others, the details of the Medal Competitions which are held in the summer are published below. BOYS The competition is open to boys of 12 to 15 years whose birthday is in the following age groups and who are first claim members: Group 1. 12th birthday between 2nd April and 1st October 1955 2. 12th birthday between 2nd Oct.1954 and 1st Apr. 1955 3. 13th birthday between 2nd April and 1st October 1955 4. 13th birthday between 2nd Oct.1954 and 1st Apr. 1955 5. 14th birthday between 2nd April and 1st October 1955 6. 14th birthday between 2nd Oct.1954 and 1st Apr. 1955 7. 15th birthday between 2nd April and 1st October 1955 The competition consists of six events: High Jump, Long Jump, Shot Putt, Javelin, 880 yards and 100 yards. items.sum: Coaching notes by F. Simmons on a Surrey County A.A.A. coaching course, with Oscar State's weight-training demonstration, Geof Dyson's lecture, and a call for club coaches to work with Franz Stampfl.
items.s: COACHING CHAT Coaching notes by F. Simmons on a Surrey County A.A.A. coaching course, with Oscar State's weight-training demonstration, Geof Dyson's lecture, and a call for club coaches to work with Franz Stampfl. During the week end of November 27th 28th I attended a coaching course promoted by the Surrey County A.A.A. It was disappointing to me that I was the only qualified coach from Belgrave who attended. It is not enough to have gained your Honorary Coach's badge. Surely there is more to learn so that we can use that knowledge for the benefit of our club members. A demonstration of weight training by the expert Oscar State was given. I watched this most carefully and also had an attempt at some of the demonstrations. I was convinced that these could assist the not so well endowed in physique, this after being sceptical on the subject for a long time. These exercises are also of great assistance to sprinters, jumpers and throwers and can also help middle and long distance men. The loop films on the subject which you were taking were most helpful and gave you as a coach a clear idea of what to look for and how to spot a bad habit in an athletds action. We were also given advice on how to help athletes to cure this, stressing that it is not always wise to alter the athlete's natural action. Geof Dyson gave a lecture on "Mechanics without tears". I thought I should probably fall asleep but strangely enough I was absorbed by the lecture and followed it closely and hope that I have learned something from it to help me when I go for my test on the Jumping events in February. After tea on Sunday we were shown the film on the European Games and some shots of the various stars in action. This was followed by a general discussion and it was decided to have another course in January. More details will be available later so if you are keen to go please contact me. It was also arranged to have a County Coaches Meeting at which all County and Club Coaches will be welcomed. We are the only club in the County to have a Coaches' panel but to be quite honest it is not functioning as I think it should be. We could make our presence felt if more attended these courses put on by the County so that we all have at least the fundamental knowledge of events at which we do not specialize. Lastly I would like, if it is at all possible, for Club Coaches to work in closer union with Franz Stampfl. This can easily be done without losing your individuality. He is most anxious to help any member of Belgrave, whether a coach or an active athlete. F. Simmons. Oscar State Oscar State demonstrated weight training Geof Dyson Geof Dyson lecture "Mechanics without tears" Franz Stampfl Franz Stampfl coach F. Simmons F. items.sum: Field events section notes on Sunday training at Battersea Park, coming competitions, and Percy Luxon's award of the Tommy Green Cup.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS Field events section notes on Sunday training at Battersea Park, coming competitions, and Percy Luxon's award of the Tommy Green Cup. Although the Field Events Section has been very quiet this last three months, some of the members have been in training at Battersea Park on Sunday mornings under the direction of Franz Stampfl and Frank Simmons. Now is the time to get down to business as we are all going to have a busy time next summer, with the Sward Trohpy, Kinnair Meeting, Waddilove Trophy, the Doris Shield and a new competition for the Vancouver Trophy. The standard of field events in the club is improving and it was very pleasing to see Percy Luxon awarded the "Tommy Green" Cup for the best club performance of the year. I understand that M. Harris is now back from the Services and he should prove a useful addition to our shot putters. I hope to have been in touch with all the Field Events men by the time you receive this magazine and wish you all good luck for the summer season. items.s: BITS AND PIECES Club notes asking missing members to return, "Spotter"'s observations on members' habits, and members' placings in the Civil Service and Inter-Banks cross-country races. Many once familiar faces have been missing so far this season. This applies to all sections of the club. Where are you hiding yourselves. The Cross Country Captain would like to see more of Len Herbert, Archie Bedford and Peter Hitchcock, to mention a few. Jack Goswell is waiting to see young Joe Scamell, Gordon Waddingham, Percy Wilson, and a contributor who calls himself "Spotter" adds his observations on what he "sees and hears" - Members who are not giving the Cross Country Captain their support. The poor excuses they give when asked about it. The practice of going out in twos and threes very early instead of with the packs under the pack leaders. This applies mostly to youngsters who should be seeking the advice of experienced men. The members who attend the school at Battersea Park on Sunday mornings but seem reluctant to have a go in inter-club matches. Are they being told not to? The members who manage to get to the hall when there is an away fixture. The reluctance of members to ask advice of Franz Stampfl. Remember he has been engaged as our professional coach and is willing to help you. On the day of the Club 7, Cliff Roffey was 4th and David Baulch 7th in the Civil Service Cross Country Championship, whilst Eric Bishop was 16th in the Inter-Banks. items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial noting the death of Bill Fish, the season's improved team placings, and new club trophies from Mrs. Aplin and Don Brown. Fellow Members, We regret that yet another Club stalwart in the person of Bill Fish, has passed away. He will be remembered by most of our present day members as the man who sat at the gate at Battersea and Tooting Tracks and we shall certainly miss his cheery face during the coming track season. An appreciation by Alf Harley will be found in the following pages. Looking back over the past few months, it is very encouraging to note the improved performances of our members as compared with the previous year. 1st in the South of the Thames, 2nd in the Southern Counties and 5th in the National shows considerable improvement amongst the runners, whilst the walkers, who were 3rd in the National 10, gained a place for the first time for some years in that event. Whilst there is still room for improvement, it would seem that we are definitely on the upgrade and we can look forward with confidence to further improvement during the coming months. We are indebted to Mrs. Aplin, Frank Elson's sister, and Don Brown for two more Club Trophies. Mrs. Aplin has generously offered to present a trophy in memory of Frank and in view of his long association with race walking, the committee, with the approval of Mrs. Aplin, decided to allocate it to the newly instituted 7 miles Track Walking Championship and it is hoped that Mrs. Aplin will be at the track to present it for the first time. Don Brown has presented a Style Award for the 2 miles Track Championship, which should act as a further incentive to our walkers. It is interesting to note that we now have 39 Club trophies for which members may compete. Editor. items.sum: Obituary of Life Member and Vice President W. J. "Bill" Fish, who died on March 5th, with a note on the passing of former Assistant Hon. Secretary Harry Fearn.
items.s: W. J. FISH. Obituary of Life Member and Vice President W. J. "Bill" Fish, who died on March 5th, with a note on the passing of former Assistant Hon. Secretary Harry Fearn. Members will learn with real regret of the death of our Life Member and Vice President, "Bill" Fish, which occurred on March 5th. Bill had been a club stalwart for many years and even in recent years, when gravely handicapped, he still managed to get to our track meetings and act as Chief Steward. In the 1920's he turned out regularly in our walking events and teams and for very many years he was a tower of strength in preparing the track for our meetings and in clearing away afterwards. He was always on hand at our open dances carrying through a difficult job on the door and every Saturday he was at Clapham Junction Station with our special rail tickets for members, and in attendance at our mid-week quarters for a similar purpose. In addition we relied upon him to prepare and maintain our sets of numbers for all our racing throughout the year. In fact, Bill worked hard for Belgrave in many ways, never sparing himself. When one remembers that his market work had him out daily in the small hours, how easily and justifiably he could have excused himself from performing those many duties he undertook on our behalf. But he did not, and his devotion to and hard work for the club - inspite of difficulties which could easily have become acceptable excuses - provide a great example for our younger members. We mourn his passing and extend our sincere condolences to Bill's family. We also note with regret the passing of Harry Fearn, a former Assistant Hon. Secretary of this Club and a great sower of strength in the days when our track training and meetings were held at the Sports Ground of Prices' Athletic Club. W. J. Fish W. J. items.sum: Tribute to club professional coach Franz Stampfl on his departure for a lectureship at Adelaide University and the post of National Coach of Australia.
items.s: FRANZ STAMPFL Tribute to club professional coach Franz Stampfl on his departure for a lectureship at Adelaide University and the post of National Coach of Australia. It is with regret we have to announce the departure of Franz Stampfl for Australia in July. Franz came to Belgrave as a young man in the summer of 1937 and quickly endeared himself to those with whom he came in contact. Within a few weeks he had organised our training as it had never been done before. He did not ask us to do what he himself could not. His enthusiasm and personality were such that members were attempting to do things they had previously avoided. The war years came and Franz was lost to us, until four years ago when due to the request of club members, who had heard a lot about him, the club were happy to again ask him to become our professional coach. This wise move had an almost immediate effect as our Field Events men began to show improvement which has continued until now when they are in a happy and flourishing state. The encouragement he has given to what was the "Cinderella" side of Belgrave - the sprinters - is tremendous. We can now safely say we have our strongest ever sprint team. It is to be regretted that our longer distance men have not sought his assistance for I feel that he would have been able to give them an abundance of good advice. It is not generally known that Franz is also a first class coach of distance running. It is not yet too late to ask his advice, so distance men, what about it! As for the reason for his departure, he has been offered a lectureship at Adelaide University and will be the National Coach of Australia. Australia's gain is our loss and we wish him "Bon voyage" and every success in his new venture. On a more personal note, I would like to add my appreciation of the help I have received as a club coach. I only hope I shall be able to pass on to club members some of the lessons I have learned during the past four years. Frank Simmons. Franz Stampfl Franz Stampfl club professional coach; leaving for Australia in July to be National Coach of Australia Frank Simmons Frank Simmons club coach Australia Adelaide University

items.s: CHRISTMAS DAY PAARLAUF Report and result of the newly instituted Christmas Day Paarlauf (pairs relay) on Wimbledon Common, won by Len Bishop and Eric Gebbett. Friendliness was, as befitted the season, the keynote of a highly successful Paarlauf, a newly instituted Christmas fixture, run round the green at Wimbledon Common on Christmas morning. In perfect conditions, apart from a brisk breeze, twelve runners turned out to gain their first experience of this comparatively new type of relay. To ensure reasonably even paring, the names of the six best runners were placed in one hat and the remainder in another. This method turned out to be quite satisfactory as the field kept surprisingly close together throughout the race, 332 yards covering them all at the finish. Aubrey Reeve, Hon. Sec. of the Wimbledon A.C. who kindly came along to help, made the draw and the race was started outside Lauriston House by John Jewell, the Assistant Hon. Secretary of the Road Runners Club. After 300 yards, our former member, Jim Edgar, running by special invitation, went ahead opening up quite a gap, but Ron Linstead clsed up on him at the half mile mark and overtook him running with great style and ease. Ron paired with "Pub" Childs, got well ahead during the first four laps of the 1415 yards circuit, but the pace then told and Len Bishop, paired with Eric Gebbett, who had been running a fast but steady race closed up gradually taking the lead on the 5th lap, a lead which they never lost again during the race. After the 27 minute whistle had gone, no further change over was allowed and Charlie Walker, paired with Gordon Biscoe, appeared to be caught napping, Gordon being caught in possession of the baton. However it is doubtful whether even Charlie could have made much impression in the last three minutes as Len and Eric were well ahead and Gordon did very well to hang on to 2nd position. John Burr and Dave Hooper, both rather unfit, ran extremely even laps but were unabe to get into the running and Jim was breathing down Dave's neck when the final whistle blew. Dave Baulch and Charlie Dabbs also lapped with admirable regularity but had to be content with 3rd position. After the race everyone adjourned to the cottage to wash down and enormous baking of Mince Pies provided by Mrs. Jean Manning with a hot and rather alcoholic "Witches brew" concocted by Arthur Whitehead. We feel sure that the runners would like to thank Charlie Smart, Aubrey Reeve and John Jewell for their very capable handling of the race.
