items.label: No. 129
items.sum: Note that member John Bromley, a former steeplechaser, won the 17-mile Singapore to Jahore walking race for the second year.
items.s: John Bromley wins big walk. Note that member John Bromley, a former steeplechaser, won the 17-mile Singapore to Jahore walking race for the second year. We are indebted to a member of Thames Valley Harriers for the report of a Walking Race from Singapore to Jahore,a distance of just over 17 miles,which was won by none other than John Bromley former steeplechaser and Brighton Relay runner in the very good time of 2hrs.56mins. This race,which was promoted by the Singapore Free Press,was held on a Sunday morning,when no less than 650 competitors lined up for the start at 6am. According to press cuttings,John won this race last year,but has apparently kept his achievement up his sleeve as this appears to be the first intimation that he has turned to road walking.We do like to hear of the activities of our members who are overseas and hope that any others who are carrying on the good work will let us know about it. Of the 650 starters,430 finished the course,and John received once again the handsome trophy presented for annual competition by Messrs Bata,the shoe people,and the prize of a cinecamera presented by Twentieth Century Fox Films Ltd. Well done John. Bill True is making note of the result in case you continue walking on your return to this country. S.C.R. items.sum: Note from the new Youth and Junior Section secretary on training packs at Wimbledon, with results of a junior 3 mile road race and a 4 lap road relay at Battersea Park.
items.s: For the Attention of all Juniors and Youths Note from the new Youth and Junior Section secretary on training packs at Wimbledon, with results of a junior 3 mile road race and a 4 lap road relay at Battersea Park. This article is primarily for the benefit of the Youth and Junior Section of our club, of which you, the members, have nominated me as Secretary. There are a few points I would like to make which I feel some of you would like to know. ONE. is that I am always ready to listen to any suggestion as regards the functions of our sections. TWO. I am endeavouring to form one, or more training packs during the Winter months; at the moment, we are training from Wimbledon on Tuesday and Thursday nights at 7-0 pm. and Saturday afternoons. I am grading the packs to enable runners of varying ability to enjoy these runs and also to develop each individual without his being run off his legs. This is most important as every Champion will tell you pack running is the foundation of Team running by which we can endeavour to win the Major Events during the Cross Country Season. There are two results which apply to our Section:- 3 Mile Road Race at Wimbledon 29.9.56 K. Miller is a new member and shows every promise. 4 Lap Road Relay at Battersea Park 21.10.56. This race was organised by M. Pyer. and was arranged to give our younger members a chance to show what they could do. Their ages ranged from 12½ to 15½ years. One of our members, E. Penny, recorded second fastest time over the course, which is approximately 1¾ miles. His time was 8 mins. 49secs. which is very good running, but a Mitcham lad did even better- his time being 8 mins. 42 secs. A. W. Penny. (Secretary) Junior Section. 1. A.W.Black - 15.41. 2. K. items.sum: Teasing notes about cross-country runners neglecting club nights at Belgrave Hall, not wearing Belgrave vests and skipping an away road relay.
items.s: Stirrings Teasing notes about cross-country runners neglecting club nights at Belgrave Hall, not wearing Belgrave vests and skipping an away road relay. It is a pity that some Cross-Country Runners (not Night-School Students) who manage the journey to run at Wimbledon some evenings, have apparently forgotten the whereabouts of Belgrave Hall on Club Nights. Members may be assured that if they bring their shampoo on Tuesday or Thursday we can arrange for the extractor fan to be dismantled and converted into a hair dryer. An assurance has been received that in the later cross-country events, runners at present so allergic to their Belgrave vests when representing their Club will wear them. Do they mean when they should be in their County vests? It is heartbreaking to learn that the official reason for not supporting an away road relay where free overnight accommodation had been promised was given as the reluctance of runners to miss their Sunday morning training run!!! Wimbledon Belgrave Hall

items.label: No. 130
items.sum: Editorial asking members to send in regular reports, explaining a plan to post the magazine with the fixture cards, and urging full Belgrave support in all matches for the 1957 season.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial asking members to send in regular reports, explaining a plan to post the magazine with the fixture cards, and urging full Belgrave support in all matches for the 1957 season. Dear Fellow Members, Once upon a time, we used to read this magazine, and we often wondered why it was that the editors were repeatedly asking the officials of each branch of the Club, to send in REGULAR reports of its activities, together with any other items of interest. Now we know! We are not magicians, and cannot be expected to prepare the magazine in the few days immediately before it is due to be printed. To lighten our task therefore, we must ask that reports be sent to us weekly, BY ANYONE, be he spectator, competitor or official. In fact, the wider the field of contribution, the greater the interest of the magazine. What could be more simple than scribbling a report on the way home in the train? Furthermore, in the interests of economy, it is hoped to combine the despatch of the Belgravian with that of the fixture cards, thereby saving approximately £10 per annum. This cannot be achieved unless the magazine can be completed each quarter and sent for printing on time. So let's be hearing from all you budding reporters. We would like to thank those anonymous contributors who have sent us articles for this edition. No doubt they will appreciate that where we receive more than one report on the same event, the contents, as near as possible, are combined, and any loss of style will be understood. By the time this edition is distributed, the track season will be with us, and the programme of long distance road races will have commenced. We want to see full Belgrave support in all the major events, on the Track, in Field Events, and on the Road. Whilst agreeing that athletics is a sport to be enjoyed, win or lose, we feel that the time has come for us to endeavour to assert ourselves as the premier club in the South, and to do this by putting our full strength into all matches. We have an abundance of talent in our ranks, at all ages. Messrs. Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches. Everyone must start at the bottom, and none is so good that he can afford to ignore minor events. The presence of a "Star" in a race is a challenge to the lesser lights to topple him from his pedestal, and he learns that only hard work will keep him there. The unknown having tasted victory will be eagerly looking around for his next "head". Keen competition within the Club for team places is the key to success, but it must be made certain that there are sufficient "B" team matches to enable second string men to gain that experience necessary for promotion to the "A" team. We hope to be reporting the successful commencement of the 1957 season in our next issue. Your coaches can only guide you, you must do the work. Your success will be their well-deserved reward. So go to it and good luck! Your Editors. items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR. 10th. NOV. Report of a poor Belgrave turnout at the South of Thames Junior cross-country race at Brighton, with Charlie Dabbs 8th and the A, B and D team placings. SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR. 10th. NOV. Is the Brighton seaside air not encouraging enough itself or does the thought of a journey frighten many Belgravians? Whatever it was, there was a poor turnout for this event - less in fact, than half those entered. I would add that one of our newer members' worked until midday and then journeyed down by train to compete. The race itself was disappointing from the point of view of Club supporters, who were also few in number. Charlie Dabbs gave of his best again and finished 8th., but I feel much credit should go to J. Dooley, who although entered in the "D" team, finished 54th. to be the third Belgrave man home. As for the other competing members, I am sure they would all admit to having had better runs than this. Once again Arthur Whitehead must be thanked for supplying a very welcome cup of tea to all our runners at the finish. Placings and team positions:- 7th.Belgrave "A" ( 8 C. Dabbs, 50 G. e: City of Rochester 5 mile Road Race
items.s: CITY OF ROCHESTER 5 mile ROAD RACE 17th NOV. 1956 Report of Jack Brown winning the City of Rochester 5 mile road race from Salvat of Finchley, with Ray Tooby 12th and Len Bishop 46th. CITY OF ROCHESTER 5 mile ROAD RACE 17th NOV. 1956 The usual cold, misty weather greeted the starters for this year's race, but soon warming to his task, Jack Brown set about the opposition in no uncertain manner and was soon in the leading bunch with Salvat of Finchley and Cameron of T.V.H. Jack and Salvat ran neck and neck until approximately 500yds from the finish, when Jack's fine burst of speed proved too much for his opponent. The winning time was only 8sec. outside George Knight's course record. Ray Tooby, continuing his welcome return to form, ran very well to finish 12th, only three seconds behind Haslam (T.V.H.). Len Bishop who arrived only just in time for the start, finished 46th. It was a pity we did not have more support for this event, as no doubt we could have been placed in the team race. 1st J.W. Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap. Second place in the handicap went to Clive Shippen who finished 5th in the actual race - a very good performance. items.s: THE MITCHAM"15" JAN. 12th. Report of Belgrave winning the Mitcham 15 team award, with Jack Brown beating O'Gorman and cutting 41 seconds off Jim Peters' course record; the text places Len Bishop 15th but the result and a later sentence give 14th. THE MITCHAM"15" JAN. 12th. Our road runners notched a further great victory when providing the individual winner of this very popular event and carrying off the team award. Continuing along his road of success Jack Brown sliced off 41 seconds from Jim Peters course record, a most meritorious performance. The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of a dozen, including our own trio, Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop on the other. Jack and O'Gorman, however, had what appeared to be a burning desire to be all alone and with a big effort between 5 and 9 miles (at which point the time was 44m 30s!) they had established a lead of 20 seconds. Any hopes of individual honours cherished by the following group had by now completely vanished. The further these two went, the diminutive O'Gorman and the taller Jack, his hair bouncing with each stride, the greater the gap became, and Keily, who had moved up to third, was soon almost out of sight. Colin, Eric and Len were firmly dug in at 8th, 9th and 15th respectively and Jim Heathfield, confounding everyone, looked very comfortable in 28th place. The wise head of Collis had obviously intervened in Jim's training. Back to the leaders, where, with 400 yds. to go, Jack produced an amazing turn of speed which completely overwhelmed O'Gorman, with the incredible result that Jack ran out the winner by 14 seconds! It is indeed food for thought when one realises that these two had run throughout at approximately 4m.58s. per mile; how about the marathon Jack? With Eric and Colin finishing in good style 8th and 9th, no doubts were felt about the team result. A word of consolation to Len Bishop for finishing 14th in a fast time, yet being denied a team prize. However, let this be a reminder that road-running honours are going to be difficult to come by this season. It was good to see our London to Brighton men, Alan Bishop, MacDonald and Wortley sharpening up early in the season, it is hoped they will soon be starting their long preparation. A special word of praise to Jim Heathfield, whose time of 89m.28s. would open the eyes of many considered road runners. If the Mitcham "15" is any criterion, then the Belgrave vest will be well to the fore in all the leading road events during 1957. items.s: CLUB 10 MILES CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP 26th JAN. 1957 Report and result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship, won by Jack Brown for the eighth successive Macher Shield, with Paget winning the handicap. CLUB 10 MILES CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP 26th JAN. 1957 Although the course was below the stipulated distance (approximately 9¾ miles), the times were nevertheless very fast. In addition the terrain was rather muddy in places and light rain was falling during most of the race. The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind. At eight miles Brown was 1 min. 20 sec. to the good, with Walker 20 sec. in front of Baulch, and Tooby, having pulled away from Gebbett, now running fourth. Over the last couple of miles there were no positional changes amongst the leaders, but the distance between them lengthened, and at the finish Brown came home an easy winner in the excellent time of 50m.27s. Jack must be congratulated on winning the "Macher Shield" for the eighth time in succession, but we must also extend our congratulations to Charlie Walker—for indeed it is no disgrace to be runner-up to Jack—and Dave Baulch for a really splendid performance. items.s: Carnival Dance 26th Jan. 1957 Account of the Social Section's carnival dance, with a comedy sketch, rock n' roll dancing, games and music from the A.T.C. Skiffle Group. Carnival Dance 26th Jan. 1957 Once again the Social Section of the Club did a fine job, and a good time was had by all. Stan Vickers and Ray Hall again acted as Phillip Harbens in the Sausage and Mash Supper Comedy, this time ably assisted by Mrs. Goswell and Mrs. Knifton, who took the part of Mrs. Beatons. Dancing went very well with all the old-timers lowering their dignity to do rock n' roll; it was a treat to watch. The various games and activities (mainly organised by Bill Lucas) proved very pleasant interludes, as well as a source of great enjoyment both to those taking part and to those watching. The A.T.C. Skiffle Group provided some very lively interval music - thanks boys. It only remains for me to ask "When's the next dance?" CHRISTMAS Report and result of the annual half-hour paarlauf at Christmas, poorly supported because of a clash with a Herne Hill fixture and won by the Belgrave pair Charlie Walker and C. Henn. ANNUAL HALF-HOUR PAARLAUF. CHRISTMAS This event would have had much more support had there not been a friendly fixture with Herne Hill on the same day. When it is considered how much work Arthur Whitehead puts in to this race he must find it very discouraging to have his efforts (unwittingly it is hoped) sabotaged in this manner. The race itself, run in very pleasant weather, resolved into a dual between a Belgrave pair, Charlie Walker and C. Henn, and two Hercules runners, who together with four others had been invited to compete. When the signal, indicating three minutes to go, was given, Charlie and D. Cobb of Hercules were running together in the lead. It is a very difficult business to try to estimate just how much time is left but Charlie managed it to a nicety and putting in his effort with about ten seconds to go, drew away to win by several yards. items.sum: Report of a Belgrave team winning an eight-mile cross-country match against Westminster Bank at Epsom by one point, with Flanagan first.
items.s: MATCH V. WESTMINSTER BANK AT EPSOM 28th Dec. Report of a Belgrave team winning an eight-mile cross-country match against Westminster Bank at Epsom by one point, with Flanagan first. MATCH V. WESTMINSTER BANK AT EPSOM 28th Dec. As there was an"A" team match at Wimbledon on the same day we were fortunate in mustering nine runners at Epsom for this pleasant little fixture. The course of eight miles was genuine cross-country, consisting of hills, mud and plough, with a short stretch of road. Flanagan ran very well to finish first, beating Gilham of the Bank by 15 sec. They were followed by three Bank runners but as the next six were all Belgravians, the balance was tipped slightly in our favour and we won by one point - a very fair result. Afterwards we were entertained to tea, for which we were very grateful, and a somewhat strenuous afternoon was brought to a fitting conclusion. Our hosts expressed the wish that we might visit them again next year - fixture committee please take note ! items.sum: Report of the South of the Thames senior cross-country race at Maidenhead, where the Belgrave team finished only 15th, complaining that no individual results were sent in.
items.s: SOUTH OF THE THAMES SENIOR Report of the South of the Thames senior cross-country race at Maidenhead, where the Belgrave team finished only 15th, complaining that no individual results were sent in. SOUTH OF THE THAMES SENIOR Held at Maidenhead on Feb. 2nd over an extremely heavy course this race proved a big disappointment for the Club when our team could finish only 15th. We do not agree with the view held in some parts of the Club, that reports of races in which the Club is unsuccessful should be withheld from this magazine. This attitude, which we feel is quite wrong, probably explains the almost complete lack of news from the Cross-Country Section. We cannot therefore give any details of individual performances in this race as they are not in our possession. We can only hope that someone will do something to remedy this unsatisfactory state of affairs and see to it that we are regularly supplied with results, be they favourable or otherwise. South of the Thames Senior Maidenhead

items.s: NEW YEAR CELEBRATIONS DEC.29th. Account of the Social Committee's New Year celebrations, with a bangers-and-mash supper, games, a skiffle band and thanks to Bill Lucas as M.C. and Tom Carter. NEW YEAR CELEBRATIONS DEC.29th. It seems an understatement to say the evening was a resounding success, in the light of the gaiety, fun, entertainment and the whole gamut of carefreeness devised by our Social Committee. Bangers, grilled to a turn, potatoes, bashed and pounded to insensibility by a team of master cooks, headed by such International figures as Messieurs Vickers, Hall and Goswell with a posse of Presidents to act as scullions. The resulting "Chef-d'oeuvre", supported by lashings of tea, rolls and butter, etc., was treated with suspicion until the full delicacy of the masterly preparation was appreciated with cries more. This was a prelude to a programme of carnival festivities which for gaiety, fun and whole-hearted co-operation from all, led to an ever-to-be-remembered evening. Nothing appeared forgotten or left to chance. That difficult warming up period was successfully negotiated by a series of games, chief of which was sniffing at mysterious looking bags. The consequent fun soon broke the ice. A "Skiffle Band" performance introduced by Eric Penny thoroughly livened up the interval and the numerous encores were sufficient proof of appreciation. Thank you Eric and your colleagues for their grand show. It is unnecessary to dwell on the lovely and charming ladies present, they were indeed all beautiful, sufficient to thank them for their presence and co-operation; our reward is to see them so thoroughly enjoying themselves. Finally a word of appreciation to our Social Committee for a wonderful evening, particularly to Bill Lucas for his grand job as M.C. to which we were all indebted, and to Tom Carter for all his work so enthusiastically carried out. items.sum: Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Epsom, where the Belgrave senior team finished 3rd behind South London and Thames Valley, led by Jack Brown, with junior and youths race notes and positions.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. EPSOM. FEB.16th. Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Epsom, where the Belgrave senior team finished 3rd behind South London and Thames Valley, led by Jack Brown, with junior and youths race notes and positions. SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. EPSOM. FEB.16th. Senior race. We are back amongst the top Southern clubs again as a result of the fine performance of our team in finishing 3rd. behind South London and Thames Valley. Our six scoring men, led by Jack Brown, were all well placed throughout, and whilst commendably they held those placings, one did not see the spectacle of the claret and gold vests moving up through the field in last desperate attempts to whittle away those points. However, let nothing detract from their performance, it was a welcome and heartening sight, and it should not be overlooked that the course was one mile short. A fast start saw a keen struggle for the lead with our second claim member, Bill Bird of Ranelagh actually leading during the early stages. Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth. Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner. Then came Chas. Walker, Pete Bagnall, Dave Baulch and Eric Gebbett, all running strongly and all four within reach of one another but unable apparently to join forces, a fact which probably cost us second team place. Although still very husky from a heavy cold, Shippen was about the 100 mark with Len Bishop, Eddie Short and Jim Heathfield further back. And so it was, our lads hung on grimly to their early gains and ran out a good third with Jack Brown, a little disappointed perhaps, our first man home. The Bels were ably backed up by the moral and vocal support of many members, and it was good to see Tom Carter, a most decididly active President, whipping 'em up along the line. Many of us know from past experience, especially as juniors, what encouragement is derived from the attendance of Club officials of whatever capacity, at events of this nature. This was brought to mind even more by the presence of Ernie Duffett, whom we were glad to see looking fit and well. Arthur Penny seems to have earned the respect and loyalty of those juniors under his care and it is to be hoped that his efforts will be rewarded next year by some real team running again in those events in which we were once so prominent. Latent talent will not pass Arthur's eye unnoticed. Our sages tell us that we always perform better in the National than in the Southern, so let us look to even better news after the Parliament Hill battlefield on March 9th. Positions :- 10, J.W. items.s: WALKING NOTES. Walking notes congratulating the club's Olympic walkers, welcoming new juniors, and appealing for support for the track season and the Brighton walk. WALKING NOTES. These are, of necessity, brief, but tell of the continued progress of the Club. To others I have left the Olympics, but I am sure I echo the sentiments of all when I say, "Well done Eric and Stan, you were a credit in every way to the Club". With these two, ably backed up, we have great hopes of winning the National 10 again; Sheffield eight years running is too much! Tuesday evenings throughout the Winter have seen good turn-outs at the hall. As a result we lead the Southern clubs in the Winter "Opens" again. We have a fine crowd of up and coming Juniors and welcome Bryan Cormick, George Barratt, M. Small and John Gilbert. May they look back with pride on the day they became "Bels". Coach Don Brown is always pleased to help you, and we start our track season soon. We want a good school at Battersea on Tues. and Thurs.; it is essential to all short distance men, whom we look to, to regain our Inter-Club Track Title this year, whilst we hope the long distance men also retain our hard won titles. I hope to issue dates of fixtures we are supporting this year, along with the R.W.A. 20 and Kilos and the Brighton. We look forward to a grand Summer and to A.A.A. titles for Stan and ....? - who knows? Rally round supporters, your vocal efforts are needed to drive the "Bels" along. Unless we get more support we may have to discontinue the hire of a coach for the Brighton; a nearly empty coach on the journey down is such an expense - the competitors could more cheaply return by train. Let me know early please so that I can see whether a coach is warranted. Training with a happy crowd is great fun. Experiences gained are many. Stan Vickers, back from Melbourne, revealed his prowess in cooking "Bangers". Come along, join in the good fellowship that is to be had. Reap the benefits of FITNESS. In closing, my thanks to all who have helped me in various ways during a busy season. By their ever-ready help and co-operation they enabled the Club to stage another successful Open Walk and the S.R.W.A. Garnet Cup Championship. Thank you, one and all, Yours, Jack Goswell. items.s: RESULTS OF COUNTY 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIPS 23RD FEBRUARY, 1957 Reports and results of the Surrey, Kent and Middlesex 10 miles walking championships, with Eric Hall winning Surrey, Stan Vickers Kent, and Belgrave walkers placing second for Cadogan A.C. in Middlesex; the Surrey text gives Switzer 9th and Coleman 10th while the table gives 10th and 11th. RESULTS OF COUNTY 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIPS 23RD FEBRUARY, 1957 SURREY AT MITCHAM We started two teams, and 44 walkers faced the started in driving rain. Eric Hall took the lead, closely followed by George Williams. Eric broke away after half-a-mile and thereafter was in no danger of defeat. 63 sec. up at the half distance, he won by 2 min.15sec. from George, who had walked well and always held second place from Dave McMullen who suffered from cramp at 7 miles, but held 3rd place, finishing almost 2 min. ahead of the fourth man. We scored 1,2,3, with Ray Switzer 9th and Joe Coleman 10th. Ray Hall, walking as an individual gained County colours by finishing 6th. Jim Edwards, in his first County 10, performed well. Our "B" team was completed by Joe Wilson, George Webb and Dan Logan, who suffered from the cold. What a distance man Webb would make with regular training! He has obvious potential. Summing up - a grand repeat performance by Eric and a first class team. 43 finished KENT AT BEXLEY Stan Vickers retained his title, winning by the incredible margin of 7m.32s. in 78m.14s. Another new course record (that's three on the trot). Well done Stan! MIDDLESEX AT EASTCOTE Driving rain for a couple of hours or so before the start of this race threatened almost impossible conditions, but fortunately it eased as the competitors started on the hilly course. We had eight walkers competing for Cadogan A.C. and although our chances of a win were slender, we were not without hope. Metropolitan W.C. soon put paid to these by a splendid exhibition of team walking, eventually winning with the absolute mimimum score of 10pts., finishing the first four home. Ted Smith was our great hope for the individual title and at two miles had a lead of afew yards over the field. From the three mile point however, he must have become very tired at the sight of Met vests for he found himself walking with six or seven of their men from then on. Eventually Ted finished sixth, a creditable performance. George Checkley walked strongly in the second half of the race, gaining several places and finishing just in front of Bob Newson who walked evenly throughout. Our fourth man, Hugh McGreechan lost several places in the last two miles but our margin over the third club, Polytechnic H., was always an appreciable one. Of our others, Cyril Yescombe and Harry Shields had their usual social outing, and George Place and Syd Spencer seemed to enjoy their trip round this corner of Middlesex which still has fields and trees to show something remaining of a rural atmosphere. items.s: THE R.W.A. "GARNET CUP" CHAMPIONSHIP Report and result of the R.W.A. Garnet Cup 10 miles walk staged by Belgrave at Belgrave Hall, won by C. Williams of Ilford, with Belgrave 4th team and Ray Middleton their best man in 14th. THE R.W.A. "GARNET CUP" CHAMPIONSHIP At Belgrave Hall 2nd Feb. 1957 Local arrangements for this Southern 10 miles event (which is a "limited" Championship in that many barring clauses operate) were entrusted to us by the Race Walking Association; and we are confident that this trust was not misplaced. Our excellent accommodation at Belgrave Hall is indeed a great foundation to build upon, and with Jack Goswell and Arthur Whitehead working like beavers to ensure faultless arrangements for the planning and conduct of the race, and with Syd Roberts in charge of the scoring and recording details, we had all the ingredients for the perfect promotion. All that was needed in addition was reasonable weather and a good field - and these, too, were forthcoming. Stan Horton, Chairman of the R.W.A. Southern Area, started the field of 114 walkers, and C. Williams of Ilford A.C., the favourite, was soon in the lead and retained this to finish a very worthy winner from A.G. Thomson of Met. W.C. with M. Tadd of Brighton A.C. third. As our winning team of last year was no longer eligible and as many of our other walkers have previously shed their "Junior" status, we realised that our team prospects could not be considered of the brightest; but that they would give of their utmost we were sure, and we could not ask for more than that. The team race was keenly fought out and at one time was very open, but Met. W.C. gradually strengthened their hold to eventually finish easy winners. Woodford Green took second medals, and Brighton A.C., by two points, deprived us of third place. We had expected Trevor Luck to take a forward position in this year's race but he unfortunately broke a wrist a fortnight earlier, thus belying his name, and must wait another year. True he started but it was a forlorn hope with arm in plaster from wrist to elbow and training lost; he did well and revealed great pluck in finishing the race. Our three, Ray Middleton, Nick Milsum and Ray Switzer pursued a steady course together for the first half of the race and then began their advance through the field, with Middleton proving himself our best man on the day, finishing in 14th position. Our team was completed by Cyril Yescombe, and thereafter the Belgrave vests followed in at intervals until we had finished twelve men of the 107 completing the course. When next year's event comes round we are sure that many of our walkers will be showing that they have made progress; and one of our boys who should assuredly make the grade is John Keown. In conclusion, a pat on the back to our team and the assurance that we shall be among the placings again next year; and our renewed sincere thanks to all who helped with the event, with particular reference to the herculean labours of Jack and Arthur. items.sum: Eric Hall's account of the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games, including the athletics highlights and the walks in which he and Stan Vickers competed.
items.s: THE OLYMPIC GAMES Eric Hall's account of the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games, including the athletics highlights and the walks in which he and Stan Vickers competed. THE OLYMPIC GAMES By Eric Hall Our quarters were situated in the Olympic Village, Heidelburg, 10 miles from the Stadium and we reached them at 7a.m. on 12th Nov.1956 after a five day flight from London. The accommodation was pretty good except when it rained - as it did early in our stay - then everything was thick mud. Also excellent was the food, with great variety as well as quantity: indeed if one tackled every meal one couldn't do any training. The Opening Ceremony on Nov. 22nd will always be remembered as the big moment of the Games. We were driven the 10 miles to the stadium in coaches and the streets were lined with cheering crowds. The actual march of ¼ mile into the stadium was used by the crowd for some good-humoured bantering such as:- "Where's the Ashes?" "What about Jim Laker" We managed, however, to hold our own. At last the Games were open and we were greeted with our first spell of warm weather - 84degrees. Soon the athletes were holding the attention of over 100,000 spectators every day and on the Friday the first finals were decided. You know the results by now so I will not dwell on the details, but certain things, however, stick in one's memory at every athletic meeting. First of all, the machine-like running of Kuts - 400m steady, 70 to 100m fast - "steady" being 68s. in the 10,000m and faster still in the 5,000! Then the ease with which Bob Morrow completed the first double sprint victory since Jesse Owens's in 1936. Greg Bell long-jumping 25ft odd with a damaged leg-muscle which finally "went" on his last jump and Derek Johnson so nearly beating Tom Courtney in the 800m. One of the highlights of the Games was the high-jump duel between Dumas of the U.S.A. and unknown Porter of Australia - Dumas who found it too much trouble to convert metres to feet and Porter who peered at the bar before jumping. Bob Richards needed three attempts to qualify in the pole vault and Oerter, who had not seen a discus a year ago, won the Gold Medal, while our own Mark Pharaoh missed third place by five inches. In the javelin, Danielsen never really got loosened up until his last throw when he threw it almost out of the arena to record over 280ft. We had our sad moments also, the last Saturday proving the worst day, with our comparative failure in the 1500m - I do not mean failure in the extreme sense of the word, as a 4m.2s. mile is no flop! At that time I was out on the marathon course and saw Ron Clark and Fred Norris run themselves to a standstill and finally retire, to leave Harry Hicks gamely battling on to the finish, although being attacked with cramp on the track. However, our three relay teams kept the flag flying. The girls track events were shared amongst the Australians with our girls making the 100 & 200 metres finals, while the field events were dominated by the Russians. Perhaps the greatest moment of the Games, for me, was to see two of our men leading an Olympic field - and one of them a Belgravian. I mean of course, the 20km. walk in which Stan Vickers put up such a remarkable performance in holding off the Russians for so long and then giving chase in faultless style. Indeed, by his style, Stan earned for himself the title of "The Walker". I must not overlook the fact that we won a Gold Medal - all praise to Chris Brasher -"the hack who finally became a Champion". So much has been said and written about this event that I do not intend to say anything except that the two steeple-chasers, Rozsnyoi and Larsen, were great sportsmen. The 50km. walk brought us a spot of bother when Don Thompson, who was in fifth position at the time, collapsed from the heat with only 3kms. to go. He was taken to hospital but fortunately made a very quick recovery and now shows no ill effects. The feeding arrangements for this race and for the Marathon were good as was the policing of the courses. The judging in the 20km. walk left much to be desired and Stan should have had at least a bronze medal. However, we should be thankful for the fact that there were no international incidents. Stan was selected for the British Empire versus U.S.A. meeting but owing to the chaos it is not certain where he finished. He apparently had a good time in Sydney and it should be noted that the aforementioned city is now back to normal! We flew home via the United States, so making a round-the-world tour of 27,000 miles, a month's holiday and an unforgetable experience. As Stan says, "roll on 1960". Eric Hall P.S. We would both like to thank all those Club members who gave us their best wishes before we left. We would add that even if we didn't win we at least took part and had a very good try. E.W.H.& S.F.V. items.s: COACHING The Coaching Hon. Secretary lists the club's coaches for the coming season and invites offers of help and attendance at coaching courses. COACHING Our coaches these days may not be numerous but we will do all we can to assist anyone who will take the trouble to seek our advice. Frank Simmons will as usual be looking after the sprinters and relay-teams and putting in a tremendous amount of hard work. Stan Davies, Charlie Smart, Arthur Penny and George Isaac can give you assistance in the middle and long distances. Micky Pyer will be continuing his good work with the boys and youths and all our younger members should get to know him. I, myself, can, I hope, help all budding Field Events men and will seek to improve the better performers. Having mentioned that our Coaches are none too numerous, I would welcome any offers of assistance from people who think they are past their best and would like to help the younger members. A number of Coaching Courses are run throughout the season which, if attended, will give anyone a good insight into modern methods of training and technique. Some of these courses are for active athletes too and will benefit anyone who attends and more particularly if he takes his coach along with him. I shall have details of these from time to time and will be only too glad to pass them on to those interested. T.C. Jones, Coaching Hon. items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP Field events notes by T.C. Jones urging members to train and enter championships, aiming to retain the Sward Trophy at Chiswick, and reviewing the club's throwers and jumpers. FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP The Field Events Notes in the last issue were, I'm afraid, rather scanty owing to pressure of space. The Summer Season is fast approaching and I hope all Seniors, Juniors and Youths will be getting down to training in earnest for the coming fixtures. Your Captain, Mal Ash, Vice Captain Dave Ansell and myself want your full support so that we can turn out strong teams. What we want to see more than anything else is the name of Belgrave well represented in County, District and A.A.A. Championships. You may not be good enough to win or get a place but there are standard certificates or medals to be won. The entries of our Youths and Juniors are particularly needed in these events. I will be able to supply all information as to dates and venues of these meetings in due course. Our main effort this Summer will be to retain the Sward Trophy which we won so handsomely last year. This meeting will take place at Chiswick on May 11th and there is no reason why we should not have a very strong team. I remember our first puny efforts in this competition some eight or ten years ago when we only gained half a point - how we gradually built up year by year culminating in success. Go to it lads and retain that Trophy. Just a "by the way" here - in the past our Cross-Country and road-relay teams have had great vocal support. There is no reason why such a meeting as "The Sward" cannot be just as interesting. Throwers and Jumpers will respond to encouragement by Club-Mates and Supporters in the same way as runners and walkers. They'd be glad to see and hear you at Chiswick. Thames Valley Harriers started last year a Winter Field Events Meeting and again this year put on a similar meeting. Roy Liggins, Ted Gaworski and Percy Porter competed. Percy was 2nd in the Hammer and Ted was in the first six in the Discus. We ourselves decided to promote a similar meeting on March 2nd at Battersea. Support from all Club members is essential and I have been promised entries from some of the top performers in the London area. Let's trust the weather will be kind and so help to make this a worthwhile effort. During the season we shall have the usual Club matches. We have received invitations to compete in most of the big trophy matches including the "Kinnaird" and "Brockman". Your efforts last year were all well rewarded and this year we should do even better. Mal Ash assures me he will be making his usual stupendous efforts again and we hope to see him pull off the A.A.A. Decathlon as well as successfully defending his Surrey and Southern titles. John Powell Jones and Dick Harris will, I hope, get nearer that 50 feet with the shot and Ted Gaworski be as consistent as ever with both shot and discus. Our Long-Jumpers are quite strong again with Percy Luxom, Dave Ansell, Charlie Jones, Adjei and Mal Ash all round about or over 22 feet. I hope to see Dave Ansell do 23 feet consistently. Luxom and Jones together with Norman Caves are out main Triple-Jumpers and should do well. Our Javelin men, Roy Liggins and George Edwards, should both improve and get nearer the 200 ft mark. We also have a number of promising Juniors including Reg Chamberlain who got 2nd place in the Surrey Long Jump last year and we hope to see more Youths competing along with Colin Clair and Malcom Draper. In addition to the Club matches we shall, as usual, hold some Handicaps and I would like to see these better supported than in the past. These events are ideal for some of you runners to try out a new event and who knows, some of you may show more potential here than in the distances you have been struggling over in the past. T.C. items.sum: Report of the club children's party, with thanks to the ladies who catered and the helpers who entertained.
items.s: THE CHILDREN'S PARTY 6th Jan. 1957 Report of the club children's party, with thanks to the ladies who catered and the helpers who entertained. THE CHILDREN'S PARTY 6th Jan. 1957 Like the dance the week before, this party went off very well, although it was quite noticeable that the adults outnumbered the children easily. The food and drinks were catered for by the ladies of the Club, Mesdames: Carter, Shepherd, Savage, Penny and Morrell, while their better halves thoroughly enjoyed themselves entertaining the "kids". Bob Taylor deserves special mention as he really worked hard keeping the older boys amused with balloon football - well done Bob! Father Christmas gave a very convincing performance and presented each child with a gift, I'm sure some of the grown-ups were jealous - I know I was. Musical songs and games were arranged by Auntie Brenda and Uncle Bill Lucas with Auntie Joan at the piano. On behalf of the children and lookers-on I would like to say - a big thank-you to all the helpers - we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. By the way, Mr. Harry Evans, the cake was delicious - thank you. P.S. I would like to ask the great Mr. Stanley Vickers to look after his hot-dogs in future - one was found on the kitchen floor, exactly a week and a day after it was cooked!!!? items.sum: Letter from Arthur Whitehead thanking those who marked cross-country courses during the winter and the members who supplied equipment.
items.s: Letter from Arthur Whitehead thanking those who marked cross-country courses during the winter and the members who supplied equipment. We are pleased to include the following letter from Arthur Whitehead, to whom the Club owes so much :- Dear Editors, Now that the Cross-country season has unfortunately ended, may I express, through you, my thanks to those who have assisted the Club by marking courses throughout the Winter. This is, whatever the unitiated may think, an extremely difficult and energetic task and our reward is in the knowledge that nobody (perhaps Dooley would prefer me to say no visitor) went off course. It is delightful to think that we have been able to assist such a variety of organisations as our County AAA, the Stock Exchange, the Breweries, Boy Scouts and Catholic Schools and all of these have expressed their deepest appreciation which I would wish to pass on to all concerned in full measure. We are entitled to assume also that the marking of Club Championship courses and inter-club matches is appreciated. Upon the "stores" side may I thank Arthur Penny for the poles which have so much improved and brightened our Finish, George Beecham for a further consignment of flag material, Gordon Biscoe for making the Finish remain upright and Mrs. Edgar for the colourful flags she so kindly made for the starting pens of the County Senior race. The other side? The incessant sabotage of our marks by small boys; false courses laid; flags destroyed and stolen; really frantic last second re-markings. Yes there always problems but don't let's dwell on them too much. Who knows, some of our members other than the odd dozen who have helped this year may next year come along too and we may at length even be able to persuade some of our older runners that it is not asking too much to expect them to take their very serious and important training run round the marks rather than in Richmond Park. But I doubt it. Yours etc. Arthur Whitehead. items.h: THREE NATIONAL TITLES IN ONE YEAR !
items.sum: Editorial celebrating the walkers winning all three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year and members' county championship successes on the track.
items.s: THREE NATIONAL TITLES IN ONE YEAR ! Editorial celebrating the walkers winning all three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year and members' county championship successes on the track. By the magnificent victory of our walkers in the R.W.A. 50 kilometres event at Preston we become the first club ever to have held the three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year - a brilliant achievement! This latest win was accomplished, be it noted, without the assistance of Eric Hall, who was forced to retire from the race owing to the extreme heat. We extend our sympathies to Eric, who, with more favourable weather conditions might easily have completed a superlative double, as he had already won the 20 mile title. Congratulations to those members who showed the Belgrave colours to such fine effect in gaining win and place medals in the track championships of FIVE counties, a remarkable feat! Most notable were the brilliant doubles of Brian Morris (Sussex 220 & 440 yds.), Ivan Mayers (Middlesex 100 & 220 yds.) and Clive Ryan (Surrey Junior 100 & 220 yds.). Another noteworthy performance was that of B. Morris and G. Leroy in finishing 1st and 2nd in the Kinnaird 440 yds. final, both inside 50 sec. Morris followed this up a week later when finishing a very close second in the Southern 440 with a time of 48.6 sec. In view of these splendid efforts our chances of annexing the forthcoming A.A.A. 4 x 440 yds. relay are very bright indeed. It now seems that we have first class performers in almost all the events in which a club of our standing participates, and the days when we lost matches due to our inability to put competitors in certain events are gone. A particular instance springs to mind here, when, a few years back we won almost every track event against L.A.C. and still lost the match. Thanks to Jack Chappell, Bill Merryman and Charlie Jones, the result of such a match now would be quite different. items.s: BELGRAVE 37th ANNUAL 7 MILES OPEN WALK 24th NOV.1956 Report and team results of Belgrave's 37th annual 7 miles open walk, won by Belgrave to regain the Berman Cup. We were again favoured with fine weather for this popular event, the rain keeping off until after the finish. Our grateful thanks are due to all officials and helpers, who, despite petrol rationing, ensured a well organised event. Once more the ladies did fine work selling programmes and Arthur Whitehead was host to a Belgrave Hall 'overflow'; we are indebted to them. Also to all those who generously supported the Prize Fund I say "THANKYOU". Without their help this event would not be staged. The largest entry of the season, 248, included 55 Bels, and we finished SIX teams! 176 walkers started. We were out to regain The Berman Cup, and right well we did, with 27pts. to Woodford's 34. The individual title went to Ken Matthews, Royal Sutton Coldfield, who won easily from George Meadows of Highgate and Williams of Ilford. Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th! Ray Middleton, on leave from the R.A.F. was 29th, a fine show; he was rewarded by winning the handicap. items.label: No. 131
items.sum: Report on the National Cross-Country Championships at Parliament Hill on 9 March, run in deep mud, with Jack Brown 11th and Belgrave 11th senior team and 30th junior team.
items.s: NATIONAL CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS Report on the National Cross-Country Championships at Parliament Hill on 9 March, run in deep mud, with Jack Brown 11th and Belgrave 11th senior team and 30th junior team. Parliament Hill March 9th. Any Northern or Midland competitors who expected civilised parkland conditions in the first 'National' to be staged in London for many years, were sadly disappointed, for a veritable sea of mud faced them from start to finish. A mild, cloudy afternoon, an enthusiastic, well controlled crowd of spectators and enormous fields; the value of a season's hard training was now to be put to the test by over 1500 runners. First to taste the conditions were the youths, and the usual hard fought, closely bunched race was well dealt with by the recorders; competitors pouring in at well over a hundred-a-minute. Under the conditions our lads performed well, and we were glad to see that Arthur Penny was able to get a good turn-out. In a very large field, A. Black, following his unfortunate mishap at Epsom, ran well to finish 66th with K. Miller, D. Taylor and J. Radford all finishing in the first half of the field and within 16 places. The senior race provided the largest field of the day, when 771 runners were soon swarming up the steep hill at the start. At first sight our chaps did not seem well placed and were well split up. Jack Brown was lying about 36th with Eric Gebbett leading the rest of the team in about 120th position. A course of this nature however, called for restraint in the early stages, when many spent too much energy endeavouring to move up before they had even allowed the field to settle down. There our men showed that at least they could hold on to their positions, and after 3 miles Jack had moved up to the twenties, Eric was running extremely well, just outside the hundred; Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Chas Walker and Len Bishop were our scoring team in that order. Chas seemed comfortable, but quite unable to move up and was soon to be in danger of being caught by Len. Jack's progress was a treat to watch, for from 6 miles he slowly went through to pass Keily, Hicks, Heywood, our second claim member Bill Bird, running a 'blinder', and was soon lying about 15th. This was cross-country running of a type we had not seen from him before, for none would call him a mudlark and never before had he showed such cool tactics. The finish saw Jack in 11th place, with Gebbett our next man home 114th, Dave Baulch 141st, Ray Tooby, who had manfully stood up to a course for which he was not physically suited 147th, whilst Chas Walker held on to finish 173rd from Len Bishop 181st. It was clear from the team result, in which we finished 11th, that with P. Bagnall, P. Newell, and with Chas occupying a position more worthy of his undoubted ability, we could have finished in the first six. However, 11th was a creditable performance out of 69 teams to finish. Others to finish were, C. Shippen 205th, J. Heathfield 340th and D. Hooper 362nd. In the junior race we saw a new Pirie, for the manner in which North slammed the field in such conditions, was a revelation. It seems almost a travesty of justice that he was not awarded his international vest. None of our lads looked very happy in the mud, and considering that 1200 runners had already torn the course up, who could blame them! However, Flanagan ran extremely well to gain 40th place, but one wonders how much better he would perform with a less loping action; his style was definately unsuited to the going. Stevens ran a very steady race, and hung on grimly in the closing stages, when obviously very tired, to be our second man home, 143rd, a fine performance in a big field. Tupper and Couzens completed our team, scoring 204 and 254. As a team we finished 30th out of 58. However, the great thing was that we had a full team, and we feel sure next year will be a different story when a little more welding has been done. items.sum: Report by J. Goswell on the National 10 mile walking championship at Coventry on 9 March, won by Stan Vickers from Eric Hall with Belgrave regaining the team title; team result printed as 37 pts though the scoring four placed 1, 2, 17 and 20.
items.s: NATIONAL 10 MILE WALKING CHAMPIONSHIP. Report by J. Goswell on the National 10 mile walking championship at Coventry on 9 March, won by Stan Vickers from Eric Hall with Belgrave regaining the team title; team result printed as 37 pts though the scoring four placed 1, 2, 17 and 20. Coventry March 9th. A high-spirited party of eighteen travelled up by train for this event. In view of our good form throughout this season, we were confident of regaining the team title, held for the past eight years by Sheffield U.H. We were without Syd James, and Dave McMullen was not at his best, owing to an attack of flu. First-class dressing accommodation was provided at a boy's school on the outskirts of Coventry. The only fly in the ointment was the weather; it rained incessantly for the whole afternoon, making conditions very unpleasant. One hundred and fifty walkers started at 2-20 p.m. and Stan Vickers went straight into the lead, closely followed by Matthews of Sutton Coldfield. Eric Hall was in the first ten, while the rest of our lads were in the middle of the field. One man (not a 'Bel') was actually disqualified in the first fifty yards! Passing the mile in 7m.12s., the two leaders were still together, but at three miles Stan had opened up a gap of twenty yards. Shortly afterwards Matthews was disqualified and thereafter Stan was not headed. Eric Hall was now fourth and when the third man was ruled out he quickly moved up to second place, about 200yds. behind Stan. A quick check at 4¾ miles proved that we were already on top, with 36pts. to Met.W.C's 50 and Sheffield well back. Our scorers at this point being :- 1, S.Vickers; 2, E.Hall; 16, Ted Smith; 17, George Checkley. Bob Newson and Dave McMullen were close behind, followed by G.Beecham, H.McGreechan and J.Coleman. At a further check three miles later, the team position was almost the same, with Belgrave 39pts to Met.W.C's 55 and Sheffield still a long way behind. Stan was now moving perfectly although Eric had gained slightly on him. At this stage Eric's second place was being threatened by Chaplin of Coventry and Allen of Sheffield, three times winner of this event, who was moving rapidly through the field. Fortunately for Eric this threat didn't materialise, as he was able to hold off Chaplin, while Allen faded and fell back to fifth place. Still moving effortlessly Stan went on to win by 16sec. from Eric with Chaplin 42sec. further back. Ted Smith was an untroubled 17th and George Checkley 20th, to complete our scoring four. We actually finished 7 in 29 - a great performance and a splendid example of Belgrave team spirit. How jubilant we all were when the team result was announced! At the presentation, by the deputy Mayor of Coventry, Stan received the plaque awarded to him by the R.W.A. for exceeding eight miles in the hour at Parliament Hill last September. We made a very hurried journey to the station to catch the 6-17, somewhat handicapped by having to carry a very large cup and a shield. There was even greater evidence of high spirits on the way home, and justifiably so, after such a resounding victory. Don Brown, Alf Harley and Harry Evans who travelled with us must have felt well satisfied with the result, and Alf reminded me of his words of four years ago, when he said "keep at it, and you will have a champion or champions come along". How right he was, for here we were with 1st and 2nd individuals and a winning National team. Our training and team spirit have certainly paid handsome dividends and to every member of our team I say "Well done, as fine a victory as any in the long history of the Club". J. Goswell. items.s: ILFORD ROAD RELAY - MARCH 16th Report on the Ilford Road Relay of 16 March, where Jack Brown broke the lap record and Belgrave finished 2nd to Thames Valley, with stage times. In a large field we were off to a good start, when Eric Gebbett ran in 7th on the first stage, 30 seconds behind the leaders, Blackheath. Eric handed over to Ray Tooby, who moved up well to place us 3rd, despite clashing with Redrup of Wycombe Phoenix who broke the lap record. Our next man, however, Jack Brown, was to have none of this, and proceeded to smash Redrup's record and put us in the lead with a scintillating run. Dave Baulch ran well to hold our lead but on the next stage, Len Bishop had to give best to Ellis of T.V.H., and we were now second. A rather unhappy looking 'Jumbo' Masters, whom we welcomed back after a long absence, hung on to our position but we had slipped back on times. However, Colin Collis, running at a distance well below his usual, and George Flanagan consolidated our position with well judged running. On the 9th stage, Dave Maclean found this flat course well to his liking and produced a fast time, though without altering our position. With Norris on the last stage for T.V.H. items.s: CAMBRIDGE ROAD RELAY - MARCH 23rd Report on the Cambridge Road Relay of 23 March, where Belgrave's A team was 3rd and B team 23rd, with stage times. On an almost spring-like day, about thirty teams competed in this popular event. We fielded two teams, and our first stage runners were Len Bishop 'A' team, and G. Stevens 'B' Team, who both ran well, on a stage when positions are rather close, finishing 6th and 18th respectively. Ray Tooby moved up to 4th place on the next stage, and Chas Walker, with an almost identical time, ensured that our next man, Jack Brown, was within striking distance of the leaders. Once again Jack established a new lap record, but failed to catch Heywood of H.H.H. who also put up a very fast time. The 5th stage run by Jumbo Masters, saw us drop to 3rd place behind T.V.H. and H.H.H. and our last man, Eric Gebbett, although running well was unable to improve on this. Our 'B' team were unfortunate in that McLean had a very bad cold and lost 13 places and 5 minutes on the second stage. items.label: No. 131
items.sum: Feature arguing that quantity of training lets ordinary athletes become good ones, citing Eric Hall, Eric Gebbett and Colin Collis.
items.s: SILK PURSES AND SOWS' EARS Feature arguing that quantity of training lets ordinary athletes become good ones, citing Eric Hall, Eric Gebbett and Colin Collis. Which are you? They say you cannot make one from the other, but if the first represents the international class athlete and the second the "scrubber", the impossible can be achieved. Who would have thought when Eric Hall was finishing in the middle of Junior 1-mile walk fields that here was a budding Olympic walker? There are others who, if they have not reached the "silk purse" grade have produced an article of high quality rayon. One is Eric Gebbett, who finished 8th in our youths cross-country championship in 1950 ( 13th and last was the now well known R. Darchambaud) and has achieved 2h.33m.17s. for the marathon and holds the club record for stage 5 of the Brighton relay. Another is Colin Collis, who, although finishing 135th out of 140 in the 1946 National Youths cross-country and has yet to beat 4m.50s. for a mile, has "produced" a 1h.51m.58s. "20" and a 2h.56m.35s. "30" . How is it done? Methods of training vary but one thing is common to all those not endowed with natural ability who have made good and that is QUANTITY of training. One must be prepared to give anything from 1 to 3 hours, 6 or 7 times a week, for month after month. Bad weather, sore feet, social inconvenience and a hundred other difficulties must be overcome. Not everyone is prepared to make these sacrifices, but perhaps more would if they felt sure the results could be achieved. They can. We have temporarily lost the services of Jack Brown. We must make some more silk purses if we are to maintain our high standard of performance in middle distance running. We have plenty of sows' ears and plenty of material that would need less drastic adaptation. In Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Pat Newell and Brian Hallowell, to name but a few, we have runners of the class of which champions are made. All that is needed is for them to set their sights higher in terms of mileage and standard of performance. Let everyone take as his motto "It can be done"- and it will. Percy Verence. items.label: No. 131
items.h: Is Belgrave Hall taken for granted ?
items.sum: Letter from Len Marchant, who has moved to Essex, comparing the South East Essex cross-country league's facilities with the comforts of Belgrave Hall.
items.s: Is Belgrave Hall taken for granted ? Letter from Len Marchant, who has moved to Essex, comparing the South East Essex cross-country league's facilities with the comforts of Belgrave Hall. My contribution takes the form of an appreciation of the luxury of Belgrave Hall, and the great variety of country on it's doorstep. For twenty years I, together with many others I'm afraid, took all this for granted. It was not until I moved right away from the vicinity of Wimbledon that it was brought home to me, in no uncertain manner how very fortunate are the active members of the Club. As you may know, there is in existence a South East Essex cross-country league, formed by five clubs, Brentwood A.C., Hadleigh Olympiads, Chelmsford A.C., Hornchurch A.C. and Southend A.C. I have just completed my first winter season over here, competing in four of the five league matches, and I couldn't help making comparisons, as surely Darchambaud of S.L.H., and George Knight of Essex Beagles must have done; they turned out for Chelmsford and Brentwood respectively while I ran for Southend. I am sure the clubs concerned would not object if I say that compared with Belgrave Hall things are pretty grim! Brentwood and Hornchurch use children's schools, though I must admit that hot water is on tap at Hornchurch. Chelmsford have a fair-sized hut with a small plunge-bath. I was one of the lucky people back early - I wouldn't like to say what it was like for the tail-enders! Unfortunately I missed the Hadleigh match, but I'm told they also use a hut. For the league match, Southend have probably the best accommodation - the modern Belfairs School - and although the showers are only chest-high to adults, the water is hot. The school canteen is also available. The only fly in the ointment is the fact that the start is half-a-mile away. With regard to the courses, there is even less comparison. Of necessity, they are unimaginative, being hemmed in by building developements - no Wimbledon Common or Richmond Park here! In my opinion Chelmsford have the best course, with varied country, 2-300 yds. of plough on each lap and the usual brand of Essex mud, but never really out of sight of buildings. For training and club championships Southend use a small hut, (about the size of the Belgrave Hall committee room) on the golf course at Belfairs. Water is heated over a primus stove and we wash one leg at a time! The ceiling is so low that on more than one occasion I have knocked it while taking off my shirt and put the lights out! Every time I go there I am reminded of the days at the "Rising Sun", not only by the rather primitive conditions but by the same feeling of comradeship and club spirit that used to hit you as you entered the back room of that pub in Pimlico. I only hope we can build that same spirit at Basildon, but I feel we won't until the cross-country section gets going, which can't be too soon for me. This may sound like so much sob stuff to some people but the atmosphere I've been talking about was there at Belfairs on 23rd Feb., when we had finished the club 10 miles championship in the worst weather of the season. After five laps of continuous ankle-deep (and sometimes knee-deep) mud, back to a small drum of hot water. I was second to Roy McCalla, so once again was lucky enough to get washed while the water was still reasonably clean. So can you wonder why I make comparisons. After having enjoyed the finest winter accommodation and some of the best country that any club in the land can offer, if I ever hear anyone bemoaning their lot at Belgrave Hall again I'll recommend them to a couple of helpimgs of the South East Essex League, and all that it implies. I'm sure Ken Cuff will back me up. Len Marchant. items.sum: Announcement of the Belgrave annual dinner on 16 November 1957 at the Mecca Restaurant, Barrington House, Gresham Street, with tickets at 19/6d. in the club's 70th anniversary year.
items.s: BELGRAVE DINNER Announcement of the Belgrave annual dinner on 16 November 1957 at the Mecca Restaurant, Barrington House, Gresham Street, with tickets at 19/6d. in the club's 70th anniversary year. Saturday November 16th 1957 We are breaking new ground this year and have booked the Mecca Restaurant in Barrington House, Gresham Street, London E.C.2 for our annual function. This is a very smart and capacious restaurant in a newly erected block of office property in the City of London, and to those of you who work in that area it may already be well known as a resort for morning coffee or for lunches with prices ranging from those paid by the proletariat to those within the expense accounts of City Directors.The décor is excellent and the facilities for dinner-dances first class, with adequate bar space providing drinks at nominal prices. The situation is within easy walking distance of Bank (Northern & Central lines) and St.Pauls (Central line) stations and extensive car-parking facilities are available. We are forced to increase the price beyond that of previous functions owing to the trend of rising prices throughout the catering trade, but we are confident that the extra shilling or two will not be missed by members and it will be well worth the much improved food and the ideal setting. Tickets are now available at 19/6d. per head and we hope that everyone will apply as soon as possible and support your Social Committee in the endeavours they are making on your behalf. Remember that this year is our 70th anniversary and we would like to make the occasion a worthy one for a Club with such a long life as ours. Belgrave Dinner Mecca Restaurant Barrington House Gresham Street City of London Bank St.Pauls

items.s: LONDON SHIPPING 10 MILES ROAD RACE Report on the London Shipping 10 miles road race at Hayes on 20 April, won by Jack Brown in a course record with Belgrave taking the team award. Hayes, 20th April On what was more like a June day, with temperatures in the 60's our team crushed what little resistance was offered, to win both individual and team awards. At 5 miles Jack Brown had "lost" the field and looked set for another easy win, Colin Collis followed in 5th position from Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop. Our first 6 men at this stage were within the first twelve positions. The effects of his early effort slowed Jack down on the second lap, but he still ran out a clear winner from Haslam of T.V.H. in a new course record. Collis was 5th and Len Bishop who had moved up six places, finished 6th. A tired Walker was our last scoring man, while Eric Gebbett demonstrated his dislike of warm weather by falling back over the last few miles to finish 9th. items.sum: Stage-by-stage report by 'Olympian' on the National London to Brighton Relay of 13 April 1957, in which Belgrave finished third behind South London Harriers and Thames Valley Harriers and Jack Brown set a stage record, with individual times.
items.s: NATIONAL LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY Stage-by-stage report by 'Olympian' on the National London to Brighton Relay of 13 April 1957, in which Belgrave finished third behind South London Harriers and Thames Valley Harriers and Jack Brown set a stage record, with individual times. April 13th 1957 We more than excelled our expectations by taking third place behind South London Harriers and Thames Valley. It had been generally expected that Sheffield United with their all-round strength and a sprinkling of "stars" would also finish in front, and that the best we could hope for was a fourth position. The boys however, ran like heroes especially in the latter part of the race and more than compensated for an off-day by Pete Bagnall on the first leg. Pride of place goes to Jack Brown for his excellent run on the seventh leg which gave him a stage record. This was made with no help whatsoever as the team in front were well out of sight for most of the leg and those behind were never with Jack. It should also be recorded that other notabilities on this stage were Sando, Driver, Heatley, O'Gorman, Keily and Ingles, all of whom beat the previous record and all of whom gained assistance in battling with the opposition. It is sad to relate that this will almost certainly be Jack's last run on the Brighton road for at least three years as he has now moved to Cyprus with the Civil Service. Now to the story of the race, taken individually stage by stage. 1st Pete Bagnall A very fast start from Old Palace Yard along the Embankment with most of the twenty runners bunched together and Pete nicely placed. At Chelsea Bridge the leaders made a break and Wood(Sheffield), Mayatt(Aylesford), Gilligan(Pembroke) and Eales(Tipton) opened up a thirty yards lead from seven others (including Pete) by Queens Road Circus. Before Cedars Road Wood and Gilligan had gone ahead and at this point Bagnall was having a bad time back in 14th position. However, a desperate effort over the half mile brought us up to 13th, almost one minute behind Pembroke for whom Gilligan had taken an 8 seconds lead over Ken Wood. Ahead of us were such dangerous teams as Sheffield, Poly, Woodford Green and Victoria Park(Scotland). Fortunately S.L.H. and T.V.H. were also in the dumps. 2nd Charlie Walker Conditions perfect for a fast run with twelve teams ahead strung out at regular intervals. Just right for Charlie who likes opposition such as this and he really rose to the occasion, and despite an early set-back when Cameron(T.V.H.), running very strongly, passed and went away, he made progress to such an extent as to take us up to 7th and at the same time produced a Belgrave best for the stage. Poly, with a first-class run by D.J.P. Richards, were in the lead with T.V.H. second, Cameron having made up twelve places, and Sheffield 3rd. We were then 52 seconds in arrears. 3rd Len Bishop With all due respects to Len this was not his sort of stage, but it is easy to be wise after the event. He battled to the end but had to give way to five teams, amongst whom was S.L.H. represented by Ibbotson who did the fastest time of the day and moved up from 10th to 4th. At Purley we were 2 min. 10 sec. behind Sheffield who had again taken the lead, with T.V.H. still second, 13 sec. back, and Poly third. 4th Pete Newell A new complexion, as far as we were concerned, came over the race from the moment Pete took his baton. He set about the opposition as if his life depended upon it, and took us through to fifth, only 1 min. 29 sec. in arrears. This earned him the second fastest time of the day, surpassed only by Darchambaud who was 3 sec. faster. It was however, a Belgrave best and was only 12 sec. outside the stage record held by none other than Ken Norris. 5th Eric Gebbett Eric continued the good work through Redhill and quickly passed Poly to take us into fourth place. Unfortunately the three leaders were running close together, over three hundred yards ahead, and Eric had no opportunity of getting to grips with them. His time of 22 m. 8 s. was the second fastest of the day, only one second slower than Barden of Sheffield, and was also a Belgrave record. Sheffield were again in the lead with T.V.H. second and S.L.H. third. 6th Ray Tooby Ray took over 86 sec. behind the leaders and ran steadily throughout. The three teams in front were however battling together and naturally made progress as a result. Ray was therefore forced to give ground, although retaining his fourth place, and at Lowfield Heath we were 2 min.12 sec. behind S.L.H., who had gone into the lead through a good run by Laurie Reed, 2 min.6 sec. behind Sheffield and 2 min.1 sec. down on T.V.H. Nevertheless, Tooby can be said to have performed well and it is good to see him back to something like his old form. 7th Jack Brown Ahead of Jack were Ingles of T.V.H., Driver of S.L.H. and Walker of Sheffield, all battling together. Ingles and Driver soon dropped Walker but Jack was making headway on all these runners and at the end of the stage was again within 2 min. of the leaders and only 27 sec. behind Sheffield, who had dropped to third. As previously mentioned Jack made a stage record by knocking 32 sec. off the former time - a magnificent effort. 8th Colin Collis Good running in fifteen and twenty mile races is not the qualification for taking the second longest leg of this event against opposition such as Ken Norris, Mick Firth and Johnny Nichols, all of whom are seasoned international performers. It is essential that this stage should be given to a "faster" man, to combat the star performers from other clubs. Colin unfortunately was not at his physical best, but drove himself to the last ounce to hold his position, which he did successfully, although losing much ground on the leaders. At the end of the stage we were 4 min. down on T.V.H. who had taken a 35 sec. lead over S.L.H. Sheffield were exactly 2 min. ahead of us. 9th George Flanagan Not deterred by the big gap ahead with no-one in sight, George set about his task in workmanlike manner and by steady running closed the two-minute gap with Sheffield by no less than 60 sec. and pulled back fifteen seconds on T.V.H. the leaders. S.L.H. however, through Scovell, moved further away by another 20 sec. At this point there was little doubt that the winners were to be either S.L.H. or T.V.H., but Belgrave still stood a chance of taking third, as Sheffield appeared to have put their faith in running all their best men on earlier stages and were definately flagging. George's time was the second fastest on the stage. 10th Dave Baulch A spirited performance by Dave brought third place well within our grasp and gave him the fastest time of the day on this stage. Our supporters gave the runner no peace - he was goaded, cajolled, egged on and shouted at for practically every inch of the 4¼ miles and rose to the occasion in great style. This was one of Dave's best runs for the Club. 11th Brian Hallowell We have always made a point of allocating the last stage to one of our faster track men and on a number of occasions it has paid dividends. This was no exception, for Brian soon ate up the 25 sec. gap between himself and the Sheffield runner, and across Preston Park took over third place and went on in fine form to consolidate this position. This was Brian's first attempt on the Brighton road, and if this is a pattern for the future we can expect great performances. His time of 17.19 was first class, surpassed by very few other runners, and was accomplished with the ease of the natural athlete. Result :- 1st South London Harriers 4 hrs. 25 min. 52 sec. 2nd Thames Valley Harriers 4 hrs. 27 min. 3rd Belgrave Harriers 4 hrs. 28 min. 59 sec. The winning time was a new course record, while T.V.H. and ourselves were within the former record. items.s: SURREY COUNTY 20 MILE ROAD RACE Report of the Surrey County 20 mile road race of 4 May, won by Eric Gebbett, with Belgrave second to Walton A.C. in the team result. This event was held on the 4th May. Our hopes of retaining the team title received a setback when Colin Collis arrived and announced that he would not be able to run owing to a leg injury. We were also without the services of Geoff Pearson. However, with the minimum of three runners we did as well as could be expected, although Walton's margin over us was greater than the result would suggest, owing to the questionable practice of deleting individual positions when arriving at the team result. Eric Gebbett ran far above his usual form to win in the very fast time of 1 hr. 48 min. 49 sec. and was in fact the first Club member to win this race since 1939. Len Bishop, in his first race over this distance also performed very well. Result :- 1st E. Gebbett 1.48.49; 4th L.C. Bishop 1.52.37; 9th H.A. Bishop 2.00.10. WALTON A.C. 10 pts. BELGRAVE H. 11 pts. items.s: FIRST TRACK MEETING Report and results of the Captain's versus Vice-Captain's training match that opened the track season at Battersea Park on 27 April. The track season opened at Battersea Park on Sat. 27th April with a Captain's versus Vice-Captain's training match, which was held in conjunction with a Ladies' Meeting. A goodly number of members and supporters turned up, and some very interesting racing ensued. The Field Events Section however, were conspicuous by their absence, as will be seen by the fact that Ivan Mayers won the Shot Put in addition to completing the double in the sprints. Other notable performances were put up by D. Carter, who was runner up in both sprints, and Clive Ryan, who won both the Junior 100 and 440 yds. Whilst there was no actual scoring, it would seem that the honours were fairly evenly shared by the two teams.
